# AUDIO

**No music of any kind, at any volume** — no drone, no swell, no riser, no sting, no bass hit, no synth, no strings, no instruments, no score. **Every sound is something in the room actually making it.**

**Close and tactile.** The **impacts on the run are distinct and separate**, each with a small space around it — **never mush, never a continuous roar.** Around them, the wreckage is messy and continuous: books slapping down, pages fluttering, splinters skittering, wood groaning. A stone hall full of paper: dry flat slap-back, low dead air.

**The vocabulary:** one sharp dry **crack** of hundreds of seals breaking at the unlock; a **dense fast cascade of tiny mechanical sounds** through the fold; the lock a **running wave of hard clicks**; the **low heavy rumble** of the roll, boards resonating under the weight; the **dull knock** of each paddle landing **with a wood crack inside it**; the **soft slap** of books going over and landing flat; the **hush** of running on covers; the **hard bright ring** of the bracket; the **hollow boxed tone** in the brass pipe; the **fast even run of bright rings** along the rod comb; the **dry rattle** of the drawer; the **three sharp cracks** of the laths; the **groan** of the sagging shelf dropping; the **half-second of silence** in the fall; the **enormous flat thud** on the floor; the **gritty roll**; the **soft tap** at the boot; then **three small dry ticks** as the timer counts.

**The rhythm emerges from the impacts themselves** — never created by music, an instrument, pitching or tuning the sounds, or a beat underneath. **If an instrument or a score is audible, the piece is wrong.**

---

# AVOID

**No cuts anywhere.** No hidden cuts, no match cuts, no jump cuts, no whip-pans, no dissolves, no fades, no black frames, no cutaways, no second camera, no viewpoint the camera has not travelled to. **The headings are moments in one take.** **The sphere is in frame in every frame** — if the picture ever shows something without it, that is a cut and the shot is wrong.

**The camera never pulls back off the sphere** — never a wide, never an establishing view, never a survey of the room, never the whole bookcase in frame, never the object small in the picture. **It stays close enough that the sphere fills a third to a half of the frame throughout, and at the end it only ever gets closer.**

**THE ENDING IS AN EXTREME MACRO OF A RUNNING TIMER.** The readout fills the frame with nothing else in shot, and **the digits change three times — `9`, `8`, `7` — so the countdown is plainly working.** If the timer sits on a single number, never changes, is unreadable, is out of focus, is small in the frame, or if the last frames are a wide, a medium, the whole sphere, the boots or the room, **the ending is wrong.** The camera never pulls back off the panel once it is there.

**The first frame matches <<<image_2>>> but is never held** — no static opening, no waiting, no pause; the machine has begun by 0.3s.

**The camera orbits the machine through the whole fold** — real travel around the object, not a pan, not a tilt, not a turntable and not the object rotating while the camera holds. **We never go inside the machine** — no interior, no circuitry, no travelling through the eye.

**The transformation never morphs** — no melting, liquid metal, dissolving, particles, nanites, voxels, glitching, parts appearing from nowhere or vanishing. No CGI-slick, glossy, weightless look, no whooshing, no motion trails, no speed lines. No flourish, no pose, no reveal, no head-turn to camera. **The finished sphere has no legs, no spikes, no feet and no face.**

**The impacts stay distinct** — however messy the destruction gets, the contacts themselves never blur into a continuous clatter, never overlap into mush, and the beat is always countable.

**It never rises.** No rebound, no hop, no skip, no arc, no bouncing down the shelves, no floating, hanging or sailing. It never rolls uphill, never changes direction without something changing it, never flies, hovers or steers. **One free fall only — the last one.** **Everything it dislodges falls downward** — no debris flying outward, no explosive scatter, no shockwave, no slow-motion wreckage.

**The whole bookcase never collapses.** Boards crack, lips break, laths snap, books fall — but the structure stands, nothing shatters into fragments, and there is no demolition.

**The size never changes** — always about 15 centimetres, always smaller than the book spines, small against the boot.

**One lens** — 85mm, no zoom, no focal-length change. **No fisheye, no barrel distortion, no wide-angle character**, including at floor level. Never stabilised, gimbal, Steadicam, dolly, crane, drone or locked off — hard handheld in every frame.

**The books are never black, never uniform, never monochrome** — coloured, labelled, dusty and various. The grade stays cold, blue-grey, underexposed and desaturated — **no warm or golden wash, no amber, no firelight, no embers, no glow, no bloom, no flares, no visible practical lamp.**

**Nothing lights up** on the sphere except the readout at the end. **It counts `9`, `8`, `7` and nothing else** — instantaneous changes, plain red digits; never flashing, blinking, pulsing, beeping, glowing, lighting the boot or the floor, and never a timecode, milliseconds, a progress bar or a scrambling number.

**It stops in front of him, not beside him** — square on, centred between both boots, readout facing him. Never rolls past, never stops to one side, never hits hard.

**Charlie is never seen above the boots** — no face, no body, no legs above the ankle, no hands, no creature, no reaction. **Only the two boots.**

**No explosion, no blast, no flash, no smoke, no fire.** No other person, no machine, no bird after the fold, no text and no interface graphics beyond the readout. The air is never clear — haze and dust throughout. No digital or clean modern look, no crisp digital sharpness, no artificial grain overlay — 35mm film, coarse, underexposed, muddy. No speed ramp, no slow motion, no strobing. No fade or cut to black.

## HOW IT MOVES

**Everything is snap, not glide.** Every change happens **in one frame**: elements appear whole, jump to a new position, and vanish. **No easing, no fades, no dissolves, no motion blur, no smooth tweens, no drifting animation, no bouncing, no elastic settle.** If something moves, it was somewhere else the frame before.

**Speed is the point.** At full flight there are **ten to twenty discrete changes per second** across the frame — far more than can be read. The eye should catch pattern and rhythm, never detail. **It is machine-time, not human-time.**

**Everything is aligned.** All motion is horizontal or vertical, snapped to an invisible grid. **No diagonal drift, no rotation, no scaling, no perspective, no 3D.**

**What moves, constantly:**

**the dot field** — dots flicker in and out across the whole frame every frame, thousands of small events, the density breathing; clusters gather and dissolve;
**the hairline skeleton** in the central rectangle rebuilds itself several times a second, nodes jumping, connecting lines re-drawing to different points, never settling on one solution;
**the central tracking rectangle** re-snaps: it jumps position, resizes taller or narrower, and its corner brackets detach and re-seat;
**sub-boxes** multiply and vanish — two, then nine, then thirty small hollow squares latching onto points in the field, then wiping down to one;
**the tick scales** along the top and bottom rules step and sweep, ticks lengthening and shortening in travelling waves;
**the three filled data blocks** roll numerals at high speed, digits cycling too fast to read, occasionally freezing on a value for a beat;
**the timecode** at the lower right runs, its milliseconds a blur;
**the bar graph** at the lower left jumps to new values every few frames;
**the code string** at the upper left flickers, characters replacing themselves;
**the YGGD mark** stays fixed and never animates — the one stable object in the frame.

**Frame-wide events, used sparingly — five or six times in the fifteen seconds:**

a **horizontal scan bar** sweeps top to bottom in three or four frames, everything it crosses flashing to solid for one frame;
a **one-frame inversion** — the entire frame goes solid red with black elements, then back;
a **full clear** — every graphic wipes off in one frame, leaving pure black for two or three frames before everything snaps back;
a **tear** — the frame splits horizontally and the two halves offset sideways for two frames;
a **density burst** — the dot field jumps to hundreds of points at once, then collapses to almost none.

## THE FIFTEEN SECONDS

**0.0–2.5s — idle.** Sparse and slow. The border, the brackets, the YGGD mark, the code string, the timecode running. A thin dot field, dim, a few dozen points flickering lazily. The central rectangle sits empty. **Two or three events per second, no more.** It is watching nothing.

# AUDIO — THE RUN IS THE SCORE

**No music of any kind, at any volume** — no drone, no swell, no riser, no sting, no bass hit, no synth, no strings, no instruments, no score. **Every sound is something in the room actually making it.**

**Close and tactile — ASMR-close.** Each contact is **distinct, separate and clean**, with a small silence around it. **Never a continuous roar, never mush, never two events at once.** A stone hall full of paper: dry flat slap-back, low dead air, quiet enough that the small sounds carry.

**The vocabulary, one per event:** at the unlock, **one sharp dry crack** of hundreds of seals breaking; through the fold, a **dense fast cascade of tiny dry mechanical sounds** — servos, plates on rails, hinges, detents — all small-object sounds; the lock a **running wave of hard clicks** ending on one seating clack; then the **low heavy rumble** of the roll on old wood, the board resonating under the weight; the **dull knock** of each paddle landing; the **soft hush** of running on book covers; the **hard bright ring** of the iron bracket; the **hollow boxed tone** inside the brass pipe; the **fast even run of small bright rings** along the rod comb; the **dry rattle** of the drawer; the **three sharp dry cracks** of the laths; the **half-second of silence** in the fall; the **enormous flat thud** on the floor; the **low gritty roll**; the **soft tap** at the boot; then **two small dry ticks**, a second apart.

**The rhythm emerges from the impacts themselves** — never created by music, an instrument, pitching or tuning the sounds, or a beat underneath. **If an instrument or a score is audible, the piece is wrong.**

# AVOID

**The camera orbits the machine through the whole fold** — real travel around the object, not a pan, not a tilt, not a turntable and not the object rotating while the camera holds; the background must swing and the angle must change every frame. **It stays tight and never pulls back to a wide.** **We never go inside the machine** — no interior, no circuitry, no travelling through the eye.

**The transformation never morphs** — no melting, liquid metal, dissolving, particles, nanites, voxels, glitching, parts appearing from nowhere or vanishing; every piece of the sphere is a piece of the bird we watched move there. No CGI-slick, glossy, weightless look, no whooshing, no motion trails, no speed lines. No flourish, no pose, no reveal, no head-turn to camera, no cute movement; never charming, characterful or animal. **The finished sphere has no legs, no spikes, no feet and no face.**

**Not chaotic.** No scrambling, no tumbling, no ricocheting, no clattering, no overlapping impacts, no continuous rolling roar, no avalanche of books, no collapsing shelving, no clouds of debris. **One clean event at a time, with air around it.** Small pale splinters from the three snapped laths are the only debris.

**The camera is never chaotic** — never whipping, never searching, never wrong-footed, never violently shaken, never losing the sphere, never arriving late in a panic. Calm, close, continuous, in control. But never stabilised, gimbal, Steadicam, dolly, crane, drone or locked off — a faint handheld life in every frame.

**It never rises.** No rebound, no hop, no skip, no arc, no bouncing down the shelves, no floating, hanging or sailing. It never rolls uphill, never changes direction without something changing it, never flies, hovers or steers. **One free fall only — the last one.**

**The size never changes** — always about 15 centimetres, always smaller than the book spines, small against the boot.

**One lens** — 85mm, no zoom, no focal-length change. **No fisheye, no barrel distortion, no wide-angle character**, including at floor level.

**The books are never black, never uniform, never monochrome** — coloured, labelled, dusty and various, as described. The grade stays cold, blue-grey, underexposed and desaturated — **no warm or golden wash, no amber, no firelight, no embers, no glow, no bloom, no flares and no visible practical lamp.**

**Nothing lights up** on the sphere except the readout from 15.6s. **The readout shows `10` then `9` and nothing else** — one second apart, instantaneous changes, small plain red digits; never flashing, blinking, pulsing, beeping, accelerating, glowing, lighting the boot or the floor, and never a timecode, milliseconds, a progress bar or a large number filling frame.

**It stops in front of him, not beside him** — square on, centred between both boots, readout facing him. Never rolls past, never stops to one side, never hits hard.

**Charlie is never seen above the boots** — no face, no body, no legs above the ankle, no hands, no creature, no reaction. **Only the two boots.** The camera never leaves the sphere.

**No explosion, no blast, no flash, no smoke, no fire.** No other person, no machine, no bird after the fold, no text and no interface graphics beyond the readout. The air is never clear — haze and dust throughout. No digital or clean modern look, no crisp digital sharpness, no artificial grain overlay — 35mm film, coarse, underexposed, muddy. No speed ramp, no slow motion, no strobing. No fade or cut to black.

**This is the most important thing after the no-cut rule.**

the **horizon rolling five to fifteen degrees** off level and being wrenched back, again and again;

# THE NINE SECONDS

# **THE CAMERA — WELDED TO THE BOMB**

**This is the most important thing after the no-cut rule.**

**The camera is right on top of the sphere and stays there for seventeen seconds.** Very close — **the sphere fills a third to a half of the frame at all times**, near-macro on it, close enough to read the panel lines, the chipped paint, the dust in its seams and the grain of the wood it is running on. **It never pulls back, never widens, never lets it get small, never surveys the room and never looks at anything else.**

**It moves with the object as if fixed to it.** Where the sphere goes, the frame goes — down a diagonal, along a flat run, through the slot, off the edge, into the fall. **The sphere stays roughly in the same part of the picture the whole way down while the entire world tears past behind it, streaked and destroyed into motion.** That contrast — small object locked and sharp, everything else ripping past — is the shot.

**And it is violently handheld.** Not smooth, not stabilised, not elegant:

a **constant hard tremor** in every frame;
the **horizon rolling five to fifteen degrees** off level and being wrenched back, again and again, following the tilt of whatever surface the sphere is on;
**vertical punches** as the operator's body moves;
**overshoots** — the frame lunging past the sphere on a direction change and snapping back onto it;
**focus permanently working** — riding the sphere, going soft for a beat on impacts, snatched back;
**foreground obstructions** — book spines, shelf edges, falling books, hanging pages and splintered board sweeping hard through the frame, **blacking out part of the picture and sometimes almost all of it for two or three frames** before the sphere is there again.

**But it never loses the sphere and never cuts away to find it.** Even when something wipes the frame, the object is there when it clears. **Wild, close, dynamic, relentless — and continuous.**

# **THE SET — BUILD THIS**

**A burned library.** A tall hall of dark scorched timber shelving, bay after bay, running away into blackness. Heavy uprights, black iron brackets, deep shadow inside every shelf. **The shelves are still full of books** — crowded upright rows in **oxblood red, deep forest green, ochre, faded blue, tan and cream**, small pale printed labels, all dulled by soot and grey dust but **still clearly coloured.** Collapsed rows, leaning stacks, books wedged flat, fanned open, spines swollen and split. Loose pages caught everywhere.

**The floor is covered**: drifted books splayed open, plaster chunks, splintered board, ash. **The air is thick** with dust and drifting ash, thick enough to see the light travelling through it.

**The light:** one weak, cold, blue-grey source raking from high on one side, cutting shafts through the dust, catching the top edges of boards and the tops of spines, **everything beneath falling to near-black.** No warm light, no fire, no glow, no visible lamp. Underexposed, pushed, muddy shadows, coarse grain.

**Down the face of one bay, a route exists** — ruined furniture that happens to lie this way. In order, top to bottom:

**the top board**, flat, books crowding in at one end;
**four short angled boards**, each hanging on a single iron bracket, **jutting from the shelf faces at alternating angles**, stepping down in a zig-zag like paddles;
**a lane of hardcovers laid flat, face down, in a line** along a lower board;
**a black iron bracket standing proud** of the burnt wood at the end of that lane, a bent nail beside it;
**a narrow vertical slot between two leaning stacks**, a hand's width wide, **with a short brass organ pipe wedged inside it**;
**a brass book-rail sprung out of the shelving in a long shallow arc**, blackened and dented, **with a comb of thin iron rods rising off it at even spacing**;
**a fallen wooden library ladder** leaning across two levels, rungs worn pale on their upper faces;
**a cracked drawer pulled half out of its runner**, its open top a short channel;
**a shelf cracked through the middle and sagging**, one side dropped ten centimetres, its front lip **split and folded downward**;
**a last short board that simply stops** — **a clean overhang with nothing beneath it**, only two bare iron brackets and a metre of open black air;
**and the floor**, with a lane through the debris running forward toward camera.

**And three thin dry laths span the route** — at the end of the ladder rung, across the open front of the drawer, and across the very lip of the final overhang. Thin, blackened, cracked along the grain, resting on nothing but their ends.

# **THE FEELING — MUSICAL, AND WRECKING THE PLACE**

**It is a marble run played on a burning building.** Two things at once, and both must be there:

**The rhythm is precise.** Every contact is **a distinct, deliberate note** — a knock, a ring, a crack — and you can count the beats: roughly one a second at the top, tightening to two a second across the middle, the long rest of the fall, then one enormous final note. **The impacts are never mush and never a continuous roar.**

**The world around it is chaos.** The sphere is a dense metal ball travelling fast through dry burned furniture, and **it breaks something at almost every contact.** Boards crack and splinter under it. Laths snap. Books are knocked loose constantly — **two, three, five at a time, going over the edges, tumbling down through the frame ahead of it and behind it**, landing flat and open, spilling pages. Loose paper is thrown up in its wake and hangs in the air. Splinters and grey dust jump off the wood at every hit. **By the bottom, the run behind it is a mess.**

**The notes are clean. The destruction is not.** Percussion over wreckage.

---

# **PHYSICS**

**A dense fifteen-centimetre metal ball.** **It never bounces up.** Its upward velocity after any impact is zero — it never rises, never hops, never rebounds, never arcs, never leaves a surface it has landed on. **The only airborne moment is the single drop near the end, and it is going downward.**

**It stays in contact with the set almost the whole way**, running, sliding and rolling **through** the structure rather than falling down it. Impacts **deflect it sideways along a surface, never upward.** Everything travels **forward and down — the direction the bird was facing before the fold, toward the boots** — never backward, never behind the shelving, never away.

**Everything it dislodges falls downward too**, with weight — books drop, they do not fly outward; splinters fall, they do not blast.

# THE SEVENTEEN SECONDS

**0.0s — the first frame is <<<image_2>>>, exactly.** BRD-1 in its bird form on the top board. **Held for no time — by 0.3s it has begun.**

**0.3–3.5s — THE FOLD, camera orbiting tight.** From the first movement the camera **arcs continuously around the machine**, roughly halfway around, **staying very close**: plates, panel lines, markings and dust legible, the shelving behind destroyed into blur, **the background swinging heavily and the angle changing every frame.**

**Mechanical, intricate, believable** — panels on real hinges, plates on real rails, parts folding into spaces that were visibly there. **Every piece of the sphere is a piece of the bird, moved.** Watchmaking, not a robot movie. No flourish, no pose, no reveal.

→ **0.3–0.7s:** every seam cracks open a millimetre at once; the shell becomes a jigsaw of hundreds of standing plates; dust lifts off it. → **0.7–1.5s:** the beak splits and the halves rotate back along the skull; the skull plates peel and hinge down; the head withdraws into the chest. **The eye lenses turn inward and are covered last — from that frame there is no face.** → **1.5–2.4s:** shoulder plates rotate forward over the cavity; wings fold three times, lie flat and slide inside; the tail collapses in; the torso shortens and rounds, spars and cabling glimpsed for a fraction of a second before plates seal over. → **2.4–3.0s:** the claws release the lip and the legs **fold up and inward and are swallowed**, leaving no stub and no socket. → **3.0–3.5s:** the raised plates **drop flush in a running wave**, each with a hard click, until the shell is **one unbroken sphere.** The orbit ends on its flank.

**3.5–4.3s — the first roll.** Round and legless, it **rolls forward along the top board**, its weight audible in the wood, **shoving two books off the edge ahead of it**, and runs off the front onto the first angled board.

**4.3–7.0s — the paddles. Four beats, alternating.** It lands on the first angled board — **the board cracks under it and dust jumps** — **runs its diagonal**, drops off the low end onto the next, **left, right, left, right**, four clean landings roughly **0.68s apart.** **Each landing splits wood and knocks books loose**; three or four go over on the way down, tumbling past the sphere through the frame. Each landing a dull knock; the run between a low grinding roll. **The camera slides down with it, hard on it the whole way.**

**7.0–8.0s — the lane and the bracket.** Onto the **flat lane of books laid face down**, running its length — **a smooth quiet passage, no impact, a soft rolling hush on covers, the covers shifting and sliding under it** — and it strikes the **iron bracket** at the end. **One hard bright ring.** The bracket turns it and **the front lip of the board breaks away**, dropping books.

**8.0–8.6s — the slot.** It drops into the **vertical slot between the leaning stacks and through the brass pipe wedged inside it** — **gone from view for half a second**, the sound going hollow and boxed-in — **and the stacks collapse behind it**, books sliding down into the gap as it comes out lower down.

**8.6–10.2s — the rail. The showpiece.** It lands on the **brass rail curving out of the shelving** and **runs the whole arc**, striking **the comb of iron rods one after another** — **a fast, even run of small bright rings**, a dozen in a second and a half, perfectly spaced. **The rail flexes and rings under the weight, two rods bending as it passes.** The most musical moment in the shot; **the camera is right on it.**

**10.2–11.1s — the ladder rung, and the first break.** Off the rail onto the **top edge of a ladder rung**, running its length — and **through the thin lath at the end**, which **snaps clean in the middle**, halves dropping away, **pale splintered wood bright against the char.** **One sharp dry crack.**

**11.1–12.0s — the drawer, and the second break.** Into the **open drawer channel**, running it end to end — **a dry wooden rattle, the drawer lurching further out of its runner under the weight** — **snapping the second lath** across its open front. **One crack**, and the drawer's contents slide out and fall.

**12.0–12.9s — the sagging shelf.** It lands on the **cracked sagging shelf** — **the crack opens further, the board dropping another few centimetres with a groan** — follows the slope, and the **split lip turns it out toward the front**, onto the last short board. **Books go over on both sides.**

**12.9–13.4s — the last lath, and the edge.** It runs the last board, **snaps the frail lath on the lip** — **one final crack** — and **comes off the edge.**

**13.4–14.0s — THE FALL.** **Nothing under it.** A clean vertical drop through open air, accelerating, **loose pages and splinters falling with it.** **And the sound stops** — no contact, no rolling: **a full half-second of near-silence, the longest gap in the piece.** The camera drops with it, still glued to it.

**14.0–14.3s — the floor.** **One enormous flat concussive impact** on the boards — the biggest note in the shot, the room ringing after it, **dust blown out from under it and a board cracking.** **It does not rise.** The impact throws it flat forward into a roll.

**14.3–15.1s — to the boots.** It rolls forward through the drifted paper and fallen books, **shoving one aside**, **slowing** — and **the boots come into frame ahead of it**, planted, unmoving. The camera is down on the floor with it now, lens a few centimetres above the boards. **Books and paper are still coming down behind it out of the shelving.**

**15.1–15.6s — contact.** It comes to rest **directly in front of him, square on, a hand's width from the toes of both boots, centred between them**, its last movement a gentle nudge against one toe cap — **a soft tap, almost nothing, the quietest sound in the piece.** It stops dead, **the readout turned toward him.** Behind it, the last book lands and everything goes quiet.

**15.6–17.0s — the counter.** The camera is close on the sphere where it sits, **the readout and both boots in the same frame** — panel sharp, boots dark and soft behind it. The panel is blank. Then, in one frame, it wakes:

→ **15.6s: `10`** → **16.6s: `9`**

**Red digits** — hard, flat, deep red, the same red as the seam. Small, plain, thin, **legible but never bright**; they light nothing and change no exposure. Each change instantaneous, **one tiny dry tick** on each. **It ends holding on `9`.**

# AUDIO

**No music of any kind, at any volume** — no drone, no swell, no riser, no sting, no bass hit, no synth, no strings, no instruments, no score. **Every sound is something in the room actually making it.**

**Close and tactile.** The **impacts on the run are distinct and separate**, each with a small space around it — **never mush, never a continuous roar.** Around them, the wreckage is messy and continuous: books slapping down, pages fluttering, splinters skittering, wood groaning. A stone hall full of paper: dry flat slap-back, low dead air.

**The vocabulary:** one sharp dry **crack** of hundreds of seals breaking at the unlock; a **dense fast cascade of tiny mechanical sounds** through the fold; the lock a **running wave of hard clicks**; the **low heavy rumble** of the roll, boards resonating under the weight; the **dull knock** of each paddle landing **with a wood crack inside it**; the **soft slap** of books going over and landing flat; the **hush** of running on covers; the **hard bright ring** of the bracket; the **hollow boxed tone** in the brass pipe; the **fast even run of bright rings** along the rod comb; the **dry rattle** of the drawer; the **three sharp cracks** of the laths; the **groan** of the sagging shelf dropping; the **half-second of silence** in the fall; the **enormous flat thud** on the floor; the **gritty roll**; the **soft tap** at the boot; then **two small dry ticks**, a second apart.

**The rhythm emerges from the impacts themselves** — never created by music, an instrument, pitching or tuning the sounds, or a beat underneath. **If an instrument or a score is audible, the piece is wrong.**

# AVOID

**No cuts anywhere.** No hidden cuts, no match cuts, no jump cuts, no whip-pans, no dissolves, no fades, no black frames, no cutaways, no second camera, no viewpoint the camera has not travelled to. **The headings are moments in one take.** **The sphere is in frame in every frame** — if the picture ever shows something without it, that is a cut and the shot is wrong.

**The camera never pulls back off the sphere** — never a wide, never an establishing view, never a survey of the room, never the whole bookcase in frame, never the object small in the picture. **It stays close enough that the sphere fills a third to a half of the frame throughout.**

**The first frame matches <<<image_2>>> but is never held** — no static opening, no waiting, no pause; the machine has begun by 0.3s.

**The camera orbits the machine through the whole fold** — real travel around the object, not a pan, not a tilt, not a turntable and not the object rotating while the camera holds. **We never go inside the machine** — no interior, no circuitry, no travelling through the eye.

**The transformation never morphs** — no melting, liquid metal, dissolving, particles, nanites, voxels, glitching, parts appearing from nowhere or vanishing. No CGI-slick, glossy, weightless look, no whooshing, no motion trails, no speed lines. No flourish, no pose, no reveal, no head-turn to camera. **The finished sphere has no legs, no spikes, no feet and no face.**

**The impacts stay distinct** — however messy the destruction gets, the contacts themselves never blur into a continuous clatter, never overlap into mush, and the beat is always countable.

**It never rises.** No rebound, no hop, no skip, no arc, no bouncing down the shelves, no floating, hanging or sailing. It never rolls uphill, never changes direction without something changing it, never flies, hovers or steers. **One free fall only — the last one.** **Everything it dislodges falls downward** — no debris flying outward, no explosive scatter, no shockwave, no slow-motion wreckage.

**The whole bookcase never collapses.** Boards crack, lips break, laths snap, books fall — but the structure stands, nothing shatters into fragments, and there is no demolition.

**The size never changes** — always about 15 centimetres, always smaller than the book spines, small against the boot.

**One lens** — 85mm, no zoom, no focal-length change. **No fisheye, no barrel distortion, no wide-angle character**, including at floor level. Never stabilised, gimbal, Steadicam, dolly, crane, drone or locked off — hard handheld in every frame.

**The books are never black, never uniform, never monochrome** — coloured, labelled, dusty and various. The grade stays cold, blue-grey, underexposed and desaturated — **no warm or golden wash, no amber, no firelight, no embers, no glow, no bloom, no flares, no visible practical lamp.**

**Nothing lights up** on the sphere except the readout from 15.6s. **The readout shows `10` then `9` and nothing else** — one second apart, instantaneous changes, small plain red digits; never flashing, blinking, pulsing, beeping, accelerating, glowing, lighting the boot or the floor, and never a timecode, milliseconds, a progress bar or a large number filling frame.

**It stops in front of him, not beside him** — square on, centred between both boots, readout facing him. Never rolls past, never stops to one side, never hits hard.

**Charlie is never seen above the boots** — no face, no body, no legs above the ankle, no hands, no creature, no reaction. **Only the two boots.**

**No explosion, no blast, no flash, no smoke, no fire.** No other person, no machine, no bird after the fold, no text and no interface graphics beyond the readout. The air is never clear — haze and dust throughout. No digital or clean modern look, no crisp digital sharpness, no artificial grain overlay — 35mm film, coarse, underexposed, muddy. No speed ramp, no slow motion, no strobing. No fade or cut to black.

# BRD-1 — 15s — INTERFACE ANIMATION

*The plate, alive. Red on black, nothing else. Data at full speed — density and rhythm are the subject.*

---

15 seconds, one continuous piece, no cuts.

**THE IMAGE IS THE REFERENCE PLATE AND NOTHING ELSE.** <<<image_1>>> is the exact starting frame and the exact visual language: its **pure black field**, its **burnt orange-red**, its line weights, its corner brackets, its bracketed border, its tick scales, its dot field, its filled data blocks, its YGGD mark, its code string, its timecode, its bar graph. **Every element that moves is one of those elements.** Nothing new is invented, nothing is restyled, nothing changes colour.

**Behind it: absolutely nothing.** Flat black, RGB 0,0,0, edge to edge, for all fifteen seconds. **No photograph, no room, no person, no machine, no environment, no depth, no gradient, no vignette, no glow, no bloom, no light source.** The black is empty. **Only the interface exists.**

**One colour: burnt orange-red on black.** Nothing is ever white, amber, yellow, green, blue or any other hue, and the red never brightens into glow — it is flat, thin, drawn.

---

## HOW IT MOVES

**Everything is snap, not glide.** Every change happens **in one frame**: elements appear whole, jump to a new position, and vanish. **No easing, no fades, no dissolves, no motion blur, no smooth tweens, no drifting animation, no bouncing, no elastic settle.** If something moves, it was somewhere else the frame before.

**Speed is the point.** At full flight there are **ten to twenty discrete changes per second** across the frame — far more than can be read. The eye should catch pattern and rhythm, never detail. **It is machine-time, not human-time.**

**Everything is aligned.** All motion is horizontal or vertical, snapped to an invisible grid. **No diagonal drift, no rotation, no scaling, no perspective, no 3D.**

---

## THE DOT FIELD — THE MAIN EVENT

**The dots are the subject of this piece, and they never stop.** They are **millions of bits of information being read**, and the frame should feel like watching a machine think at a speed no person could follow.

**Never still, for a single frame, at any point in the fifteen seconds.** There is no moment where the field is frozen, calm, static or decorative. Even in the quietest passages it is working.

**Density.** **Thousands of points across the frame at once**, in three sizes — a fine dust of very small dim points, a middle layer, and a scatter of brighter larger ones — so the field has depth without any blur or 3D.

**How they behave, all at the same time:**

**they re-sample every frame** — the whole field boiling, each point extinguishing and a new one appearing a pixel or two away, so the surface never holds still and shimmers continuously;
**sampling sweeps cross the frame constantly** — narrow vertical columns of points igniting to full brightness and dying behind, travelling left to right and right to left across the whole width, two or three sweeps running at once at different speeds;
**streams run along invisible lanes** — thin lines of dots flowing horizontally and vertically at high speed, appearing at one edge and gone at the other, like data being pulled through the frame;
**density waves** roll through the field — the population doubling and halving in travelling bands, so parts of the picture thicken while others thin;
**local ignitions** — small tight clusters flaring into dense knots wherever something is being examined, holding a beat, then dispersing back into the field;
**the field reacts to the boxes** — wherever a rectangle snaps down, the dots inside it immediately thicken, organise into rows and columns for a few frames, then break up again.

**All of it in single-frame steps.** No drifting, no floating, no easing, no motion blur, no particle physics, no gravity, no swirling and no smoke — **the points do not travel smoothly, they are simply somewhere new each frame.** The impression is of enormous quantities of data being sampled, not of dust in the air.

---

**What else moves, constantly:**
**the hairline skeleton** in the central rectangle rebuilds itself several times a second, nodes jumping, connecting lines re-drawing to different points, never settling on one solution;
**the central tracking rectangle** re-snaps: it jumps position, resizes taller or narrower, and its corner brackets detach and re-seat;
**sub-boxes** multiply and vanish — two, then nine, then thirty small hollow squares latching onto points in the field, then wiping down to one;
**the tick scales** along the top and bottom rules step and sweep, ticks lengthening and shortening in travelling waves;
**the three filled data blocks** roll numerals at high speed, digits cycling too fast to read, occasionally freezing on a value for a beat;
**the timecode** at the lower right runs, its milliseconds a blur;
**the bar graph** at the lower left jumps to new values every few frames;
**the code string** at the upper left flickers, characters replacing themselves;
**the YGGD mark** stays fixed and never animates — the one stable object in the frame.

**Frame-wide events, used sparingly — five or six times in the fifteen seconds:**

a **horizontal scan bar** sweeps top to bottom in three or four frames, everything it crosses flashing to solid for one frame;
a **one-frame inversion** — the entire frame goes solid red with black elements, then back;
a **full clear** — every graphic wipes off in one frame, leaving pure black for two or three frames before everything snaps back;
a **tear** — the frame splits horizontally and the two halves offset sideways for two frames;
a **density burst** — the dot field jumps to hundreds of points at once, then collapses to almost none.

---

## THE FIFTEEN SECONDS

**0.0–2.5s — idle.** The graphics are sparse and slow — the border, the brackets, the YGGD mark, the code string, the timecode running, the central rectangle empty, **two or three graphic events per second, no more.** **But the dot field is already working hard**: hundreds of points boiling across the whole frame, one slow sampling sweep crossing left to right, a thin stream running along the lower edge. **The machine is idle; the data never is.**

**2.5–5.0s — acquire.** The rectangle **snaps** to a new position and size. Sub-boxes appear: two, then five. **The field thickens hard toward the centre**, a second sweep starts in the opposite direction, streams multiply, and the first hairlines connect nodes inside the rectangle. The data blocks begin rolling. Tick waves start travelling along the rules. **Rate climbing: five or six graphic events per second.** One scan bar sweeps through at 4.2s.

**5.0–9.0s — the storm.** Full density. **Fifteen to twenty changes a second.** **The dot field is at maximum — thousands of points, four sampling sweeps running at once at different speeds and directions, streams crossing the frame in both axes, density waves rolling through, clusters igniting and dispersing several times a second.** Over it: boxes multiplying to thirty and more, stacked and overlapping; the skeleton rebuilding continuously; numerals rolling in all three blocks; tick waves running both rules at once; the bar graph jumping every few frames. **A one-frame inversion at 6.1s. A tear at 7.4s. A density burst at 8.3s.** This section should be genuinely too much to read — beautiful and hostile.

**9.0–11.5s — organise.** Just as fast, but the chaos begins to resolve: the thirty boxes reduce to twelve, then five, all converging on the same region; the skeleton stops re-solving and holds one shape; **the dot field pulls in from the edges toward the centre in a long inward density wave, the outer frame emptying while the middle packs solid.** The data blocks lock, one at a time, and stop rolling. **A full clear at 10.6s — black for three frames — and everything returns already simplified.**

Format. Live-action cinematic footage, 15 seconds, three shots, hard in-camera cuts at 5.0s and 10.0s. Anamorphic 35mm-origin look, handheld throughout, telephoto. No music of any kind at any point. No fade, no dissolve, no cut to black — the piece ends live, mid-moment.

Subject. A young soldier, CHARLIE, eighteen or nineteen, holding a newborn creature in his cupped gloved hands. His face, head, skin and features exactly as in <<<image_1>>> — take the face only, none of that image's lighting or background. His armour exactly as in <<<image_2>>>: worn matte plating, scuffed, dust-greyed, the gloves as shown with the fingertips left uncovered, bare fingerpads against the newborn. His skin is DRY and matte — no sweat, no sheen, no wetness on him anywhere; the newborn is the only wet thing in the frame. The newborn exactly as designed in <<<image_6>>>, at exactly the scale given in <<<image_7>>> — <<<image_7>>> is the sole authority on its size and it is SMALL, filling only his two cupped palms. It is DRENCHED — heavily, freshly wet, as if just delivered: a clear viscous birth fluid coating every millimetre of it, its thin coat plastered flat in soaked dark strings, wet membrane clinging along its back and limbs, fluid running visibly off it, threading between his bare fingerpads and beading and dripping from the edge of the glove. It burns BRIGHTER now: a hot, dense golden core, its light soaking through the wet coat and the thin skin so the whole small body glows from within, the fluid on it carrying and smearing that gold across every slick surface, the wet strings of its coat lit through, the drips off the glove catching gold as they fall.

The dead adult creature is present as in <<<image_5>>>: collapsed on the floor of the room, completely dark, absolutely no light anywhere on or in her body, her chest and belly extinguished, dust settling on her.

<<<image_8>>> is the LIGHTING AUTHORITY for this whole piece: match its darkness, its golden underlit key, its falloff and its blacks — but push it considerably further, darker than that reference.

Action. Shot one: the newborn lies almost inert in his cupped hands, head down, alive only in its ribs, which work fast and shallow. It cries — thin, cracked, breaking bursts, an animal sound, not a human baby's wail, the sound muffled by its own downturned face. It moves as an animal moves, not as a person does: three or four small involuntary events across the shot and nothing else — a weak shudder that runs the length of it around 1.4s, sending a bead of fluid down its flank; a single blind limb twitch around 3.6s; the head rolling a centimetre lower and stopping, never rising. Between them it is still. Canopy's voice arrives in the earpiece at 2.2s: "Now kill the infant."

Shot two: extreme close-up on Charlie's eyes, dry and matte, the pupils flicking once, the lids pressing shut a beat too long and dragging open. At 5.6s, barely voiced: "What?" The camera tilts slowly down his face, reaching his mouth by 8.2s — the lower lip unsteady, the nostrils flaring on a short breath, the jaw working once. At 8.6s: "It's just a baby."

Shot three: he stands holding the newborn, lost, breathing badly. His fear reads in microgestures only — a swallow, a nose flare, a thumb tightening against the newborn's wet back, the shoulders lifting and refusing to settle. At 10.8s Canopy, amused: "What do you care? It's a bloody sprout." Charlie does not answer. He looks down at the newborn, then off to the side, then back down. Hold live to 15.0s.

Subject. Charlie is a thin nineteen-year-old, head shaved close, in scuffed white-and-red armour with a high collar. His face is dry — matte skin, no sweat, no sheen, no damp — faintly reddened at the nose and around the eyes from exhaustion, a scab or two on his jaw, grey dust caught in the stubble of his scalp and in the pores of his cheeks. His eyes are tired, the lids heavy, the whites slightly bloodshot. The small dark earpiece from <<<image_3>>> sits in his right ear; it never lights up. He holds a newborn creature in his two cupped gloved hands: it is tiny, shorter than the palm of his glove, about the length of his thumb. The newborn is the only wet thing in the frame — its fine coat plastered flat to its body in dark wet spikes, its skin glossy and slick, clear viscous fluid pooled in his palm and running down the glove leather. Its huge eyes are shut. A warm golden ember glows deep in its tiny chest. There is no blood on it and nothing red anywhere.

The light — match <<<image_8>>>. The whole sequence is dim. It is underexposed well below a normal image, the blacks deep and clean and swallowing most of the frame, and the eye has to work to read it. There is no key light, no fill, no rim, no backlight and no practical anywhere in shot. Second, the dead adult creature: long, thin and grey, sitting up slumped back against the base of a bookcase, her legs splayed out in front of her across the fallen books and pointing toward Charlie, arms loose at her sides with her hands palm-down, her head tipped forward onto her chest. Her body emits no light anywhere: no glow in her chest, belly, coat, mouth or eyes, and none from the dark wet split low in the side of her belly. She is a matte grey shape. Reference. The attached image supplies only the machine's materials, its surface finish, its panel-line language and its grime — matte grey armour, fine seams, worn edges. Its silhouette is not preserved. In this sheet the machine has reconfigured and no longer looks like a bird in any way.

A prop and VFX reference sheet for a small piece of ordnance, laid out flat on an even dark charcoal-grey background. Landscape, 16:9, clean technical presentation, neutral studio lighting, no environment, no floor plane, no shadows cast.
The object. The bird machine has folded itself shut into a dense armoured seed. Its wings have wrapped forward and locked around the body; its legs have drawn up and inverted; its head has retracted entirely into the mass. What remains is a single compact form roughly 15 centimetres long: a heavy tapered ovoid, wide and blunt at the crown and drawn to a point at the base, its surface built from tightly overlapping armour scales that spiral around the body like the scales of a pine cone or the husk of a beech nut. The plates are matte grey, worn at their edges, industrially machined, with fine grime in every seam — the same material and wear as the reference. It reads as engineered, agricultural and cruel: a metal seed, made to be planted.
Its armed state. Between every overlapping scale, a continuous hairline of hard saturated red glows out from inside, brightest at the spiralling seams around the widest part of the body and fading toward the crown. At the crown, where the head went in, a single dark circular aperture with a red iris burning deep inside it. Set flush into one flank, a small rectangular display showing hard white seven-segment numerals with a decimal, reading tenths and hundredths. Around the base, three short claw-shaped anchors have driven out of the shell and splayed wide, locking the object down onto whatever it is standing on, their tips bitten in. No fins, no nose cone, no fuse, no wick, no warhead shape.
Layout. Across the top of the sheet, a small transformation strip of three silhouettes in sequence, drawn smaller than the main views: the original bird machine standing, then a mid-fold state with the plating rotating and wrapping and the legs inverting, then the sealed seed. Beneath it, four large views of the sealed armed object, all lit identically: side elevation at the left, three-quarter front in the centre, top-down at the upper right showing the spiral of the scales converging on the crown aperture, and base-up at the lower right showing the three splayed anchors.
Annotation. Thin white one-pixel leader lines with small right-angle elbows point to details, labelled in tiny monospaced type: the crown aperture, the seam glow, the flank counter, the anchor claws, the scale overlap. Along the bottom, a plain scale bar marked 15 cm with a small human hand silhouette beside it for comparison. Small monospaced header text at the top left reading BRD-1 // ORDNANCE FORM.
Finish. Photographic material rendering — machined matte metal, fine grime, worn edges, subtle specular on the scale edges. The register of a real film production's prop reference sheet. Precise, filmic, restrained.
Avoid. No bird. No wings, no beak, no head, no tail, no feathers, no legs, no bird silhouette anywhere in the four main views — only the transformation strip may show the bird, and only in its first frame. No classic bomb clichés: no round black cartoon bomb, no burning fuse, no dynamite sticks, no ticking alarm clock, no missile, no artillery shell, no fins, no nose cone, no warhead. No environment, background scenery, smoke, fire, explosion, sparks or motion blur. Nothing is cracked, burned or blown apart — this is armed, not destroyed. No blue, orange or green glow: the only emissive colour is the hard red, plus the white of the numerals. No text other than the labels described. Never larger than 15 centimetres.

Charlie, in profile inside a burning explosion, is lifted off the ground and carried to the left while his exosuit breaks apart and flies off him and flames, dust, books and wood stream across the foreground — photoreal war-film realism, 120fps slow motion, camera tracking left with him.

## 6.4 to 13.5s — THE FALL

**Physics, and this is not negotiable: it is a dense fifteen-centimetre metal sphere, and everything it does is fall and roll.**

**IT SLIDES. IT DOES NOT DROP FROM SHELF TO SHELF.**

**For almost the whole descent the sphere stays in contact with the bookcase** — running, sliding, skidding and rolling **through** it rather than falling down it. It is **working its way down through the structure**, finding a way through, passing from one part of the shelving to another, always touching something. **There is no free fall until the very end.**

**What that looks like — it travels through different parts of the shelves:**

it **runs along the length of a shelf**, low and fast, knocking the spines of standing books as it goes;
it **slips through a gap between two leaning stacks** and disappears for a beat before coming out lower down;
it **runs along the tops of a row of fallen books**, skidding on the covers;
it **drops a short step onto the next board and keeps going without stopping**, carrying its speed straight into another slide;
it **skids diagonally across a broken, sagging board**, following the slope, and is turned by a metal bracket into a new line;

**Each passage sends it somewhere new** — left, right, in behind a stack, out again — and it goes over each edge at a different point from where it arrived. **It is always moving, always in contact, always going downward overall.**

**AND THEN, ONCE, IT FALLS.** It comes off the last shelf and **there is nothing under it** — a **sudden, clean, silent drop through open air to the floor**, the only real fall in the piece, longer than anything before it and unexpected after all that contact. **Straight down. **It hits the floor dead** — the single heaviest impact in the piece — **does not rise, does not rebound, does not leave the boards**, and the impact **throws it flat forward** into a roll.

**Then it rolls to Charlie.**

**And it does damage — but subtle damage, the kind real weight does.** Each landing is heavy enough to hurt the shelf it lands on: **the board flexes, cracks, and splinters where it hits** — a dry split running through the dry burned wood, a corner giving way, the board sagging or dropping a few centimetres on one side — **but it never explodes, never shatters and never collapses the bookcase.** The damage is small, local and believable: a crack, a broken lip, a shower of splinters and dust, the shelf still standing.

**No music of any kind, at any volume, anywhere in the twenty seconds** — no drone, no swell, no riser, no sting, no bass hit, no synth, no strings, no percussion instruments and no score. **Every sound is something in the room actually making it.**

**The floor and the counter.** The impacts fall away. Then **three tiny dry ticks, exactly one second apart** — small, dull and mechanical, no tone, no beep, no alarm, no rise in pitch or volume between them. **The last sound is a tick.** No voice, no comms, no breathing from anyone, nothing answering.

## 【THE LAWS】

【UNDEREXPOSED, cold and near-colourless. 35mm anamorphic, wide open, grain in the shadows. 【FLAT AND MURKY, NOT CONTRASTY — no key, no fill, no rim, no backlight; the only warm source in the whole block is the light in her belly, and it is weak.】】

【【EVERY SHOT IS HANDHELD】: a real unsupported hand — drifting, jittering, correcting late, losing the subject by millimetres and hunting back. Never stabilised, never a gimbal, never a rig, never locked. 【Razor-thin focus that hunts, goes soft and lands late.】】

【【EVERY SHOT IS TOO CLOSE】: at or near macro. NO wide, NO establishing, NO room. 【Nothing is ever readable as a place.】】

【【HEAVY HAZE AND DRIFTING DUST IN EVERY FRAME】, macro ones included; a dirty front element smearing a soft veiling flare when the warm light catches it. 【If a frame looks clear, add more haze.】】

【【THE ACTING LAW】: 【ONE small involuntary thing at a time with stillness around it. Nothing pushed, nothing shaped, nothing presented to camera.】 【If it reads as acting, it is too big. If it reads as something the camera caught, it is right.】】

FAIL: the camera is stabilised, smooth or locked = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: any frame is wide or reads as a shot of a room = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: high contrast, a sculpted key, a rim light or a black void behind a subject = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: clean air in any frame = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: the earbud absent, in the left ear, in both, or glowing = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: her position differs from <<<image_6>>> = SHOT FAILED.

**The frame — frontal, far too close from the first frame, and closing the whole time.** We are **square on to his face** for all six seconds and it is an extreme close-up from the very start. **It only ever gets tighter.**

**Where it starts (0s).** His face fills the picture and is cropped top and bottom: the upper edge across the top of his brow, the lower edge under his chin. **One ear is just inside the LEFT-HAND EDGE OF THE PICTURE, part-cropped, with the earbud of <<<image_3>>> plainly visible in it** — see the block below for exactly which ear that is and why. No margin, no air, no shoulders, no collar, no room.

**Where it ends (6s).** **Near macro on a face — his eyes and his mouth and nothing else.** The upper edge cuts through his eyebrows, so **there is no forehead and no scalp in shot**; the lower edge sits just under his lower lip, so **there is no chin, no jaw and no neck.** Both cheeks run off the left and right edges. **His eyes occupy the upper half of the picture and are enormous.** His face is cropped on all four sides and does not fit in the frame.

The move between those two sizes is continuous and never stops.

At this size the skin is landscape: individual pores, the grain and texture of it, single lashes on the closed lids, the fine hairs of the brow, the sweat sitting in the skin, the dry cracked edge of the lip, the wet line at the rim of the eye, the pulse moving in the temple. **The eyes must be legible in enormous detail** — the iris texture, the moisture, the exact moment the lids part.

---

**WHICH EAR THE EARBUD IS IN — read this carefully, it is the thing that goes wrong.**

The earbud is worn in **CHARLIE'S OWN RIGHT EAR** — the ear on the same side of his body as his right hand.

**We are facing him.** He is looking toward the camera, so his body is mirrored relative to ours. **Therefore his right ear appears on the LEFT-HAND SIDE OF THE SCREEN — the left side of the picture as the viewer sees it.**

Say it both ways so there is no ambiguity:
**HIS right ear = SCREEN LEFT. The earbud is on the LEFT SIDE OF THE FRAME.**
**HIS left ear = SCREEN RIGHT. That ear is EMPTY — there is nothing in it, and nothing is ever shown in it.**

**If an earbud appears on the right-hand side of the picture, it is in the wrong ear and the shot has failed.** There is only ever **one** earbud in the shot, and it is on the screen-left side of his head.

**How it sits in frame.** In the opening framing that ear is at the very edge of the picture on the left, part-cropped, and the earbud is clearly visible in it — its exact design, size, shape and colour from <<<image_3>>>, dark and unlit, legible from the first frame. **As the dolly closes in the ear is gradually cropped out of the left side of frame** — it goes at around the four-second mark and is gone for the final tight crop. **It is never missing while that ear is in shot**, and it is never replaced by a headset, a headphone, a helmet piece or anything with a cable.

---

**His face fills the entire frame, so there is essentially no background** — at most a sliver of the wrecked space of <<<image_4>>> at a corner, destroyed to a dark unreadable wash. **There is no light source of any kind in this shot.** Nothing glows from below, nothing warm enters the picture, nothing lights him. **The creature is never seen in any form and casts nothing.**

**The lens.** Shot on 35mm film with a long **200mm prime**, wide open, reaching in from across the room — extreme compression, a plane so thin his near eye is sharp while his far eye is already soft. **No fisheye, no barrel distortion, no bowed lines, no wide-angle character.** Gritty documentary, not cinema: underexposed and pushed, coarse moving grain, dirty milky shadows, blown unprotected highlights, colour thin and desaturated toward grey-green, dust and haze on the front element. **Witnessed, not directed.**

**The camera — one slow dolly in, and nothing else.**

The camera travels **straight in on the axis**, continuously, from the first frame to the last. **It never stops, never eases, never pauses, never backs off and never reverses** — it is closing in every single frame, including the final one. It is **slow**: a quiet, steady, relentless creep that is barely perceptible second to second and unmistakable across the six.

**The frame tightens by physical travel, not by the lens** — no zoom, no digital zoom, no crash zoom, no snap zoom, no focal-length change and no dolly-zoom. There is **no orbit, no arc, no pan, no tilt, no rise, no drop and no reframe** — the angle at 6s is the same frontal angle as at 0s. **Only the distance changes.**

Underneath the move it is **handheld and properly unsteady** — much shakier than a careful operator would allow, and at 200mm every fault of his body is multiplied into the frame:

**a constant nervous tremor** running through the whole picture, never still for a single frame;
**the frame breathing** up and down with the operator, deeper and more obvious than a float;
**drift** — his face sliding off centre and being hauled back late and clumsily, overshooting a little each time;
**the horizon rolling** three or four degrees one way, hanging there, being wrenched back past square and rolling the other way;
**two or three small vertical knocks** where the operator's weight shifts and the picture jolts;
**focus that never settles** — riding on his near eye, hunting past it as the distance keeps changing, going properly soft for a beat and being snatched back, and only landing hard at the very end.

**It grows as the camera closes.** By the last two seconds it is barely controlled: his eyes are sliding around the frame, an eye leaving the edge and being dragged back once, the roll steeper, the corrections later. **The shot ends unsteady.** It is never so violent that his face becomes unreadable — but there is not one calm, level, well-composed frame in the six seconds.

---

**THE ACTION — three things, in this order, and they do not overlap.**

**One — the head comes up.** He begins exactly as <<<image_4>>> leaves him: **head lowered, face angled down, eyes closed.** Then his head **rises** — slow, continuous, unhurried, one unbroken movement with no hesitation in it and no stopping halfway, the chin travelling up until his face is level and square to us. It takes about a second and a half. **He is not being pulled up by anything; he is choosing to lift it.** No jerk, no snap, no flourish, no tilt to one side, no roll of the head, no shake.

**Two — the eyes open.** They open **before the head has finished rising**, not after — about two-thirds of the way up, so the last of the movement happens with him already looking. They open **once, cleanly, and stay open** — no flutter, no blinking flurry, no squint, no slow dreamy reveal. What is behind them when they arrive is **decided** — but he is also frightened, and that shows. **The decision is immovable and the body around it is not.**

He looks **straight ahead, level, a few degrees off the lens axis** — past us, at whatever is in front of him. **He never looks into the camera.**

---

**THE NERVES — small, involuntary, and running underneath the whole shot.**

He has already made the decision and he is terrified of it. **None of this ever touches the decision** — it is his body leaking while his mind stays where it is. Everything here is tiny and legible only because we are this close:

**his breathing** fast, shallow and high, catching once and being let out unevenly;
**a hard dry swallow** during the rise, the whole throat moving, and the beginning of a second one before the word that he does not finish;
**the pulse visible and quick** in his temple and at the side of his throat;
**a fine tremor in the head itself** — not a shake, a vibration, so the level position he arrives at is never perfectly still;
**one nostril flaring** slightly on an intake;
**the jaw muscle jumping** once at the hinge and going quiet;
**a tic** — the skin tightening once at the outer corner of the eye and releasing;
**the corner of his mouth pulling** a fraction into something that is nearly a grimace and being bitten off immediately;
**the lower lip trembling** for a fraction of a second, twice, each time stopped;
**his eyes going wetter** as the shot goes on — the wet line at the rim thickening, without a tear ever forming or falling;
**one blink** after they open, hard and fast and single, at about four seconds, and then nothing.

**The rise itself carries the nerves too.** It is one unbroken movement, but not a smooth mechanical one — it drifts a hair off true and corrects, and it is very slightly uneven in speed, the way a movement is when the person making it is holding themselves together.

**None of it is a performance.** No pulling faces, no gasping, no mouthing, no shaking his head, no visible act of steeling himself. If any of it read as acting rather than as something escaping him, it is too big.

**AND THEN IT ALL STOPS — this is the turn of the shot.**

**A fraction of a second before he speaks, every one of those things ends at once.** Not gradually, not one by one — in the space of a few frames the nerves **drain out of him** and his face goes **cold.** The tremor in his head stills. The lip stops. The jaw goes quiet. The breathing drops away to nothing. The eyes settle and lock and stop moving.

**What is left is stoic.** Emptied out. No fear on it, no anger, no sadness, no effort, no resolve being summoned — **nothing at all**, which is far colder than any expression would be. It is the face of someone who has stopped negotiating with himself.

**He says the word out of that stillness, and he stays in it.** After the word there is no return: no shudder, no exhale of relief, no swallow, no blink, no flicker of feeling, no aftermath. **The nerves do not come back.** He holds cold, set and unreadable to the last frame of the shot.

**The contrast is the point** — four seconds of a body betraying itself, then a hard, quiet, complete stop, and the word arriving out of the flat calm on the other side of it.

**Three — he says it.**

**"No."**

## 【THE LAWS】

Not one.】】】

【【BOTH OF THEM ARE UNDERPLAYING TO THE POINT OF ALMOST NOTHING.】 【In the last version both reactions came out too big. The correction is not "a bit smaller" — it is 【FAR SMALLER THAN FEELS LIKE ENOUGH】.】】

It is matte and panelled, it does not move at all, and its eyes are dark and unlit.

**Action.** Charlie is stationary for most of the shot. Three times, and only three times, he moves in a short sudden burst — a fast half-turn on the loose books, two or three quick uneven steps where his footing slips, then an abrupt stop — and after each burst he stands completely still for a long time. He never crosses the room, never leaves her side, never travels anywhere, and never repeats the same movement. He never lowers the newborn or brings it against his chest. He speaks twice and nothing answers him either time.

**Environment.** The interior of a ruined library. Tall dark-wood bookcases still packed with books, heavy square columns, and a stone floor buried under hundreds of fallen books lying splayed open and stacked in drifts, mixed with broken plaster, masonry and grey dust. Both bodies are on top of the books. Spreading from beneath the dead creature's hips is a shallow pool of deep amber-gold translucent liquid, like dark honey lit from within, two metres across, soaking into the paper at its edges and steaming faintly. That pool is the only glowing thing in the room: the light is in the liquid, not in her. It lights the books at its edge, the underside of her hip and Charlie's boots, and nothing else.

**Camera.** A true overhead plan view. The lens points straight down at the floor, near-vertical, from three or four storeys up in the dark under the ceiling. We see the tops of things: the top of his head, the top of her skull with her body foreshortened away beneath us, the tops of the bookcases, the flat spread of books. No horizon, no wall seen face-on, no room receding into the distance. Charlie and the dead creature together occupy a good part of the frame — we are high but positioned directly over them, not surveying the building. The camera makes one single unbroken move for the whole 12 seconds: it rotates slowly around the vertical axis while descending toward them at the same time, so the floor geometry turns beneath us while the frame closes in. The move is smooth and motorised, like a crane or a drone, and it is so slow it takes a second or two to notice it at all. It never stops, never speeds up, and never shakes. 35mm anamorphic, wide open, shallow focus, oval bokeh, fine film grain.

**Look.** Cold, precise and desaturated, in the register of David Fincher. The ambient is weak cold grey-blue-green light falling from high windows and dying before it reaches the corners. The amber pool is the only warm element and it stays contained; the image is never golden or warm overall. Deep clean blacks, underexposed, no key light, no fill, no rim, no backlight. Thick grey haze hangs in the volume of the room and slow drifting smoke lies in flat sheets and lazy curls between the camera and the floor, so we look down through several layers of atmosphere and the floor is softened and greyed by it. Dust turns slowly. The cold shafts from the high windows are made solid by the haze and strike the floor in hard bright patches. The smoke drifts slowly and never billows, rolls or gusts, and the image stays dark and readable throughout.

**Timing.** 0–1.6s: we are already directly above them and already turning and descending, so slightly it barely registers; Charlie stands completely still with the newborn held out; smoke crosses between us and them. → 1.6–2.4s: first burst — a fast half-turn, two quick uneven steps that nearly go wrong, an abrupt stop; books slide and settle. → 2.4–4.4s: nothing at all; he stands; the frame keeps turning. → 4.6s: without moving, he says, quietly and reasonably, as if it will work: "It's just a baby." → 5.1–7.2s: nothing answers; total silence on the channel; he holds still through all of it, longer than is comfortable. → 7.2–7.9s: second burst — a sharp turn the other way, three fast unsteady steps, a hard stop with his shoulders up; he is still beside her. → 7.9–8.7s: nothing again; we are noticeably lower now and both bodies are larger in frame. → 8.9s: he stops mid-turn and says, faster and higher, the reasonableness cracking: "Canopy. It's just a baby." — his head tips very slightly toward his own right shoulder as he says it, without him noticing. → 9.4–12.0s: he stands completely still beside the dead creature with the newborn held out; the books settle; smoke drifts across both bodies; the pool glows and she does not; the camera keeps turning and descending to the last frame, tighter, with the room squeezed out to the edges. Nothing answers, and the shot ends there mid-move and mid-silence.

**Audio.** No music of any kind, at any volume, anywhere in the shot. Everything is heard from high up in a big stone hall full of paper, with a dry flat slap-back off the shelves and a low dead air underneath. Boots scuffing and sliding on loose paper, book covers slapping, pages tearing, plaster grit crunching, armour plates knocking, his breath fast and audible from this height, the newborn's thin quick breathing small and far, and a slow thick drip of liquid. Charlie speaks exactly twice, in his own voice, and nothing replies. The line at 4.6s comes back off the shelves as a dry flat echo, tiny in a very big space. The shot ends on room tone with no fade and no resolve.

**Avoid.** No cuts. No music, drone, swell, sting or riser. No reply, second voice, comms chatter, beep, squelch or transmission tone. No glow anywhere on the dead creature. No movement, blink or twitch from the dead creature or from the bird machine. The dead creature is never lying flat, face-down or sprawled, and never leaves the frame. The bird machine is never larger than 15 centimetres and never on the floor or on the left. No angled or three-quarter camera view, no horizon, no visible face. No handheld, shake, jitter, whip or speed change. No pacing, marching, striding, running, bouncing, swaying, fidgeting or repeated walk cycle. No bare, sandy, orange or featureless ground, no desert, no arena, no outdoors. No white, milky or opaque liquid, and the pool never spreads across the whole floor. ## 【THE LAW — TRUE OF EVERY SHOT】

**【【EVERY FRAME IS HANDHELD AND SHAKY.】** 【Unsupported, never still, never stabilised, never a gimbal, never a rig, never locked — not for one second.】 【The frame jitters on a pulse, sags, tips off level, drifts, overshoots when it corrects, slides off the subject and hunts back. 【When he moves, the camera is CHASING him and losing him.】】 【BUT SUBTLE: a real tired operator's arm, not action shake.】 【The focus HUNTS: it drifts, overshoots, lands late. Sharpness is earned.】】**

**【【CLOSE. ALWAYS TOO CLOSE.】** 【Tight singles and macro. 【NEVER a full body, NEVER a wide, NEVER the whole room, NEVER a clean two-shot.】】 【The subject is bigger than the frame and overflows the edges. 【If a frame shows a complete figure or a complete object, IT IS TOO WIDE — push in.】】】**

**【【SUBTLE ACTING. MICROGESTURES. ALWAYS.】** 【One small involuntary thing at a time, with stillness around it. 【The face changes TEMPERATURE, not SHAPE.】】 【Nothing pushed, nothing shaped, nothing presented to camera. 【IF IT READS AS ACTING, IT IS TOO BIG.】】 【A camera this close makes a millimetre enormous.】】**

**【【35mm ANAMORPHIC, WIDE OPEN】** — oval bokeh, anamorphic glass, fine grain, 【shallow depth of field, the plane millimetres deep.】】

**【【THE LIGHT】** 【The amber pool on the floor is 【THE ONLY SOURCE】 and it lights everything 【FROM BELOW】.】 【Faint, warm, uneven, local — two paces from the pool the world is black.】 【UNDEREXPOSED, FLAT AND MURKY, NOT CONTRASTY. 【No key, no fill, no rim, no backlight.】】 【Fine dust and warm steam only — NO fog, NO smoke, NO white veil.】】

**【【NO MUSIC. NONE. ANYWHERE. AT ANY VOLUME.】** 【NO score, NO strings, NO piano, NO choir, NO pad, NO drone, NO ambient bed, NO synth, NO swell, NO rising tone, NO braaam, NO sting, NO hit, NO riser, NO whoosh, NO shimmer, NO chime, NO bell, NO heartbeat pulse, NO percussion, NO tonal or emotional cue of any kind.】 【Not under the voices, not after them, not faintly, not far away.】 【EVERY OTHER SOUND IS MADE BY SOMETHING PHYSICALLY IN THAT ROOM.】】**

**【【THE NEWBORN】** 【A HANDFUL — no bigger than a grown man's hand, sitting entirely inside two cupped palms.】 【Wet, thin, loose-skinned, coat plastered flat and dark.】 【【ITS EYES NEVER OPEN — not once, not partly, not for a single frame.】】 【【AND IT HAS NO TAIL】 — the body ends at the hindquarters.】】**

FOR SECONDS.】** 【The subject of this film is 【FIVE MINUSCULE WET FINGERS CLOSING AROUND ONE BIG DIRTY ARMOURED FINGER.】】 【They are 【SEPARATE, COUNTABLE, INDIVIDUAL FINGERS】 — not a paw, not a mitten, not a lump, not a blur, not a fist, not a stump.】 【【PALE, TRANSLUCENT, WET AND WRINKLED, EACH ONE ABOUT THE THICKNESS OF A MATCHSTICK】, with tiny soft nails like grains of rice, and creases at the knuckles.】 【They read against the glove because 【THE GLOVE IS DARK, MATTE AND FILTHY AND THE LITTLE HAND IS PALE AND SHINING WET.】】 【HOLD ON THEM. If a viewer cannot count the fingers, THE SHOT HAS FAILED.】】**

**【【2. ONE UNBROKEN SHOT. NO CUT. THE FOCUS DOES THE TRAVELLING.】** 【NO cut, NO reframe, NO angle change, NO insert, from the first frame to the last.】 【The camera never moves to a new position. 【What changes is WHERE THE FOCUS IS】: it lives on the tiny hand, and when the order arrives 【IT TRAVELS BACK ONTO CHARLIE'S FACE AND STAYS THERE.】】 【The lens finds him. The camera does not go to him.】】**

**【【3. CHARLIE NEVER SPEAKS. NOT A WORD. NOT A SOUND.】** 【He does not answer, does not question, does not protest, does not whisper, does not gasp out a word.】 【【THE ONLY VOICE IN THIS FILM IS THE SYSTEM'S, ONCE.】】 【Everything that happens to him happens on his face and in his breath.】】**

**【【4. EVERY FRAME IS SHAKY.】** 【HANDHELD, UNSUPPORTED, NEVER STILL, NEVER STABILISED — not for one second, not in the macro, not while nothing is happening.】 【The frame jitters on a pulse, sags, tips off level, drifts, overshoots when it corrects, slides off and hunts back. 【The focus travel shakes too.】】 【BUT SUBTLE: a real tired operator's arm, not action shake. At macro distance a millimetre reads as a lurch — that is the amount.】】**
