## THE SHOT — 0.00–8.00

【— 【0.00–1.20 — THE LITTLE HAND, ALONE, IN THE AIR】: 【the shot opens ALREADY IN MACRO on the tiny wet hand, held up out of the palm, 【opening and closing at nothing.】】 【【WE SEE EVERY FINGER】: five of them, pale and translucent and shining wet, thin as matchsticks, the tiny nails catching the amber, 【splaying wide and curling in again, slow and blind and uncoordinated.】】 【It is not reaching for anything. It does not know there is anything to reach for.】 【The gloved finger is there, dark and out of focus, waiting at the edge of the plane.】】

【— 【~1.50 — IT TOUCHES HIM BY ACCIDENT】: 【the little hand swings across and 【the backs of the small fingers brush the side of the big gloved index finger】 — 【and stop.】】 【A beat of nothing: the tiny fingers resting against dark scratched armour, pale on black, wet on matte.】 【The focus finally lands, hard and shallow, 【and both are sharp together for the first time.】】】

【— 【~2.20 — AND THEY CLOSE, ONE AT A TIME】: 【【THIS IS THE MOMENT OF THE FILM AND IT IS SLOW.】】 【the small fingers curl over the glove 【NOT ALL AT ONCE — one, then two more, then the last, each folding over the armoured surface separately】, the pads flattening and whitening slightly where they press.】 【【THE THUMB COMES LAST】, laying across the others.】 【【THE WHOLE HAND IS SMALLER THAN ONE SEGMENT OF HIS FINGER】 — the fingertips do not meet, they do not reach halfway round.】 【The grip is 【surprisingly hard and completely blind】: a reflex, not a decision. The little arm goes tense and trembles faintly.】 【The wet skin sticks and slides a millimetre on the plate.】 【HOLD HERE, LONG, AND LET US LOOK AT IT.】】

【— 【~3.50 — AND THE CRYING STOPS】: 【the thin broken sound breaks off mid-breath. 【NOT soothed, NOT comforted — it simply STOPS, the way a newborn stops.】】 【Its breathing goes quick and shallow and quiet.】 【【ITS EYES DO NOT OPEN — they are sealed shut, smooth and wet and swollen closed, and they stay that way for every frame of this film.】】】

【— 【3.50–4.60 — AND NOTHING HAPPENS】: 【the gloved finger does not move. The tiny fingers hold. The frame drifts, loses the plane, finds it again. Behind, the blur of his face does not move.】 【HOLD. Let it become almost peaceful.】】

【— 【AT ~4.60 — CANOPY SPEAKS, ONCE (<<<audio_2>>>)】: 【the voice arrives in his right ear. 【The frame does not change. The focus does not move yet.】】

**"Charlie Zero One.... Kill the infant."**

【【HOW IT SOUNDS】: 【dry, flat, unhurried, mildly polite, completely without emotion — 【a system reading out a routine instruction it has read out a thousand times.】】 【A short flat pause between the callsign and the order, as if pulling a record.】 【Thin and slightly compressed, small and close, as if inside his ear only: 【no room reverb, no echo, no squelch, no static, no beep before or after, no distortion.】】 【NOT menacing, NOT deep, NOT growling, NOT whispered.】 【The horror is that it is bored.】】

【— 【6.00–6.40 — AND NOTHING HAPPENS AGAIN】: 【FOR MOST OF A SECOND, NOTHING. 【The words have not landed.】 The tiny fingers still grip. The amber still drips. The focus is still on the hand.】】

**【【— ~6.40 — AND THEN THE FOCUS GOES TO HIM.】** 【【THE PLANE TRAVELS BACKWARD, from the tiny hand to his face】 — 【slowly, unsteadily, in the same unbroken frame, the camera never moving.】】 【【IT HUNTS ON THE WAY】: it drifts past him, overshoots into the darkness behind, comes back, and 【lands on his face LATE.】】 【【THE TINY HAND STAYS IN FRAME】, low, going soft — a pale warm blur still wrapped around the finger, 【never leaving the picture.】】 【And the face arrives sharp.】】**

【— 【6.40–8.00 — AND HIS FACE TURNS】: **【【THE HORROR ARRIVES IN PIECES AND EVERY PIECE IS TINY.】】** 【【the eyes stop moving completely】 and go glassy, fixed on his own hands】 — a pause — 【【the pupils contract】】 — a pause — 【【the breath cuts off mid-inhale, audibly】】 — a pause — 【【the jaw sets and one muscle jumps under the cheek】】 — 【【the skin pulls tight at the temple】】 — 【【the corners of the mouth drop a millimetre and hold】】 — 【【and the eyes go wet, without a single tear falling.】】】

【【THE FACE DOES NOT CHANGE SHAPE. IT CHANGES TEMPERATURE.】 【The same face that was amazed a minute ago is now the face of someone who has just understood what he is for.】】

【【AND HE SAYS NOTHING.】 【No word, no whisper, no sound, no answer.】 【NO gasp, NO recoil, NO flinch, NO mouth falling open, NO wide theatrical eyes, NO head-shake, NO tears running, NO looking up, NO looking around.】 【【HIS EYELINE NEVER LIFTS FROM HIS OWN HANDS.】】 【He does not take his finger back.】】

【— 【AND IT ENDS WHILE IT IS STILL HAPPENING】: 【his face sharp and lit faintly from below, holding; the pale blur of the tiny hand still gripping at the bottom of frame; steam still lifting.】 【The camera stays too long, still shaking, still hunting focus on him.】 【AND THEN THE FILM SIMPLY STOPS — on the lit image, mid-breath, mid-drift. NO cut to black. NO fade. NO darkening.】】

**End state:** his face sharp and low-lit in the murk, eyes fixed and wet, mouth closed, breath stopped — and below him the soft pale blur of five tiny fingers still wrapped around his gloved one.

FAIL: its hand wraps all the way around his finger = SHOT FAILED — smaller than one segment of it, the fingertips never meeting.

FAIL: THE FOCUS NEVER REACHES HIS FACE = SHOT FAILED — it travels back onto him at ~6.40 and stays.

STANDING LAWS — IN FORCE OVER EVERY FRAME OF THIS PIECE.
No music of any kind, ever — no score, no drone, no swell, no sting, no riser, no pad, no hum used as music. Silence under everything.
No hard cut to black, no fade, no dissolve, no vignette-out — the piece ends live, mid-moment, on a working frame.
CHARLIE DOES NOT CRY. Not one tear, not one frame. No tears, no welling, no wet shine, no tear track, no glint or reflection in the eyes. His eyes are DRY and MATTE always. He is not sad and not weeping — he is CONFUSED and DESPERATE, and it shows only in microgestures.
THE ACTING LAW. Human and subtle, which does not mean blank or motionless. Emotion leaks in millimetres, through the mouth, the nose, the eyes, the hands and the arms — one gesture at a time with stillness between, never several at once, never a performance. Restrained, coiled, Fincher: the tension comes from stillness, proximity and time.
THE CREATURE ACTING LAW. The newborn is ANIMAL, not human: mostly inert, finely trembling, broken only by sudden scheduled involuntary moves. It moves LESS than feels right.
ALL CREATURE EYES ARE SOLID BLACK, edge to edge — no iris, no pupil, no sclera, no catchlight, no amber, no glow, no sparks.
The earpiece is always in his RIGHT ear, matte, and NEVER glows or lights up.
The gloves are FULL — the fingers are entirely covered in black leather. No fingerless gloves, no exposed fingertips, no bare skin on the hands.
THE ANATOMY LAW — READ THIS TWICE. Every hand in this piece is A HUMAN MALE HAND INSIDE A BLACK LEATHER GLOVE: five fingers, correct knuckles, correct proportions, a wrist, an armoured cuff. In previous generations the opening frame rendered as an unidentifiable fleshy organic mass with hair growing out of it, with no readable hand — WRONG, WRONG, WRONG. Nothing in this piece is organic tissue, muscle, viscera, fur, a nest, a cocoon or an abstract form. If a frame does not clearly read as a gloved human hand holding a small creature, the shot has failed.
THE GRIP LAW. From 1.5s to the last frame of the piece, the newborn's tiny hand is CLOSED AROUND CHARLIE'S GLOVED INDEX FINGER and never lets go. This contact is the subject of the piece. It must be visible, unmistakable and continuously held — in Shot 1 after 1.5s, and in EVERY FRAME of Shot 2. In a previous generation Shot 2 rendered with no grip at all — WRONG.
THE AIR LAW. Haze, drifting dust and a few subtle stray embers in EVERY frame, macros included. No frame contains clean air, and no frame is a black void — the ruined library is always behind, even when unreadable.
THE MOOD LAW. Severely underexposed, darker than feels right, cold and near-colourless except the newborn's warm light. Camera human and handheld, never sterile, never locked.
THE CONTINUITY LAW. The two shots are the same instant of the same scene, seconds apart, same hands, same finger, same grip, same creature, same light. The light must MATCH EXACTLY across the cut: same golden ember below as the only source, same intensity, same colour temperature, same brutal falloff, same crushed blacks, same grain, same haze density. Nothing brightens, cools, warms, lifts or changes lens at the cut.
THE REFERENCE LAW. The references below are authorities for DESIGN, FACE, MATERIALS, SCALE and LIGHT ONLY. NONE of them is a framing reference. Do not copy any reference's composition, camera position, crop or shot size. Every framing is built from the written description.
No gore, no blood, no wounds anywhere. No other creature appears. No drone, machine or robot appears. No legible text, signage, numerals or branding anywhere in frame.

Format. Live-action cinematic footage, 15 seconds, TWO shots, one hard in-camera cut at 8.0s. Anamorphic 35mm-origin look, handheld throughout, telephoto.

【【SHOT ON 35mm ANAMORPHIC, WIDE OPEN】 — oval bokeh, anamorphic glass, fine film grain in the shadows. 【Anamorphic in every shot, including the macro ones.】 【SHALLOW DEPTH OF FIELD THROUGHOUT: a plane millimetres deep, everything else soft.】】

【【THE AIR】: 【fine dust drifting, the faintest depth haze, warm steam lifting off the hot liquid.】 【NO fog bank, NO smoke, NO white milky veil — the image stays DARK and CLEAR.】】

**【【EXTREME CLOSE-UPS. EVERY SHOT. NO EXCEPTIONS.】】** 【Tighter than is comfortable, at or past macro. 【The subject is always bigger than the frame and overflows the edges — part of a face, part of a hand, part of a body, never a whole one.】 【If a frame shows a complete head, a complete animal, a complete object or a complete pair of hands, IT IS TOO WIDE — push in until it does not fit.】】

## 【THE CAMERA LAW】

**【【ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE. NO CUTS ANYWHERE.】 【The camera never stops rolling and the frame never jumps. Everything that happens — her end, the light leaving, the rise into the air — is carried by ONE unbroken move.】 【The change from her face to the particle in the air is made by the CAMERA PHYSICALLY DRIFTING UPWARD, never by a cut, never by a dissolve, never by a transition of any kind.】】**

**【【EVERYTHING IS HANDHELD, AND MORE HANDHELD THAN THE LAST VERSION — THE PREVIOUS TAKE STILL CAME OUT TOO SMOOTH.】 【The operator is holding a heavy camera far too close with no support and it SHOWS CONSTANTLY: the frame is never still for a single second — it drifts, jitters, sags, kicks slightly on his pulse and his breathing, tips off level and comes back, overshoots when he corrects, and slides off the subject and hunts back onto it more than once.】 【THE UNSTEADINESS IS VISIBLE AT ALL TIMES, INCLUDING WHILE HOLDING AND WHILE RISING — there is no moment anywhere in these twelve seconds where the frame settles.】 【It is not violent shake: it is a real tired arm at macro distance, where a millimetre reads as a lurch.】 【AT THESE DISTANCES EVERY TINY MOVEMENT IS ENORMOUS.】 【NEVER stabilised, NEVER a gimbal, NEVER a rig, NEVER a smooth glide, NEVER a locked frame — and never an action-judder effect either: a real hand that cannot keep still.】】**

【【TOO CLOSE, THROUGHOUT】: 【tighter than is comfortable, at or near MACRO from the first frame to the last. NO wide, NO establishing, NO full body, NO room. Nothing here is ever readable as a place — only coat, eye, air and light, enormous.】】

【【THE FOCUS IS NOT RELIABLE】: 【the plane is millimetres deep and it is being found by hand, in the dark. It HUNTS — goes soft, overshoots, comes back; sometimes it lands late, sometimes on the wrong thing.】 【SHARPNESS IS EARNED, NEVER GIVEN.】】

## THE SHOT — 0.00–12.00

【— 【0.00–0.80 — WE ARE ALREADY TOO CLOSE】: 【the frame opens on a readable view of her: the brow ridge, one black eye, part of the muzzle, the dusty matted coat — 【plainly HER, matching <<<image_1>>> and <<<image_3>>> exactly】 — off-axis, badly composed, cut by the frame edge, the room dissolved to soft dark behind her, heavy haze across everything, her ember guttering at its lowest.】 【A slow unsteady drift inward begins here and never stops.】 【At ~0.60 a small dry CLICK, off-screen: her breath stops for a beat, and nothing else moves.】】

【— 【0.80–2.80 — IT DRAINS OUT OF HER】: 【the fine trembling slows by degrees; the small pressure she was holding releases; the head sinks a centimetre under its own weight; the black eye stays lifted, looking off-frame at something we never see.】 【A SUBTRACTION, NOT A MOVEMENT — she is doing LESS and less.】 【One low half-swallowed broken sound in the chest, small and ugly, not a cry.】】

【— 【AT ~2.80 — THE ONE SOUND. THE ONLY LOUD THING IN THE FILM.】: 【ONE single, haunting, agonised GROWL-SQUEAL tears out of her.】 【THE REFERENCE IS A LARGE FARM ANIMAL AT ITS VERY END: raw, high, cracking, panicked, coming from the whole body and not from the throat — 【the kind of sound that empties a barn】 — unbearable to listen to and completely uncontrolled, overloading and distorting the too-close mic.】 【IT LASTS ABOUT ONE SECOND: it tears upward, cracks in the middle, and 【STOPS DEAD MID-SOUND】 — it does not taper, it does not fade, it does not finish.】 【The jaw hauls open wider than at any other moment, the face pulls tight with the effort, the neck strains once, the nostril slits flare and stick with the wet — 【but the body does NOT thrash: no writhing, no head thrown back, no flailing. THE SOUND DOES THE WORK, NOT THE CHOREOGRAPHY.】】 【The operator loses her as it hits and corrects late; the focus goes soft right across it.】】

【— 【AT ~3.90 — AND SHE IS GONE, IMMEDIATELY】: 【the instant the sound stops, everything lets go AT ONCE: 【the strained face SLACKENS IN A SINGLE FRAME】, the jaw dropping loose and staying open on nothing, the head settling a centimetre, 【the eye still open and simply stopped.】】 【NO second breath. NO shudder. NO tremble. NO slow fade. NOTHING follows it.】 【The change from a living animal to a dead one happens between two frames.】】

【— 【3.90–5.00 — THE DEAD FRAME】: 【nothing. The open loose mouth, the stopped eye, the ember at its lowest, dust settling on the wet surface of the eye. Only dust and haze still moving.】 【HOLD IT PAST COMFORT】 — the frame still drifting in, still correcting, on a face that has stopped answering.】

【— 【5.00–8.00 — THE WARMTH COMES OUT OF HER COAT】:

**【READ THIS FIRST — THE LAST GENERATION FILLED THE FRAME WITH LONG STRAIGHT GLOWING RODS, LIKE LIT STICKS OR FIBRE-OPTIC STRANDS STANDING IN THE AIR. THAT IS THE FAILURE THIS SECTION EXISTS TO KILL.】** 【【THERE ARE NO BEAMS, NO RAYS, NO SHAFTS, NO STREAKS, NO LINES, NO RODS, NO NEEDLES AND NO THREADS OF LIGHT ANYWHERE IN THIS FILM. NOTHING STRAIGHT. NOTHING WITH A LENGTH.】】

【【WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS】: 【the last warmth living inside the fine hairs starts to MOVE ALONG THEM — a faint brightness travelling slowly up the inside of a hair toward its tip, the way heat creeps along a filament — 【gathering at the very tip for a moment】 — and then 【LETTING GO: it comes free as a small soft POINT of light, no bigger than a grain, and floats.】】 【The travelling glow is INSIDE the hair, never a line in the air; the moment it leaves the hair it is a POINT, never a streak.】】

【【AND IT HAPPENS ALL OVER HER, OUT OF STEP】: 【dozens of hairs doing it, one after another and never together — the brightness creeping up one, releasing, while three others are only starting and one has already gone.】 【The freed points drift slowly upward and sideways in the haze, wandering, uneven, some barely moving.】】

【【AND EVERY HAIR IT LEAVES GOES DARK BEHIND IT】: 【the coat greying strand by strand, the warmth emptying out of the frame hair by hair.】】

【SLOW, UNEVEN, CONTINUOUS across these three seconds. 【Never a burst, never a wave, never a puff, never a shower.】】】

【— 【8.00–9.50 — AND THEY ALL BECOME ASH】: 【as each floating point drifts it COOLS: it dulls from warm to orange to a dull red pinpoint — and then 【EACH ONE BECOMES A SMALL GREY FLAKE OF ASH】: matte, irregular, frayed-edged, like a curl of burnt paper.】 【THE WHOLE FRAME TURNS OVER AT ONCE — an image of drifting light becomes an image of falling ash: the flakes lose their lift, hang, tip over, and tumble slowly downward through the haze, dark against dark.】 【No sparks, no glitter, no fairy dust, no fibre-optic look, no magical dissolve. It is matter, and it falls.】】

【— 【9.50–12.00 — AND THE CAMERA PICKS ONE】: 【ONE last point of light is still lit, and it detaches from 【THE TIP OF A SINGLE HAIR OF HER EYEBROW】 — the brow ridge above the open eye — 【and that hair goes dark as it leaves.】 【NOT off the coat, NOT off the muzzle, NOT out of the eye: off the EYEBROW.】】 【The camera CHOOSES IT and 【DRIFTS UPWARD WITH IT IN THE SAME UNBROKEN MOVE】 — slowly, unsteadily, the same fallible hand struggling to keep one tiny thing inside a millimetre-thin plane of focus.】 【HER FACE SLIDES OUT OF FRAME BELOW AND IS GONE — from here there is no eye, no coat, no animal, no floor, no room: only that one point, thick lit haze, out-of-focus ash falling around it, and enormous soft darkness.】】

【【FULL MACRO ON THAT ONE PARTICLE】: 【it is not a dot — it has a shape: an irregular warm grain with a fraying corona, its light unsteady, breathing brighter and dimmer as it turns.】 【The focus keeps losing it: it swells into a huge soft warm disc when it drifts off the plane, then contracts back into a hard little point when the hand finds it again — 【IT BREATHES BETWEEN BOKEH AND SHARPNESS ALL THE WAY UP.】】 【The other flakes drift past it, huge and out of focus, and are ignored.】】

【【SURREAL AND POETIC — THE ONE PLACE IN THE FILM WHERE BEAUTY IS ALLOWED】: 【the haze glows around it, the darkness goes soft and endless, all scale and place disappear — it could be an ember, or something enormous very far away.】 【It rises unhurried, drifting sideways, turning slightly. NO trail, NO streak, NO sparkle, NO swirl: one dim warm irregular grain of light, alone.】】

【【AND IT DOES NOT VANISH — IT BURNS OUT AND BECOMES ASH LIKE ALL THE OTHERS】: 【the warm point contracts and drops through the colours of something dying — pale warm, to orange, to a dull red pinpoint, to nothing — and what is left exactly where it was is 【A FLAKE OF ASH】: a small matte grey-black scrap with a soft frayed edge. 【One edge of it still glows faint red for a moment, and then that goes too.】】 【Then it gains weight: it stops rising, hangs, tips over, and TUMBLES SLOWLY DOWNWARD, turning on itself, drifting sideways, dark against dark — the focus losing it and half-finding it as it falls.】】

**【【AND THEN THE LIGHT IS COMPLETELY GONE — THIS IS HOW THE FILM ENDS】】**

【【THE LAST SECOND HAS NO LIGHT IN IT AT ALL.】 【After the flake forms, its last faint red edge goes out and 【THE FRAME CONTAINS NOTHING WARM ANYWHERE — not a spark, not a glimmer, not a distant glow, not a leftover ember at an edge, not one lit particle.】】 【The flake itself is now completely dark, and it tumbles down and drifts out of the frame.】 【What is left is bare grey haze and drifting dust in near-darkness: 【AN IMAGE WITH ZERO WARMTH IN IT.】】 【HOLD ON THAT EMPTY DARK FRAME A BEAT TOO LONG】 — still unsteady, still hunting focus on nothing. Then black.】

End state: an empty dark frame of grey haze and dust, 【every trace of light gone】, the ash drifted out, the camera still drifting. Cut to black.

【UNDEREXPOSED — near-black shadows, cold near-colourless palette except her failing warm ember-light. 35mm anamorphic, wide open, fine grain. 【FINCHER: surgical, coiled — tension from stillness, proximity and time.】 【【THE AIR — HEAVY, IN EVERY FRAME, INCLUDING THE MACRO ONES】: 【THICK HAZE, MORE THAN FEELS RIGHT — a dense smoke-haze between the camera and everything, a soft grey veil across every close-up; if a frame looks clear, ADD MORE HAZE】; 【fine DUST drifting across every frame】; 【a few tiny dim embers adrift, sparse and occasional, catching and going out — never a shower, never glitter.】 【No frame is clean air. Not one.】】】

**【THE ACTING LAW — THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS FILE】**

【【BOTH OF THEM ARE UNDERPLAYING TO THE POINT OF ALMOST NOTHING.】 【In the last version both reactions came out too big. The correction is not "a bit smaller" — it is 【FAR SMALLER THAN FEELS LIKE ENOUGH】.】】

【【THE RULES】: 【ONE small involuntary thing at a time, with long stillness around it.】 【No expression is ever pushed, held, shaped or presented to camera. Neither face ever CHANGES SHAPE.】 【Everything happens behind the skin and almost nothing on it.】 【RAW AND CRUDE, NOT BEAUTIFUL: what little happens is ugly, involuntary and unflattering — a body doing something it did not choose — never a composed emotional expression.】 【If a moment reads as acting, it is too big. If it reads as something the camera happened to catch, it is right.】 【The camera's own shake will read as life; the faces do not need to supply it.】】

FAIL: EITHER REACTION IS BIG, SHAPED OR EXPRESSIVE = SHOT FAILED — almost nothing, one involuntary thing at a time, the faces never changing shape. FAIL: any frame is wide, or reads as a shot of a room or of a person = SHOT FAILED — too close, at or near macro, all three shots. FAIL: the camera is stabilised, smooth, floating or locked = SHOT FAILED — a real unsupported hand, drifting, jittering, correcting, losing and refinding the subject. FAIL: deep focus = SHOT FAILED — millimetres, drifting with the camera. FAIL: iris, pupil, amber or glow in HER eyes = SHOT FAILED — solid black, edge to edge, with only a faint wet black shine. FAIL: clean empty air, or any frame without heavy haze and drifting dust = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: any object enters any frame = SHOT FAILED — the only thing that ever enters is his own empty right hand, once, in Shot 2. FAIL: the turning point is shown = SHOT FAILED — it happens in the cut and is never on screen. FAIL: the earbud absent, in the left ear, in both, or glowing = SHOT FAILED.

## MAINTAIN

Twenty seconds, three shots — 6.50 / 13.50. 【Everything in shot is a built set, a costume and a prop, photographed for the screen; both characters are invented. THE TURNING POINT HAPPENS IN THE CUT between Shot 1 and Shot 2 — nothing is ever performed on screen, and her sound stops dead ON the cut while Shot 2 opens in silence. THE CAMERA LAW: all three shots TOO CLOSE, at or near macro — no wide, no establishing, no room, no shoulders, nothing readable as a place; and the camera is a REAL UNSUPPORTED HAND — drifting, jittering, correcting, losing the subject by millimetres and finding it again, never stabilised, never smooth, never locked, and never an action-judder effect; at these distances every tiny movement is enormous, and razor-thin focus rides in and out as the frame moves. THE WAR DOCUMENTARY LAW CARRIES THE RAWNESS, NOT THE ACTING: shoot it like combat footage — the operator too close and without the shot, reframing late, lurching on his own weight, nothing ever composed, faces cut by the frame edge and sitting in the wrong part of it; the focus HUNTING, going soft, overshooting, landing late and sometimes on the wrong thing; the exposure pushed past safe with crushed grainy shadows; the front element dirty so haze and dust smear a low veiling flare whenever her ember hits it, and things drift across the lens in the extreme foreground; and BOTH SUBJECTS SIMPLY UNWASHED, NOT MADE UP AS DIRTY — a thin even film of settled pale dust and some sweat on his skin, her coat dust-dulled and matted where it is wet; NO heavy grime, NO black smears, NO caked mud, NO dirt painted into the creases. 【AND THE LIGHT BELONGS TO THE ROOM: the only sources are her weak dying ember, low and warm and off to one side from below, and the cold near-nothing ambient of the ruin — no key, no fill, no rim, no edge light, no backlight; the haze lifts the blacks so the image is FLAT AND MURKY rather than contrasty, the skin carries no bright highlights, the modelling is soft, and the wrecked library is always soft but PRESENT behind them — never a black void behind a face.】 The drama comes from proximity, duration and ugliness, and each shot is allowed ONE genuinely ugly moment held past comfort. THE ACTING LAW: both of them underplay to the point of almost nothing — FAR SMALLER THAN FEELS LIKE ENOUGH — one small involuntary thing at a time with long stillness around it, nothing pushed or shaped, neither face ever changing shape, raw and crude and unflattering rather than beautiful; if it reads as acting it is too big, and the camera's own shake supplies the life. THIS BLOCK IS MADE OF FACES, FIBRES AND LIGHT ONLY — nothing below the jaw, nothing held, no object in any frame, his hands out of shot except for the one brief moment in Shot 2 when his empty right hand comes up to his eyes. **Subject.** Three things are in frame for all 12 seconds. He holds a newborn creature out in front of him in both hands, away from his body. Second, the dead adult creature: long, thin and grey, sitting up slumped back against the base of a bookcase, her legs splayed out in front of her across the fallen books and pointing toward Charlie, arms loose at her sides with her hands palm-down, her head tipped forward onto her chest. She is dead and completely motionless. She lies flat in the frame from this angle, her body about as long as he is tall, and he stands only one or two paces from her feet so that the two of them read as one small group in the middle of a wide floor. Third, high on the right side of frame, standing on the flat top edge of a tall bookcase, a small bird-shaped machine, 15 centimetres long — smaller than a human hand, the size of a small songbird, seen from above as a tiny dark mark on the shelf edge. **Environment.** The interior of a ruined library. Tall dark-wood bookcases still packed with books, heavy square columns, and a stone floor buried under hundreds of fallen books lying splayed open and stacked in drifts, mixed with broken plaster, masonry and grey dust. Both bodies are on top of the books. Spreading from beneath the dead creature's hips is a shallow pool of deep amber-gold translucent liquid, like dark honey lit from within, two metres across, soaking into the paper at its edges and steaming faintly. STANDING LAWS — IN FORCE OVER EVERY FRAME OF THIS PIECE.
No music of any kind, ever — no score, no drone, no swell, no sting, no riser, no pad, no hum used as music. Silence under everything.

THE ACTING LAW. Human and subtle, which does not mean blank or motionless. Emotion leaks in millimetres, through the mouth, the nose, the eyes, the hands and the arms — one gesture at a time with stillness between, never several at once, never a performance. Restrained, coiled, Fincher: the tension comes from stillness, proximity and time.
THE CREATURE ACTING LAW. The newborn is ANIMAL, not human: mostly inert, finely trembling, broken only by sudden scheduled involuntary moves. It moves LESS than feels right.
ALL CREATURE EYES ARE SOLID BLACK, edge to edge — no iris, no pupil, no sclera, no catchlight, no amber, no glow, no sparks.

THE CONTINUITY LAW. The two shots are the same instant of the same scene, seconds apart. ## 【THE GLOW — HOW TO BUILD IT SO IT CANNOT GO WRONG】

**【THE GLOW IS NOT AN OBJECT. IT IS NOT A DOT, A BULB, AN ORB, A BALL, A SPHERE, A LANTERN, A FLAME OR A POINT OF LIGHT. IT IS NOT IN THE AIR. IT DOES NOT FLY.】**

**【THE GLOW IS THIS, EXACTLY: WARM LIGHT FALLING ON THE SIDES OF BOOKCASES, FROM A SOURCE THAT IS ALWAYS HIDDEN BEHIND THEM.】**

【Think of 【a strong warm lamp burning in the next aisle of a dark library】. 【You cannot see the lamp — the shelving is in the way. What you CAN see is what its light does:】】

【— 【a bright warm rim down the vertical edge of a bookcase】, where the light just clears the wood;】

【— 【warm light washed across the end boards and the spines of the nearest books】, falling off fast;】

【— 【a wedge of warm light thrown across the rubble on the floor of the alley】, with 【a hard shadow edge where the bookcase blocks it】;】

【— 【the dust in the air above that alley turning gold.】】

**【EVERY WARM PIXEL IN THIS SHOT IS ON A SURFACE — wood, paper, stone — OR IN HANGING DUST. THERE IS NEVER A BRIGHT SHAPE WITH EMPTY BLACK BEHIND IT.】**

**【THE TEST, EVERY FRAME: point at the brightest thing in the frame. IT MUST BE A LIT SURFACE — a plank, a spine, a stone. IF IT IS A SHAPE FLOATING IN SPACE, THE SHOT HAS FAILED.】**

**【AND THE SOURCE IS NEVER SEEN. NOT ONCE. NOT PARTIALLY. NOT BLURRED. NOT FOR ONE FRAME.】** 【The sight never gets an angle past the shelving. 【Whatever is back there stays back there for all twenty seconds — before the shots, during them, and after.】】

FAIL: a glowing dot, orb, ball, bulb, sphere, flame, lantern or point of light appears anywhere = SHOT FAILED — 【this is THE recurring error; do not make it again.】 FAIL: the source of the warm light is visible, even partially, even blurred = SHOT FAILED — 【only its light is ever seen.】 FAIL: any bright shape floats, hovers, flies or drifts = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: there is no hard shadow edge where the shelving blocks the light = wrong, the occlusion must be readable.

THIS IS AN INSERT INSIDE <<<image_1>>>'s SHOT AND MUST CUT INVISIBLY WITH IT: same ground of pale broken concrete, grey grit and BENT RUSTED REBAR STANDING UP OUT OF THE RUBBLE; same DIM, COOL, SOFT light from above and ahead with the OFF-WHITE PLATING AS THE BRIGHTEST THING IN FRAME and everything else falling fast to near-black — NO hard raking beam, NO warm or golden tone; same cold near-monochrome palette; same suspended dust; same camera height ON THE GROUND looking ACROSS the debris. EXTREME CLOSE-UP: the camera inches away and THE BOOT FILLS THE FRAME — nothing above mid-calf, no knee, no body, no face. IT IS HIS LEFT FOOT THAT TAKES THE STEP and the left boot is the subject throughout; the right boot stays planted, bearing his weight, and is never more than a soft dark shape at the frame edge. 35mm ANAMORPHIC wide open with oval bokeh, horizontal streaking and edge distortion, PAPER-THIN focus on the boot, achieved by physical proximity and NEVER by a long lens. The boot and ankle exactly per <<<image_2>>> and matching <<<image_1>>>'s colour — off-white plating with darker joints, dirty, scuffed, scored, dark grit in every crevice, fine dark speckling on the pale panels. THE DEBRIS IS BIG AND IT DOMINATES THE FRAME — slabs the size of his boot and much larger, thick fractured plates lying at angles across one another, propped and bridging and UNSTABLE, with grit, stone and rusted rebar between them. This is a collapsed building, NOT gravel and NOT a dusty floor. HE TAKES ONE SINGLE STEP AND IT TAKES ALMOST THE WHOLE SIX SECONDS — the boot lifts heel-first with grit falling from the tread, travels forward and HANGS over a tilted slab and a finger of rebar, PAUSES to choose, then lowers TOE FIRST and PRESSES to test, and the slab holds. THEN AT 5.00 HIS FULL WEIGHT GOES ON AND THE GROUND GIVES: THE SLAB TIPS AND DROPS, GRINDING HARD against the concrete beneath it, KNOCKS against the piece it was propped on, and A RUN OF LOOSE STONE BREAKS AWAY AND SLIDES DOWN THE PILE, still rattling after the boot has stopped, with a heavy cloud of pale dust bursting up around it. 【THIS IS LOUD. He was careful and it was loud anyway — the noise is heavy and substantial, real weight on unstable masonry, never a delicate crunch or a light scuff.】 A fine tremor runs through the ankle bearing weight. HE DOES NOT REACT — the shot ends on the debris still settling. The rifle does not appear. No music, no score, no dialogue, no creature sound.

HOW THE COLOUR WORKS — THIS IS IMPORTANT. NOT A LINEAR GRADIENT. Do NOT ramp one colour into another along a single axis. Instead the colours have SEVERAL SEPARATE CENTRES scattered at different points on her body, each blooming outward and bleeding irregularly into its neighbours. The distribution is UNEVEN, PATCHY and ASYMMETRIC — the left side does not match the right. Colour POOLS in some places and DRAINS from others, collecting in hollows and creases, thinning over bone. Boundaries are soft, ragged and irregular, never straight, never even. Adjacent fibres can carry different colours and single strands can change hue along their length. IT SHOULD LOOK GROWN, NOT DESIGNED — like lichen, patina, mould or animal markings.

## 【THE GLOW — HOW TO BUILD IT SO IT CANNOT GO WRONG】

**【THE GLOW IS NOT AN OBJECT. IT IS NOT A DOT, A BULB, AN ORB, A BALL, A SPHERE, A LANTERN, A FLAME OR A POINT OF LIGHT. IT IS NOT IN THE AIR. IT DOES NOT FLY.】**

**【THE GLOW IS THIS, EXACTLY: WARM LIGHT FALLING ON THE SIDES OF BOOKCASES, FROM A SOURCE THAT IS ALWAYS HIDDEN BEHIND THEM.】**

【Think of 【a strong warm lamp burning in the next aisle of a dark library】. 【You cannot see the lamp — the shelving is in the way. What you CAN see is what its light does:】】

【— 【a bright warm rim down the vertical edge of a bookcase】, where the light just clears the wood;】

【— 【warm light washed across the end boards and the spines of the nearest books】, falling off fast;】

【— 【a wedge of warm light thrown across the rubble on the floor of the alley】, with 【a hard shadow edge where the bookcase blocks it】;】

【— 【the dust in the air above that alley turning gold.】】

**【EVERY WARM PIXEL IN THIS SHOT IS ON A SURFACE — wood, paper, stone — OR IN HANGING DUST. THERE IS NEVER A BRIGHT SHAPE WITH EMPTY BLACK BEHIND IT.】**

**【AND THE SOURCE IS NEVER SEEN. NOT ONCE. NOT PARTIALLY. NOT BLURRED. NOT FOR ONE FRAME.】** 【The sight never gets an angle past the shelving. 【Whatever is back there stays back there for all fifteen seconds — before the shots, during them, and after.】】

## 【WHAT THIS IS】

**An enormous early-twentieth-century opera theatre that was converted into a bookshop, and then abandoned and wrecked.** The building is intact enough to read as what it was; everything inside it has failed.

## 【THE BUILDING — REPRODUCE THIS ARCHITECTURE EXACTLY】

**A converted Beaux-Arts theatre auditorium, elliptical in plan, seen from high up on one of the balcony tiers looking down and across the room.**

【THREE TIERS OF CURVED BALCONIES sweep around the room in a horseshoe, one above the other, each with an ornate moulded balustrade and a continuous run of theatre boxes behind it. The tiers are separated by heavily decorated plaster friezes.】

【THE ORNAMENT IS EXTRAVAGANT AND EVERYWHERE: gilded Beaux-Arts plasterwork, garlands, cartouches, scrolled brackets, rosettes, fluted pilasters and sculpted figures flanking the boxes. Deep coffered mouldings under each balcony.】

【A GREAT PAINTED DOME spans the ceiling high above the centre of the room — an allegorical fresco of figures and sky ringed by a moulded border.】

【AT ONE END, THE ORIGINAL STAGE SURVIVES BEHIND A TALL PROSCENIUM ARCH, with the remains of heavy stage curtains hanging in it.】

【THE FLOOR OF THE ROOM IS THE OLD STALLS — a wide flat elliptical floor at the bottom of the room, well below the first balcony, reached by stairs. IT IS A PIT.】

【BOOKSHELVES ARE BUILT INTO EVERYTHING: floor-to-ceiling ranks against every curved wall on every tier, packed into the theatre boxes, lining the backs of the balconies, and standing in long parallel ranks across the stalls floor below.】

【A DEAD ESCALATOR runs down into the stalls floor near the centre of the room, a later addition that never belonged there.】

【THE GILDING IS BLACKENED, DULLED AND FLAKING. The plasterwork is chipped, cracked and broken away in chunks; whole sections of cornice have fallen. Bare brick, lath and rusted reinforcing bar show through the wounds.】

【THE SHELVING IS DESTROYED. Ranks toppled against one another like dominoes, some still standing and full, others emptied and split. BOOKS ARE EVERYWHERE — spilled in drifts across the stalls floor, banked up against the walls, swollen, warped, water-damaged, half-buried in pale concrete dust.】

【THE FINAL STRETCH BELONGS ENTIRELY TO HIS EYES, IN EXTREME CLOSE-UP — his eyes and the skin immediately around them filling the frame, the rest of his face at the edges, the room gone.】

**HIS LOOK IS FULL OF FEAR, AND HE IS LOOKING AROUND THE PLACE.** 【THE EYES MOVE — travelling out to one edge of the black, back across, out to the other, searching the room he cannot see into, coming back and going out again. THE FEAR IS IN THEM THE WHOLE TIME AND IT DEEPENS AS THEY FIND NOTHING.】

【HE IS AFRAID AND IT SHOWS ONLY IN THE EYES. The rest of his face does not join in.】 It does not arrive as a jump or a widening — it is already surfacing as the camera lands and it rises through the final seconds. 【WRITE THE FEAR AS ONE THING, NOT AS A LIST OF SYMPTOMS. It lives in the eyes and in the quality of the held breath behind them. The mouth does not shape it, the brow does not announce it, nothing else performs it.】

**HE GIVES AWAY NOTHING BELOW THE EYES.** His head and body carry on holding the position they were already in — 【THE HEAD POSITION RUNS UNBROKEN FROM BEFORE THE LINE THROUGH TO THE FINAL FRAME.】 He does not turn, does not step, does not shift his weight, does not square up to anything, and he never reaches for anything.

【HE IS NOT FROZEN AND MUST NEVER LOOK IT — alive throughout with the involuntary motion of a real body: quiet shallow held breath, irregular blinking, tiny saccades. Stillness carried by micro-motion, never by a mannequin.】

**NOTHING RESOLVES.** He does not speak again, does not turn, does not reach for anything, does not move off. The frame stays on his eyes until it cuts.

## PERFORMANCE LAW

【UNDERPLAYED — THE MOST IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION HERE. The feeling stays under the surface and mostly does not reach the face. Reactions small, late and incomplete. Nobody demonstrates or signals. If a moment could be played big or small, play it small.】

【UNDERPLAYED IS NOT BLANK. Inner life runs continuously; thought moves behind the eyes. Restrained is the SIZE of the expression, not its absence.】

**GESTURE RULE.** The hand movements at the earbud are small, complete and mechanically plain — a hand comes from somewhere, does one thing, and stops. Nothing floats, nothing gestures, nothing is performed for the camera.

**PHYSICAL TEXTURE — PHOTOGRAPHY, NOT ACTING.** Quiet continuous breath, irregular blinking, small eye saccades, weight and fabric shifting under the armour. Photographic skin: pores, fine lines, uneven specular, dust in the creases, warm subsurface in the ears. Real human performance capture, not animation. Not waxy, no CG doll skin, no frozen mannequin.

FAIL: he cries, screams, mugs or performs agony = wrong, the pain is physical and specific, never theatrical. FAIL: a heroic or determined face at any point = wrong. FAIL: any frame where he reads as motionless or robotic = wrong.

**HIS FACE — BEFORE THE CHANGE.** Wet blood from the nose over the lip and chin. Fine scratches on the cheek, temple, jaw and shaved scalp. Dust and grit caked thick over everything, ground into the skin, cut through by wet channels. Eyes bloodshot.

**HIS FACE — AFTER THE CHANGE.** Identical in every respect except one: the blood is gone, with no residue. Only the fine scratches, the dust and the dirt — subtle, dry and realistic. Same dust pattern, same scratches, same bloodshot eyes, same lighting.

## MAINTAIN CONSISTENCY

# NANO BANANA — REPLACE THE TOWER SIGNAGE — NO BRAND RESEMBLANCE
<<<image_1>>> — THE PLATE, AND THE SOLE EDITING MASTER. The flooded ruined street: overgrown concrete buildings left and right, the derelict delivery van at lower left with its faded smiling sun and burger painted on the side, standing water and grass through the middle, smoke and a vapour trail in the pale overcast sky, and at centre-right a tall ruined concrete tower carrying the remains of a large commercial sign — a broken curved yellow element at the top, a large red sign panel below it torn through with a hole, a second broken yellow element lower down, vines growing over all of it and rust-red bleed stains running down the concrete beneath.
【THIS EDIT REPLACES THE GRAPHICS ON THAT TOWER SIGN AND NOTHING ELSE.】
---
## WHAT MUST BE REMOVED — COMPLETELY
【EVERY CURVED YELLOW SIGN ELEMENT ON THE TOWER IS GONE. Both of them — the broken one at the top and the one lower down.】 Not recoloured, not partially covered by vine — structurally replaced.
【THE LARGE RED SIGN PANEL IS GONE as a red panel.】 Its physical box, frame and mounting stay; its colour and graphics do not.
## THE BRAND — AN INVENTED CORPORATE BURGER CHAIN
【THIS IS A DEAD FAST-FOOD CHAIN AND IT MUST READ INSTANTLY AS ONE — an obvious, satirical, faintly bleak parody of a global burger corporation. The joke should land in a second: a company that sold the same meal to the entire world, now rotting in a flooded street.】
**THE NAME ON THE SIGN IS: NAZA BURGERS**
【SET IN BOLD, BLOCKY, ALL-CAPITAL SANS-SERIF — plain, corporate, mid-century commercial signage lettering. Cream or off-white letters on the panel. NO script, NO swashes, NO logotype flourish, NO curved or looping letterforms.】
## THE HARD RULE — NO RESEMBLANCE TO ANY REAL BRAND
【THE SIGN MUST READ AS A FAST-FOOD CHAIN WITHOUT RESEMBLING ANY REAL ONE, PAST OR PRESENT. The parody is of the CATEGORY, never of a specific company.】
**SPECIFICALLY BANNED:**
FAIL: an arch, or any pair of arches, anywhere in the frame = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: any yellow or golden curved form, hoop, loop or crescent = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: the letter M in any stylised, curved, doubled or monogram form = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: a red-and-yellow colour pairing anywhere on the signage = wrong, that combination is banned outright. FAIL: any recognisable existing logo, wordmark, mascot, crown, jester, colonel, clown or trade dress of any kind = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: any real company name, or a near-miss variant of one, appearing anywhere = SHOT FAILED. FAIL: any text on the sign other than the invented name and the small strapline below = wrong.
## WHAT REPLACES IT
**THE TOP ELEMENT — A BROKEN ANGULAR MARK.** Where the curved yellow form was, mount the remains of the chain's logo mark: a simple hard-edged geometric shape in painted sheet metal on a steel frame — a **blunt multi-pointed star, or a segmented angular chevron**. 【STRAIGHT EDGES AND POINTS ONLY — NO CURVES, NO ARCS, NO LOOPS, NO HOOPS.】 Most of it is gone: snapped off down one side, a couple of points bent outward, the steel armature showing through where the panels have fallen away. Faded **cream and burnt orange**, heavily rust-streaked.
**THE MAIN PANEL — A DEEP FADED ORANGE BOX.** The same physical panel, same size, same position, same torn hole through it — but the face is now weathered **burnt orange / oxidised terracotta**, sun-bleached to uneven patches, the paint blistering and peeling back to bare grey metal in places.
**THE LETTERING — "NAZA BURGERS", STILL READABLE THROUGH THE RUIN.** Across the panel in large bold cream sans-serif capitals: **OMNIBURGER**. 【THE NAME MUST STAY LEGIBLE — the joke only works if it can be read — BUT IT IS BADLY DECAYED: the paint faded and streaked, one letter hanging loose and rotated off its fixings, another missing entirely and leaving only its ghost outline and screw-holes in the panel behind it.】 The torn hole in the panel eats into the word without destroying it.
**THE STRAPLINE.** Beneath the name, in much smaller cream capitals, half-eaten by rust and vine: **A WORLD OF FLAVOUR**. 【SMALL, SECONDARY, PARTIALLY ILLEGIBLE — a corporate promise outliving the world it promised.】
**THE LOWER ELEMENT.** Where the second curved yellow form was, leave only the bare bent steel mounting bracket and a stub of torn panel edge — whatever it carried is entirely gone.
FAIL: the name is unreadable = wrong, it must be legible enough to land. FAIL: the sign looks clean, intact, freshly painted or restored = wrong, it is a dead sign on a dead building. FAIL: a mascot, character, face, cartoon or figure appears anywhere on the sign = wrong, text and the angular mark only. FAIL: the lettering is script, rounded, bubbly or logotype-styled = wrong, it is plain blocky corporate sans-serif.
## PRESERVE EVERYTHING ELSE — EXACTLY
**THE TOWER ITSELF** — its exact silhouette, height, position, the broken concrete edges, the empty window openings, the collapsed floors, the exposed structure.
**THE VINES AND GREENERY** — every creeper, exactly where it is, including the growth hanging across the sign area. 【VINES PASS IN FRONT OF THE NEW SIGN EXACTLY AS THEY PASSED IN FRONT OF THE OLD ONE — same leaves, same positions, same overlap. The new graphics go BEHIND them.】
**THE RUST-RED BLEED STAINS** running down the concrete beneath the sign — identical in position, shape and colour. 【THEY STILL READ AS DECADES OF RUST BLEEDING OUT OF THE STEEL SIGN FRAME.】
**THE STEEL FRAME AND MOUNTINGS** — the exposed armature, brackets and fixings stay where they are; only the panels they carry change.
**EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE FRAME, UNTOUCHED:** the buildings left and right, the flooded street and standing water, the grass and trees, the concrete blocks in the water, the smoke and vapour trail, the sky, and 【THE DELIVERY VAN AT LOWER LEFT — its smiling sun and burger artwork stays exactly as it is, unchanged, since it resembles nothing in particular.】
**THE FRAMING** — identical crop, composition and aspect ratio.

FAIL: the van, the water, the buildings, the smoke or the sky change in any way = shot failed. FAIL: the crop changes = wrong.
## GRADE AND TEXTURE
【MATCH THE PLATE EXACTLY: cool, desaturated, misty, filmic, slightly flat overcast light with no cast shadows.】 The new signage sits in the same colour space and the same haze as everything at that distance — 【IT IS FAR AWAY AND SLIGHTLY ATMOSPHERIC, so it must NOT be sharper, cleaner, brighter or more saturated than the tower it is mounted on.】 Match the plate's film grain across the replaced area.
FAIL: the new sign is crisper or more vivid than its surroundings = wrong, it reads as pasted in. FAIL: it is lit differently from the rest of the tower = wrong, the light is flat overcast throughout.

## SUBJECT OF THE PAINTING

An old, dark, academic oil painting. A bullring at night. The arena floor is a wide sweep of pale sand, hot and bright, lit as if by a single high lamp. Everything above it is deep black, and out of that blackness the crowd emerges only as tiers of tiny pale faces, hundreds of them, small dabs of light curving away around the ring.

At the centre lies A BLACK BULL, collapsed, enormous, filling the lower middle of the canvas, one white-tipped horn catching the light, its head down on the sand. Banderillas stand out of its shoulders at angles, sticks wrapped in red and gold paper, a small red cape hanging from them.

Standing over it, small by comparison, A MATADOR in a gold-embroidered suit of lights and a white shirt, his head bowed, looking down at the animal. He is not triumphant. He is standing very still.

Beneath the bull, spreading across the pale sand, A POOL OF DEEP CRIMSON — the most saturated colour in these thirty seconds. A sword and a dark bundle of cloth lie nearby. In the lower right corner, a signature in red paint.

【IT IS A PAINTING — BRUSHWORK, CRAQUELURE, VARNISH AND CANVAS WEAVE VISIBLE AT CLOSE RANGE. IT NEVER BECOMES A PHOTOGRAPH, IT NEVER MOVES, IT NEVER ANIMATES】

FAIL TEST: IF ANYTHING INSIDE THE PAINTING MOVES, IT IS WRONG.

He climbs with the rifle in both hands, muzzle LOW, ready but not shouldered. It stays low through the whole painting passage — he is not covering a room, he is looking at a picture. It comes UP into his shoulder only in the last two seconds, fast and instinctive.

NO DIALOGUE. No voice, no whisper, no muttering, no breathed words, no voiceover, no narration. HE NEVER SPEAKS.

## FORMAT LAW — 35MM ANAMORPHIC

Shot on 35mm anamorphic. This is an OPTICAL description, not a delivery format. Oval, vertically stretched bokeh in every out-of-focus highlight. Horizontal smear on any bright point. Barrel distortion and horizontal stretch increasing toward the edges of frame. Fast, soft focus falloff. Visible lens breathing on any focus change. Corners noticeably softer than centre. Fine 35mm grain, present in the shadows, never buzzing.

【ANAMORPHIC IS THE LENS, NOT THE CROP — SEE FRAME LAW】

## FRAME LAW

FULL FRAME. Edge to edge. No letterbox, no black bars top or bottom, no cinema-scope matte drawn into the picture, no border of any kind. The image fills the entire frame. FAIL TEST: IF THERE IS A BLACK BAR ANYWHERE, IT IS WRONG.

## STATIC LAW — THE CAMERA IS ON STICKS AND IT DOES NOT MOVE

THE CAMERA IS LOCKED OFF. In fragments one, two, three, four and six the camera is on a heavy tripod and it is DEAD STILL. No handheld. No breathing. No micro-drift. No push in. No pull out. No dolly. No gimbal float. No orbit. No shake. No reframing to follow him. HE MOVES INSIDE A FIXED FRAME AND SOMETIMES HE LEAVES IT.

【THERE IS EXACTLY ONE CAMERA MOVE IN THIS ENTIRE THIRTY SECONDS AND IT IS IN FRAGMENT FIVE】

The single permitted move: in FRAGMENT FIVE the camera tilts UP, slowly and smoothly, from the blood on the floor to the stair. That is a TILT ON A LOCKED HEAD — the camera body does not travel through space, it only pivots upward. Slow enough that a viewer would call it patient. FAIL TEST: IF THE CAMERA MOVES IN ANY FRAGMENT OTHER THAN FIVE, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF FRAGMENT FIVE'S MOVE TRAVELS FORWARD OR SIDEWAYS INSTEAD OF PIVOTING UP, IT IS WRONG.

## CUT LAW

FIVE HARD CUTS. Six fragments. Straight cuts on the exact timecodes below — no dissolve, no fade, no whip, no morph, no match-cut trickery, no speed ramp. The camera position changes ONLY at a cut.

## LIGHT LAW — CLAROSCURO

The only light in this building comes through windows. Tall, hard, directional shafts of pale daylight falling into a room that is otherwise deeply, honestly dark. Enormous dynamic range: the lit stone is bright enough to bloom slightly, and two metres away the shadow is near black with nothing recoverable in it. Dust hanging in every shaft, drifting slowly, catching the light.

MOST OF THE FRAME IS DARK. He is often half in shadow with one side of his face carved out by window light and the other side gone entirely. Blacks are dense and neutral. Nothing is lifted. Nothing is filled. No practical lamps, no fire, no lens flare, no artificial source, no coloured light.

【THE CAMERA DOES NOT COMPENSATE — NO AUTO-EXPOSURE LIFT, NO IRIS OPENING UP, NO BRIGHTENING OF THE SHADOWS】

FAIL TEST: IF THE INTERIOR IS EVENLY LIT AND READABLE EVERYWHERE, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF HE IS SO DARK YOU CANNOT TELL WHERE HE IS LOOKING, IT IS TOO FAR THE OTHER WAY.

## DEPTH LAW

Shallow. Wide open. In every fragment ONE thing is sharp and everything else falls away fast into oval anamorphic blur. Focus is a decision, not an accident — the sharp thing is stated in each fragment below and nothing else in that frame is sharp.

## COLOUR LAW

The world is colourless and only two things are not. Desaturated to the edge of monochrome: pale grey stone, bone-white plaster, brown-grey dead leaves, cold blue-grey window light. The two exceptions are the muted brick-red panels of his exosuit and, in fragments five and six, the blood. No greens pushed, no warm golden hour, no teal-and-orange, no colour grade that looks like a filter.

## SILENCE LAW — PACE

This is slow. This is heavy. Nobody rushes. He moves like a man who does not want to be heard. Long held frames, long held stillness, and inside that stillness the small precise movements of a person listening. NOT a music video. NOT a montage. Every fragment holds long enough to feel uncomfortable.

## PERFORMANCE LAW

Contained. Almost nothing on the face and everything underneath it. No wide eyes, no gasp, no mouth hanging open, no theatrical fear, no head-shaking, no hand to the mouth. He is a professional in a bad place. The reaction is in the jaw, the breath, the stillness before he moves. FAIL TEST: IF HE ACTS SCARED, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF HE LOOKS BORED OR BLANK, IT IS ALSO WRONG.

## DIRT LAW

His face is filthy — dried mud, dust, sweat lines through the grime, damp hair stuck to his forehead. The exosuit is coated. He has just come out of the field and it shows in every frame. He does not clean himself here.

## CLOCK LAW — THE CLOCK IS DEAD

The clock does not work. Its hands are FROZEN and they stay frozen for the whole shot. They do not advance a single degree. There is no tick, no tock, no pendulum, no second hand sweeping, no mechanism sound of any kind. Ivy has grown across its face and into the crack in the plaster around it. It is a stopped object on a dead wall. FAIL TEST: IF THE HANDS MOVE, EVEN SLIGHTLY, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF THERE IS TICKING IN THE SOUND, IT IS WRONG.

## BLOOD LAW

The blood is OLD and it is a TRACE, not an event. A dark, dried, near-black smear on pale stone — one wide streak where something was dragged, breaking into scattered drops. Matte, tacky, partly soaked into the porous stone, dulled at the edges. Dead leaves stuck in it. NO body. NO wound. NO injured person. NO fresh liquid pooling. NO gore. It is a mark on a floor, and its only job is to point at the stair.

【IT IS EVIDENCE, NOT AN INJURY】

## BRD-1 LAW

BRD-1 is a small mechanical bird, machined and worn. It perches on his LEFT shoulder plate, gripping the armour. IT IS VISIBLE IN FRAGMENT THREE AND IN NO OTHER FRAGMENT. In fragment three it launches off his shoulder and flies past the camera, and AFTER THAT IT IS GONE — it does not come back, it does not land on him again, it does not appear in the background, it is not heard again. It never becomes a real bird, never grows feathers, never softens.

【AFTER IT PASSES THE CAMERA IN FRAGMENT THREE, HE IS ALONE】

FAIL TEST: IF BRD-1 IS ANYWHERE IN FRAGMENTS FOUR, FIVE OR SIX, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF IT LOOKS ORGANIC, IT IS WRONG.

## LEAF LAW

Dead brown leaves are everywhere inside this building — drifted against the walls, scattered across the floor, sitting on every single tread of the stair. They are dry. When he steps, a few shift. Nothing swirls dramatically, there is no wind indoors.

# FRAGMENT ONE — 0.00 to 4.20 — HE COMES THROUGH THE DOOR

CLOSE-UP. Locked off. The camera is INSIDE, low and close, waiting just past the threshold of the small dark doorway from <<<image_5>>>. Behind him, through the doorway, blown-out white daylight — the exterior is three or four stops overexposed and reads as pure glare.

He steps through into the dark. His face fills a good third of the frame, chin toward the bottom third, the top of his head near the top edge. He is a black silhouette for the first half second and then, as he clears the doorway, the interior window light finds the side of his face and CARVES it — one cheek, one eye, the ridge of his nose lit, the other half of his head gone into black. Rifle up across his chest, both hands on it, muzzle low.

SHARP: his eye. Everything else — the doorway behind, the glare, his own shoulder — is soft.

He does not stop walking. He passes the camera and leaves frame at the very end, and for the last quarter second the frame is just the blown-out doorway and the drifting dust.

# FRAGMENT TWO — 4.20 to 9.60 — FROM THE CLOCK

HARD CUT. GENERAL SHOT. The camera is WHERE THE CLOCK IS — high on the wall of the stair hall, <<<image_8>>>'s position, looking down and across the whole room. Wide. The full architecture of <<<image_6>>> visible: the stone stair rising at the back, the balustrades, the drifted leaves, the tall windows throwing hard slabs of light across the floor.

【THE CLOCK IS THE CAMERA, NOT THE SUBJECT — WE DO NOT SEE THE CLOCK IN THIS FRAGMENT】

CHARLIE IS OUT OF FOCUS. This is the whole point of the shot. Focus is planted on the ARCHITECTURE — the near edge of the balustrade, the cracked plaster, the leaves in the light — and he walks through the room as a SOFT, BLURRED, UNRESOLVED SHAPE. His brick-red panels smear into oval bokeh. His face is unreadable. He never comes into focus, not for a single frame, and the camera does NOT rack to him.

FAIL TEST: IF CHARLIE IS EVER SHARP IN THIS FRAGMENT, IT IS WRONG.

He enters small at the left, crosses the room slowly through a shaft of window light — bright for a moment, then swallowed by shadow, then bright again — and stops near the centre, facing the stair. Dust turns in the light he disturbs.

# FRAGMENT THREE — 9.60 to 14.60 — FROM ABOVE, AND THE BIRD

HARD CUT. Camera on the SECOND FLOOR, on the landing above, locked off, looking DOWN over the balustrade into the hall — a steep high angle, the geometry of <<<image_6>>> reading as symmetry beneath us.

Far below and small, CHARLIE stands in the doorway of <<<image_5>>>, framed by it, a shaft of daylight behind him. He is STILL. He is looking up and around the room, taking the place in. BRD-1 is perched on his LEFT shoulder plate.

SHARP: Charlie and the doorway. The near balustrade in the foreground is a soft dark mass across the bottom of frame.

At roughly 12.60 BRD-1 DROPS off his shoulder and FLIES — straight up toward us, fast and direct, growing enormous in the last third of a second, and PASSES THE CAMERA, out of frame at the top. It does not curve, it does not circle, it does not hover. It goes past us and it is gone. The camera does not follow it. The camera does not flinch. We hold on Charlie below for a beat after it has left.

# FRAGMENT FOUR — 14.60 to 18.60 — HIS FACE

HARD CUT. CLOSE-UP, FRONTAL, locked off. Eye level. He is centred, head roughly filling the middle of the frame — top of the skull a seventh down from the top edge, chin a little past halfway. Behind him the hall falls away into deep unreadable blur, one hard window shaft breaking the darkness over his shoulder as an oval smear.

Hard side light. One half of his face lit and textured — every grain of dirt, every bead of sweat, the cracked lip, the damp hair. The other half in black.

SHARP: his eyes.

He is reading the room. Small movements of the eyes, not the head. He breathes once, out, through the nose. Then — slowly, deliberately — HE TURNS HIS HEAD DOWN, chin dropping, eyes going to the floor, as if something on the ground has just registered. He holds there, looking down, and we cut.

# FRAGMENT FIVE — 18.60 to 24.80 — THE BLOOD, AND THE TILT

HARD CUT. CLOSE-UP OF THE FLOOR. Locked off, angled down at the pale stone. Filling the frame: THE BLOOD — an old, dark, dried smear across the stone, near-black, matte, with scattered drops trailing off to one side and dead leaves stuck in the edge of it. A slab of window light cuts across one corner of the frame; the rest is shadow.

SHARP: the blood. Nothing else.

Hold on it, dead still, for about two and a half seconds. He is not in this shot.

Then THE CAMERA TILTS UP — slow, smooth, patient, a single continuous pivot on a locked head. It follows the trail of drops across the floor, to the foot of the stair, and up the flight from <<<image_7>>> — the pale stone steps, dead leaves on every tread, and the dark smear continuing UP, step after step, getting fainter, disappearing into the darkness at the top where the stair turns and the light does not reach.

Focus pulls with the tilt, so the stair resolves as the floor goes soft — visible lens breathing on the pull. The tilt ENDS on the dark top of the stair and holds there.

FAIL TEST: IF THE BLOOD DOES NOT VISIBLY CONTINUE UPWARD ONTO THE STEPS, THE SHOT HAS FAILED.

# FRAGMENT SIX — 24.80 to 30.00 — HE GOES UP

HARD CUT. Back to the close-up of FRAGMENT FOUR — same locked-off camera, same frontal framing, same lighting, matching exactly.

He is looking up now, off past the camera toward the stair. Jaw set. He has understood something and he does not like it. HE IS ALONE IN THIS FRAME — nothing on his shoulder, nothing in the air, nobody with him.

NOBODY SPEAKS. THERE IS NO DIALOGUE IN THIS SHOT AND NO VOICE OF ANY KIND. His mouth does not move.

Hold on him, dead still, for a long three seconds. His eyes stay on the stair. His jaw works once. He breathes out through the nose. Then he moves — he steps FORWARD and OUT of the bottom right of frame, toward the stair, alone. The camera does NOT follow. The last half second is the empty frame he has left behind: the dark hall, the shaft of window light, the dust still turning.

## MAINTAIN CONSISTENCY

Same man, same face, same filthy skin, same exosuit, same rifle in his hands throughout. HE DOES NOT SPEAK AND THERE IS NO DIALOGUE. 35mm anamorphic optics, full frame, no bars. CAMERA LOCKED OFF IN FIVE OF THE SIX FRAGMENTS — the only move in the whole thirty seconds is the slow upward tilt in fragment five. Window light only, hard and directional, deep black shadow, no fill, no lift. Shallow focus with one stated sharp subject per fragment, and CHARLIE NEVER IN FOCUS IN FRAGMENT TWO. The clock's hands never move and never make a sound. The blood is old, dried and near-black, a trace and not a wound, and it goes UP the stairs. BRD-1 is a machine, seen in fragment three only — it flies past the camera and never returns, and he finishes this thirty seconds alone. Slow, heavy, quiet. Five hard cuts, no dissolves. Nothing brightens, nothing swells, nothing hurries.

Monumental history painting of a bullring at the moment after the kill — three elements only. The black bull lies dead on its side in the raked sand, a dozen banderillas bristling upright from its shredded shoulders, ribbons soaked black-red and dripping, a sword buried to the hilt between the withers. Blood is everywhere on the animal: pouring in a thick unbroken rope from its open mouth, running from both nostrils, sheeting down the barrel of its body from every barb wound, matting the hide into wet clotted ridges, pooling in the folds of its neck. Beneath and around it a vast lake of blood has spread across the sand — metres wide, deep enough to hold a mirror reflection of the torero standing in it, its edge creeping outward in dark fingers where the sand drinks it, its centre still liquid and glossy, skinned over and rippling faintly, with long drag-streaks and hoof-scuffs printed through it. The torero stands alone at the edge of that pool, boots stained to the ankle, in his gold-embroidered traje de luces, montera in hand, turned toward the stands. Behind them the tiered ranks of the audience rise in their thousands behind the barrera, under a colonnaded gallery. Nothing else in the arena — no horses, no attendants, no mules, the sand beyond the blood completely empty.
Lit by one narrow shaft of hard light falling from high and far to the left, striking only the torero, the dead bull and the pool of blood, holding them in a tight island of illumination and nothing more. Inside that shaft the light is fierce and near-white — blazing on the gold bullion of the jacket until it burns out to pure lead white, raking across the wet black hide so it reads like oiled stone, and igniting the blood into a sheet of molten crimson that becomes the brightest colour in the painting, throwing warm red bounce up onto the man's jaw and hands from below. Outside it, everything collapses. The fall-off is violent, one hand's breadth from lit to unreadable: the sand goes bone white to umber to black within a metre of the pool's edge, the barrera is barely a suggestion, and the entire audience — all thousands of them — is swallowed into dense warm blackness, present only as the faintest scatter of pale smudges where a brow or a collar catches a stray photon, more felt than seen. The colonnaded gallery above is absolute black. Ninety percent of the canvas is shadow, transparent and glazed rather than flat, so the darkness has depth and heat in it. No fill light anywhere. No sky. Spotlight-hard, altar-like, the bodies and the blood burning out of an ocean of dark.
Zurbarán, Seville c.1640. The same darkness turned mystical and utterly silent. Everything stills: the torero stands motionless and frontal like a saint in a devotional panel, sculpturally simplified, the folds of his cape rendered with hard clean edges and a chalky matte white that seems lit from within. The blood pool is a single perfect black-crimson shape, almost geometric. Ascetic, hushed, no motion, no gesture, no crowd noise — the arena as chapel and the animal as offering. Reverent rather than gruesome.
Composed at grand-manner scale — three metres across, figures near life-size, deep recession into darkness, a governing diagonal running from the carcass up to the invisible gallery. Oil on linen, generations of ambered varnish, fine age craquelure across the darks, faint stretcher-bar lines. Photographed straight-on in a museum gallery, heavy carved and gilded frame at the edges, the surface reading as enormous.

He pushes to rise — his hand slipping once before it catches, an uneven straining effort, his rifle barely suggested at the edge of the shaft, his earbud still seated, his watch visible on his wrist — and this time he makes it, painfully, up onto his knees only, not his feet, and does not fall again. He never speaks.

Subject. A newborn creature lying in a pair of cupped gloved hands. The newborn exactly as designed in <<<image_6>>>, at exactly the scale given in <<<image_7>>> — <<<image_7>>> is the sole authority on its size and it is SMALL, filling only the two cupped palms.

ITS TINY HAND IS TOUCHING HIS FINGER. One of the newborn's small wet hands rests against the bare uncovered fingerpad of Charlie's forefinger — the minute fingers laid over the skin, curled loosely around the edge of it, slick and shining where the two surfaces meet. This contact is the emotional centre of the frame and must be clearly readable: the enormous scuffed armoured finger, the tiny soaked hand on it. The hand does not grip hard, does not wave, does not reach — it simply rests there, trembling faintly, tightening once by a millimetre and easing.

It is SOAKED — but the wetness is FINE-GRAINED, scaled to a tiny body. A thin, tight, unbroken film of clear birth fluid sheeting over every millimetre of it, glossy and continuous, following the form rather than sitting on it. Its thin coat is plastered flat into soaked hair-thin strings and whorls, matted tight against the skin. A translucent membrane clings in a thin sheet along its back and one hind limb. The droplets are TINY — a fine scatter of pinhead beads, barely more than a mist, gathered along the edges of the coat and in the creases of the glove; where fluid runs it runs as hair-thin threads, not streams. Nothing pools. No fat drops, no thick strands, no heavy hanging beads, no globs — every droplet at the scale of water on a small animal, not on a human hand. The whole surface is slick and streaming-wet at a MINIATURE scale, alive with countless small specular highlights that shift as it breathes.

Its head is FACED DOWN — the skull tipped forward and hanging heavy toward the palm, the face angled down and away from camera, never lifted, never raised, never turned toward the lens. We read the wet crown of the skull, the soaked nape, the curve of the spine — not the face, not the eyes. If any sliver of eye is glimpsed it is solid black, edge to edge, no iris, no pupil, no catchlight, no glow.

In its chest sits a single golden ember, and it burns BRIGHT — a hot dense golden core, the only light in existence in this frame. Its light soaks through the wet coat and the thin translucent skin so the whole small body glows from inside, the ribs reading as dark bars against the burn. The fluid film carries and smears that gold across every slick surface; the hair-thin wet strings of the coat are lit through; the tiny beads along its edges read as a scatter of minute gold points; the little hand on his finger is lit through from behind, its fingers translucent gold at their edges.

AND IT SHEDS LIGHT AS PARTICLES — VERY SUBTLE. A few minute golden motes lift off its wet body — pinpoints, smaller than dust — rising slowly and unevenly out of the coat, drifting a centimetre or two, and fading out in the air. Only a handful at a time, sparse and irregular, some barely registering. From the BODY ONLY — the back, the flank, the wet coat — never the eyes, never the mouth, never streaming out of the ember. On a first viewing this should read as a faint shimmer around the newborn, not an effect.

The hands are Charlie's, armoured as in <<<image_2>>>: worn matte plating, scuffed, dust-greyed, the gloves as shown with the fingertips left uncovered, bare fingerpads shining wet where they touch the newborn. Only hands and forearms — no face, no body, no helmet, nothing above the wrists.

Action. The newborn lies almost inert, head down, alive only in its ribs, which work fast and shallow, each breath shivering the film of fluid on its side. It cries — thin, cracked, breaking bursts, an animal sound, muffled by its own downturned face. It moves as an ANIMAL moves, not as a person does: three small involuntary events across the shot and nothing else. At 1.4s a weak shudder runs the length of it and sends a single pinhead bead tracking down its flank in a hair-thin line. At 2.8s the tiny hand on his finger TIGHTENS by a millimetre and eases — a reflex, blind, unmeant. At 3.6s a single blind limb twitch, the wet foot slipping a millimetre on the glove and stopping. At 4.4s the head rolls a centimetre LOWER and settles — never rising. Between these it is completely still. Throughout, the few golden motes keep lifting off it and dying in the air. ## SHOT 1 — 0.00 to 9.00 — NINE SECONDS, HIS FACE, DRAGGING

**EXTREME CLOSE-UP. THE LENS IS ON THE CONCRETE.** The camera lies in the dust a few centimetres above the floor, level with his head, retreating slowly ahead of him so his face holds the same size in frame. His face fills the picture. A forearm and a fist come into the bottom of frame as he pulls. Everything past him is black.

**0.00 — 4.00** — **HE DRAGS HIMSELF FORWARD.** The fist plants in the grit ahead of him and hauls. His face comes with it, cheek almost touching the floor, jaw set, teeth showing. Each pull costs him: the breath catches, hisses out through the teeth, and his eyes screw shut for a second before opening again. Dust rolls past his face. Blood from his nose leaves a mark in the grit.

**4.00 — 6.30** — He stops. Drops his forehead into the dust. Breathes three fast shallow breaths. Then plants the fist and pulls again.

**6.30 — 9.00** — **HIS EYES STOP MOVING.** Something out ahead of him has caught them. He does not move. 【VERY FAINT AND VERY SMALL, REFLECTED IN THE WET OF HIS EYE, A WARM POINT OF LIGHT SWELLS AND FADES.】 One forearm is still lifted off the ground and it stays there. He does not put it down. He does not blink. His breathing stops.

## SUBJECT OF THE PAINTING

An old, dark, academic oil painting. A bullring at night. The arena floor is a wide sweep of pale sand, hot and bright, lit as if by a single high lamp. Everything above it is deep black, and out of that blackness the crowd emerges only as tiers of tiny pale faces, hundreds of them, painted as small dabs of light, curving away around the ring.

At the centre lies A BLACK BULL, collapsed, enormous, its bulk filling the lower middle of the canvas, one white-tipped horn catching the light, its head down on the sand. Banderillas stand up out of its shoulders at angles, their sticks wrapped in red and gold paper, one small red cape hanging from them.

Standing over it, small by comparison, A MATADOR in a gold-embroidered suit of lights and a white shirt, his head bowed, looking down at the animal. He is not triumphant. He is standing very still.

Beneath the bull, spreading across the pale sand, A POOL OF DEEP CRIMSON — the single most saturated colour in the entire thirty seconds. A sword and a dark bundle of cloth lie on the sand nearby. In the lower right corner, a signature in red paint.

【THIS IS A PAINTING — BRUSHWORK, CRAQUELURE, VARNISH AND CANVAS WEAVE ARE VISIBLE AT CLOSE RANGE. IT NEVER BECOMES A PHOTOGRAPH, IT NEVER MOVES, IT NEVER ANIMATES】

The black bull lies dead on its side in the raked sand, a dozen banderillas bristling upright from its shredded shoulders, ribbons soaked black-red and dripping, a sword buried to the hilt between the withers. Blood is everywhere on the animal: pouring in a thick unbroken rope from its open mouth, running from both nostrils, sheeting down the barrel of its body from every barb wound, matting the hide into wet clotted ridges, pooling in the folds of its neck. Beneath and around it a vast lake of blood has spread across the sand — metres wide, deep enough to hold a mirror reflection of the torero standing in it, its edge creeping outward in dark fingers where the sand drinks it, its centre still liquid and glossy, skinned over and rippling faintly, with long drag-streaks and hoof-scuffs printed through it. The torero stands alone at the edge of that pool, boots stained to the ankle, in his gold-embroidered traje de luces, montera in hand, turned toward the stands. Behind them the tiered ranks of the audience rise in their thousands behind the barrera, under a colonnaded gallery. Nothing else in the arena — no horses, no attendants, no mules, the sand beyond the blood completely empty.
Lit by one narrow shaft of hard light falling from high and far to the left, striking only the torero, the dead bull and the pool of blood, holding them in a tight island of illumination and nothing more. Inside that shaft the light is fierce and near-white — blazing on the gold bullion of the jacket until it burns out to pure lead white, raking across the wet black hide so it reads like oiled stone, and igniting the blood into a sheet of molten crimson that becomes the brightest colour in the painting, throwing warm red bounce up onto the man's jaw and hands from below. Outside it, everything collapses. The fall-off is violent, one hand's breadth from lit to unreadable: the sand goes bone white to umber to black within a metre of the pool's edge, the barrera is barely a suggestion, and the entire audience — all thousands of them — is swallowed into dense warm blackness, present only as the faintest scatter of pale smudges where a brow or a collar catches a stray photon, more felt than seen. The colonnaded gallery above is absolute black. Ninety percent of the canvas is shadow, transparent and glazed rather than flat, so the darkness has depth and heat in it. No fill light anywhere. No sky. Spotlight-hard, altar-like, the bodies and the blood burning out of an ocean of dark.

The audience out of the dark becomes a mass of leering half-formed faces, and the torero is small, mean and ordinary against the enormous dead animal. Bone black, dirty ochre, a filthy carmine. No nobility anywhere. Modern in its bleakness, painted like a witness rather than an artist.

PRODUCTION FRAME — a controlled film-set sequence: a costumed sixteen-year-old actor stands in a windy winter field looking up at a derelict building, a small puppet drone settles on his shoulder, he wipes his face and walks toward the entrance with a prop rifle. NOTHING IS FIRED, nobody is hurt, no violence.

FORMAT LAW — 35MM ANAMORPHIC, AND THE ANAMORPHIC CHARACTER MUST BE VISIBLE. Vintage 2x anamorphic glass: THE DEFOCUSED BACKGROUND BOKEH IS OVAL AND STRETCHED VERTICALLY, never round; HIGHLIGHTS SMEAR HORIZONTALLY; GENTLE BARREL DISTORTION AND STRETCH TOWARD THE EDGES, so shapes near the sides pull wider than at centre; FOCUS FALLS OFF FAST AND SOFTLY into a creamy, slightly swirling wash; the lens BREATHES as the camera moves. SOFT AND LOW-CONTRAST WIDE OPEN, corners softer than centre. 【ANAMORPHIC IS THE LENS, NOT THE CROP — SEE FRAME LAW】

GRADE — EXACTLY <<<image_5>>>. Fine even grain, gentle halation on the white sky, MILKY LIFTED BLACKS, LOW CONTRAST AND SLIGHTLY FLAT, A COLD DESATURATED WORLD AGAINST WARM SKIN. GENTLY SOFT THROUGHOUT: no crisp edges, no micro-contrast, no digital sharpening. NO camcorder or video look, NO chroma noise, NO handheld shake, NO 4K sharpness, NO HDR, NO glossy CGI sheen, NO warm sunlight, NO blue streak flares, NO sun flare. IF IT LOOKS SLICK OR MODERN, IT IS WRONG.

FRAME LAW — DELIVER THE FULL FRAME. 【ANAMORPHIC OPTICS, BUT NO WIDESCREEN CROP】 NO black bars, NO letterbox, NO matte, NO borders. THE PICTURE REACHES ALL FOUR EDGES. 【THE WIDESCREEN CROP IS DONE BY HAND AFTERWARDS】 Nothing essential near the top or bottom edge, since those may be cropped later. FAIL TEST: IF THERE ARE BLACK BARS ANYWHERE, IT IS WRONG.

CUT LAW — TWO FRAGMENTS, ONE HARD STRAIGHT CUT. NO dissolves, NO fades, NO wipes, NO flash frames, NO speed ramps, NO slow motion.

MOTION LAW — BOTH FRAGMENTS ARE A DOLLY IN. 【ONE IN EACH — BOTH, NOT ONE】 In each the camera travels continuously forward along its own axis from first frame to last: motorised, dead level, perfectly smooth, easing rather than jerking, never stopping and never arriving. IT IS A REAL PHYSICAL MOVE, NOT A ZOOM. KEEP IT RESTRAINED — the frame tightens gently, never lurching. NO LOCKED-OFF FRAME AND NO HANDHELD. NO pan, NO tilt, NO zoom, NO crane, NO shake. FAIL TEST: IF EITHER FRAGMENT DOES NOT MOVE IN, IT IS WRONG.

FRAGMENT ONE — 0.00–6.00 — THE FACE. FRAMING, PRECISELY: A CENTRED, SYMMETRICAL MEDIUM CLOSE-UP FROM SLIGHTLY BELOW EYE LEVEL, THE LENS TILTED A FEW DEGREES UP. HIS HEAD IS DEAD CENTRE LEFT TO RIGHT. THE TOP OF HIS SKULL SITS ABOUT A SEVENTH DOWN FROM THE TOP EDGE — real headroom, not cropped. HIS CHIN SITS A LITTLE OVER HALFWAY DOWN. BELOW IT THE HIGH COLLAR FILLS THE LOWER CENTRE, and THE TOPS OF BOTH PAULDRONS ENTER THE BOTTOM CORNERS, CUT BY THE BOTTOM EDGE. HIS SHOULDERS SPAN ABOUT TWO THIRDS OF THE WIDTH. 【NOT CROPPED AT THE FOREHEAD, NOT A TIGHT HEAD-ONLY CLOSE-UP】

THE BACKGROUND BEHIND HIM IS <<<image_7>>> AND IT IS A LONG WAY OFF. 【FAR AWAY IN THE DISTANCE, NOT LOOMING BEHIND HIS HEAD】 It sits across the open field, small and low in frame: A NARROW HORIZONTAL BAND OF DARK COLONNADE at about the level of his jaw, NO TALLER IN FRAME THAN THE DISTANCE FROM HIS CHIN TO HIS EYES — dark column shapes with black gaps, greyed and flattened by distance and mist. ABOVE IT, PALE EMPTY SKY AND HAZE FILL THE TOP OF THE FRAME BEHIND HIS SKULL. BELOW IT, A WIDE BAND OF DULL STRAW GRASS — THE FIELD BETWEEN HIM AND THE BUILDING. ALL OF IT THROWN COMPLETELY OUT OF FOCUS, smeared with oval bokeh, nothing legible — but the rhythm of the columns and the central block still read as shape. FAIL TEST: IF THE COLUMNS ARE BIG BEHIND HIM OR FILL THE UPPER HALF, THE BUILDING IS FAR TOO CLOSE. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF ANY PART OF THE BACKGROUND IS SHARP, IT IS WRONG. A DOLLY IN runs the whole six seconds.

0.00–2.00 — HE IS ALREADY LOOKING UP, past and above the lens, at something enormous. He has just stopped running: chest heaving, mouth half open. WATER ALL OVER HIS FACE, AND THE DIRT — see DIRT LAW. BRD-1 comes in from the right and hovers.

2.00–3.20 — IT LANDS. BRD-1 drops the last of the distance and SETS DOWN ON HIS LEFT SHOULDER, claws finding the plating, wings folding. He does not look at it — only a small settle of the shoulder.

3.20–4.60 — HE WIPES HIS FACE — see WIPE LAW. One hand up, one hard pass down, THE DIRT COMING OFF.

4.60–6.00 — The hand drops out of frame. HIS EYES GO STRAIGHT BACK UP and he is still. BRD-1 makes ONE SMALL MECHANICAL HEAD-TURN.
