HE IS TINY — NO MORE THAN A FIFTEENTH OF THE FRAME HEIGHT, a small dark mark at bottom centre seen from behind, walking away through the grass toward the steps. AT THE EXTREME LEFT AND RIGHT EDGES, BARE BLACK WINTER BRANCHES intrude a little into frame. A DOLLY IN tracks forward behind him, dead level, centred on the black opening. IT ENDS WITH HIM SHORT OF THE STEPS AND STILL WALKING — he never arrives, turns, stops or speaks.

WIND LAW — HARD, COLD AND CONSTANT, IN BOTH FRAGMENTS. 【NOT A GENTLE BREEZE — A REAL WINTER WIND WITH WEIGHT BEHIND IT】 It blows steadily across the field, gusting every few seconds. IT HITS HIM AND YOU CAN SEE IT. IN THE CLOSE-UP: the WIND STREAMS ACROSS HIS WET FACE and he holds against it — EYES NARROWING AND WATERING at the edges, ONE HARD BLINK as a gust catches him, water and grit driven off his skin sideways, his BREATH TORN AWAY, THE HIGH COLLAR AND STRAPS SHUDDERING. He does not turn away. IN THE WIDE: he LEANS VERY SLIGHTLY INTO IT, stride bracing, straps whipping, dust torn off the grass and driven past him in low streaks.

THE WORLD IS FULL OF IT: THE BARE BLACK BRANCHES AT THE EDGES HEAVE AND LASH, swinging over and springing back, never still for a frame. THE TALL DRY GRASS IS FLATTENED IN RUNNING WAVES tearing across the field. DEAD LEAVES SKATE ACROSS THE STONE. THE MIST IS DRAGGED SIDEWAYS. BUT HE STAYS ON HIS FEET AND THE SHOT STAYS CALM: never staggered, never blown back, never shielding his face. THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE WITH THE WIND — dead level and smooth on the dolly. FAIL TEST: IF THE GRASS, THE BRANCHES OR HIS FACE ARE STILL, THE WIND IS FAR TOO WEAK. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF YOU COULD NOT TELL FROM THE CLOSE-UP ALONE THAT IT IS WINDY, IT IS WRONG.

DIRT LAW — THE DIRT IS ONE SPECIFIC MARK AND YOU MUST BE ABLE TO POINT AT IT. Before the wipe his face carries A SINGLE DISTINCT DARK FLAKE OF WET GREY-BROWN MUD ON HIS CHEEKBONE, under the eye and slightly toward the ear, about a fingernail across, with A SHORT SMEARED TAIL DRAGGING DOWN AND BACK. Around it fainter grime: silt in the stubble, a grey film along the lower lids, specks on temple and jaw. 【ONE MARK STANDS OUT, THE REST IS FILM】 It is WET DIRT, not dust — it sits ON the skin and catches light, and it never changes place, shape or side before the wipe.

WIPE LAW — ONE PASS, AND IT TAKES THAT MARK OFF. A gloved hand comes up and DRAGS DOWN OVER HIS FACE ONCE — palm flat, hard against the skin, forehead to chin, PASSING DIRECTLY OVER THE MUD ON HIS CHEEKBONE, pushing the water off in a sheet. 【THE WHOLE POINT IS THAT THE MARK DISAPPEARS】 AFTER THE HAND PASSES, THE FLAKE AND ITS TAIL ARE GONE — that cheekbone bare and faintly pink — and THE DIRT IS NOW ON THE GLOVE, a grey-brown streak across the palm as it leaves frame. HIS FACE IS STILL WET AND SHINING; THE MUCK GOES, NOT THE WATER. He BLINKS THE REST OUT and flicks the hand to shed it. He does NOT wipe twice, rub his eyes, use a cloth, or wipe slowly. FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN STILL SEE THE MUD AFTER THE HAND HAS PASSED, IT IS WRONG. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF HIS FACE COMES OUT BONE DRY, IT IS WRONG.

PERFORMANCE LAW — SMALL, HELD, NOT PERFORMED. HE IS SEEING SOMETHING HE DID NOT EXPECT AND CANNOT MEASURE, and that is the only note. Give it in MICRO-GESTURE — the mouth a little open, the jaw setting, ONE SLOW BLINK, the eyes travelling upward as though following something very tall. BANNED: gasping, mouth falling open in awe, eyebrows shooting up, head shaking, stepping back, hand to mouth, tears, smiling, speaking, ANY look into the lens. HE DOES NOT REACT TO THE BIRD LANDING. ONE CHANGE, THEN STILLNESS. FAIL TEST: IF A STRANGER COULD NAME THE EMOTION IN ONE WORD, IT IS TOO BIG.

SKIN LAW — HIS FACE IS REAL AND NOT PRETTY, AND THIS IS HALF THE LOOK. PALE, COLD, BLOTCHY TEENAGE SKIN per <<<image_5>>>: visible pores, faint acne and redness, freckling, chapped patches, pink around the nostrils, DARK SHADOWS UNDER THE EYES. THE SHAVED HEAD SHOWS ITS STUBBLE PATTERN and a wet shine with SMALL DISTINCT DROPLETS. BANNED: skin smoothing, retouching, beauty grade, waxy skin, makeup, any hint of a CG face. FAIL TEST: IF THE SKIN LOOKS CLEAN, EVEN OR FLATTERING, IT IS WRONG.

LIGHT LAW — FLAT, COLD AND FROM A WHITE SKY. Overcast winter daylight, soft and directionless, no sun and no shadows. On his face it catches the wet skin, brow, cheekbone and scalp. NO hard shadow, NO rim light, NO backlight, NO lamps, NO glow on the armour, NO coloured light.

## ANCHOR LAW — WHAT THIS DEVICE IS AND HOW IT WORKS

【READ THIS AS AN INSTRUCTION MANUAL. THE ACTION ONLY MAKES SENSE IF THE MECHANISM IS UNDERSTOOD.】

**WHAT IT IS.** <<<image_6>>> is a SMALL HAND-SIZED BOX — no bigger than a cigarette packet, largely hidden by his fingers when he holds it. A floor anchor. NOT a grappling hook, NOT a gun, NOT a launcher, NOT a drone, NOT a winch.

**ITS PARTS.** A dirty bone-white TOP PLATE carrying the red logo, over a gunmetal LOWER BODY. Set into the lower body, THREE ROUND BORES IN A ROW, each with a polished steel collar and pale dust packed around it. AT REST THE THREE SPIKES ARE RETRACTED AND HIDDEN INSIDE THOSE BORES — nothing protrudes; the bores read as three empty holes. A small orange knurled wheel and a copper stud sit on the edge beside them; a round connector port sits on one end.

**HOW IT IS USED, STEP BY STEP:**
ONE — he lays the box FLAT on the floor, BORED FACE DOWN, so the three bores are against the concrete and the spikes inside them point straight DOWN.
TWO — he puts his palm on the white top plate and presses down to hold it steady.
THREE — his thumb pushes the ORANGE STUD on the edge.
FOUR — THE THREE SPIKES FIRE DOWNWARD OUT OF THE THREE BORES, all at once, in one hard fast stroke, like three nails driven simultaneously — punching into the concrete and burying themselves. The concrete cracks and spits pale dust around each one. The box slams flush to the floor.
FIVE — the box is now PINNED to the floor and does not move. He lifts his hand off and it stays exactly where he put it.
SIX — A THIN GREY STEEL CABLE runs out of a slot in ONE END of the box, at floor level, away across the ground and over the lip. The orange wheel is the brake controlling how fast it pays out.
SEVEN — he takes hold of that cable, goes over the edge, and his weight comes onto it. The box takes the load.

**WHAT IT NEVER DOES.** Never glows, never lights up, never hovers, never transforms or unfolds, never fires a hook or projectile, never spins. Nothing leaves it except the three spikes, straight down into the floor.

FAIL TEST: IF THE SPIKES POINT ANYWHERE OTHER THAN DOWN INTO THE FLOOR, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF THE DEVICE IS BIGGER THAN HIS HAND, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF IT GLOWS, HOVERS OR TRANSFORMS, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF THE CABLE COMES OUT OF THE TOP OR IS ATTACHED TO HIM RATHER THAN RUNNING FROM THE BOX, IT IS WRONG.

## CABLE LAW

A THIN GREY STEEL CABLE, three or four millimetres — fine multi-strand wire rope with a visible helical lay and a broken satin sheen. Not a rope. Not fibrous. Not thick.

## SILENCE LAW

NO DIALOGUE. No voice, no whisper, no shout, no voiceover, no narration. NOBODY SPEAKS.

He heard it. His eyes are fixed upward, hard and calculating. Jaw tight. One shallow breath. His hand adjusts its grip on the cable.

Then — SUDDENLY — HE DROPS. No warning, no build, no slow slide: between one frame and the next he is GONE STRAIGHT DOWN out of the bottom of frame, and dust and grit pour down through the empty air he was in.

FAIL TEST: IF HE SINKS SLOWLY OR SLIDES OUT OF FRAME, IT IS WRONG. IT IS INSTANT.

# FRAGMENT FIVE — 20.40 to 25.00 — THE FALL

HARD CUT. FROM ABOVE, WIDE, LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN, LOCKED — and it does NOT shake.

【HE FALLS FACE-DOWN — HIS FACE AND CHEST TOWARD THE GROUND, HIS BACK TO THE SKY】 We are above him, so WE SEE HIS BACK: the rifle flat on the exosuit, the back of his skull, his arms out and reaching down toward the floor coming at him. HE IS NOT ON HIS BACK. HE IS NOT FACE-UP. He does not tumble and he does not fight — there is no time to. The loose cable whips alongside him and the broken slab and the small anchor fall with him.

BENEATH HIM THE FLOOR IS THERE AND IT IS COMING UP — pale rubble-strewn concrete catching the cyan light, growing in the frame, unmistakably close. THIS IS A SHORT FALL AND IT ACCELERATES. It is over in a couple of seconds.

AT THE END, THE IMPACT — and the frame FILLS INSTANTLY WITH GREY DUST, a hard blooming cloud that swallows him and the falling concrete together. We do not see the landing itself.

# FRAGMENT SIX — 25.00 to 30.00 — ON THE GROUND

HARD CUT. LOCKED OFF, DEAD STILL, AND VERY TIGHT — his head and one shoulder fill the frame, cropped by the edges. NOT a medium. NOT a wide. We are right down on the concrete beside his face.

【HE LANDED ON HIS FACE — THAT IS WHY HE IS BLEEDING】 He is face-down on the rubble, cheek and jaw against the broken concrete, head turned toward the lens. The side of his face that hit the ground is RAW: a split through the eyebrow, a gash along the cheekbone, grit driven into the skin, BLOOD running wet and red into the grey dust and beading on the concrete under his mouth. One arm folded awkwardly under him. Dust raining down through a cold cyan shaft.

HE IS IN REAL PAIN AND FIGHTING TO BREATHE. He COUGHS — hard, wet, involuntary, shaking his whole head and hurting him — then again, then a strangled inhale that will not come. Catching gasps between them, mouth open, jaw working. Eyes squeeze shut and open. Fingers scrape the concrete. He tries to push up on one arm and it gives out.

【HURTING BADLY, BUT NOT PERFORMING】 It is involuntary — coughing, gasping, flinching — not acting. NO screaming, NO groaning theatrically, NO writhing, NO speech. FAIL TEST: IF HE OVERACTS OR SCREAMS, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF HE LOOKS MERELY WINDED OR UNHURT, IT IS ALSO WRONG. NO exposed injury, NO pooling gore.

AT ABOUT 28.20 BRD-1 ARRIVES — dropping fast out of the dark, decelerating hard, LANDING on the concrete beside his face, close and large in the foreground. It steadies, leans in toward him, head tilting, LOOKING AT HIM, and makes one short low mechanical note. IT DOES NOT FLY AT THE CAMERA.

He gets one eye open and finds it. Another cough. We hold there, into the cut.

SHARP: his face. BRD-1 in the near foreground is slightly soft.

## MAINTAIN CONSISTENCY

Same man, same face, same exosuit, rifle magnetically flat on his back, earbud in his RIGHT ear throughout. 35mm anamorphic, full frame, no bars. Six fragments, one camera behaviour each — a fluent steadicam that STARTS ON THE DEVICE and travels to reveal him, ROUGH lateral handheld, a FAST hard dolly in on the anchor, locked close-up in near darkness, locked wide for the fall, locked VERY TIGHT on his face on the ground. HE DESCENDS AT A REAL WORKING PACE and THE LIGHT LEAVES HIM AS HE GOES. The anchor is a SMALL box laid flat, spikes retracted in three bores until they fire straight down into the concrete; the cable is thin grey steel from a slot in one end. HE LANDS ON HIS FACE — that is where the blood comes from — and ends in a VERY TIGHT locked shot, cheek on the concrete, COUGHING HARD and fighting for breath, involuntary rather than performed. BRD-1 DROPS IN BESIDE HIS FACE IN THE LAST TWO SECONDS. NOBODY SPEAKS.

## FORMAT LAW — 35MM ANAMORPHIC

Shot on 35mm anamorphic. An OPTICAL description, not a delivery format. Oval, vertically stretched bokeh in every out-of-focus highlight. Horizontal smear on bright points. Barrel distortion and horizontal stretch toward the edges. Fast, soft focus falloff. Visible lens breathing on any focus change. Corners softer than centre. Heavy fine 35mm grain, present in the shadows.

【ANAMORPHIC IS THE LENS, NOT THE CROP — SEE FRAME LAW】

## FRAME LAW

FULL FRAME. Edge to edge. No letterbox, no black bars, no cinema-scope matte drawn into the picture, no border. FAIL TEST: IF THERE IS A BLACK BAR ANYWHERE, IT IS WRONG.

## CUT LAW

TWO HARD CUTS. Three fragments. Straight cuts on the exact timecodes below — no dissolve, no fade, no whip, no morph, no speed ramp, no extra cuts.

FRAGMENT ONE — STEADICAM. Smooth, floating, gliding, following him. Not handheld, not locked.
FRAGMENT TWO — LOCKED OFF from the floor of the room below, looking straight up.
FRAGMENT THREE — LOCKED OFF, extreme close-up on his hand and the device.

FAIL TEST: IF FRAGMENT ONE IS HANDHELD OR JITTERY, IT IS WRONG.

## WEAPON LAW — HE PUTS IT AWAY

【THIS IS A SCIENCE-FICTION FILM SET. THE RIFLE IS A PROP. NOTHING IS FIRED, NOTHING IS AIMED AT ANYONE, THERE IS NO VIOLENCE IN THESE FIFTEEN SECONDS.】

HE STARTS WITH THE RIFLE IN HIS HANDS. Stock in against his shoulder, both hands on the weapon, muzzle level and forward, walking behind it — working, covering the corridor ahead of him. IT IS NOT ON HIS BACK IN THE FIRST FRAME.

THEN HE STOWS IT. When he reaches the hole and stops, he takes the weapon down and PUTS IT BEHIND HIM: a single practised movement — the muzzle drops, he swings the rifle up and over his shoulder onto his back, releases it onto the sling, and gives it one small settling shove with the heel of his hand so it sits flat against the exosuit. Two seconds. No fumbling, no examining it, no ceremony.

AFTER THAT IT STAYS ON HIS BACK for the rest of the shot and both his hands are free.

FAIL TEST: IF THE RIFLE IS ALREADY SLUNG ON HIS BACK AT 0.00, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF HE STILL HAS IT IN HIS HANDS AT THE END OF FRAGMENT ONE, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF HE DROPS IT ON THE FLOOR, IT IS WRONG.

## SKY LAW — OVERCAST

【THE SKY ABOVE THE COLLAPSED CEILING IS CLOUDY】

A FLAT, HEAVY, OVERCAST SKY — an unbroken ceiling of pale grey-white cloud with visible soft structure and tonal variation in it, darker toward one side. NOT a clear blue sky. NOT a blown-out featureless white void. NOT sunny.

The light it throws is consequently SOFT AND DIRECTIONLESS from above — bright, cold, shadowless daylight rather than hard sun shafts. Everything below is lit evenly and coldly from overhead, edges are soft, contrast is low outside, and the deep interior shadows stay deep because no light reaches them, not because the sun is hard.

FAIL TEST: IF THE SKY IS BLUE, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF THERE ARE HARD SUNBEAMS OR SHARP-EDGED SHADOWS FROM ABOVE, IT IS WRONG.

## LIGHT LAW

ABOVE — cold overcast daylight down through the broken ceiling of <<<image_7>>>, a stop or two over on the pale plaster. Soft, even, chalky. Dust hanging and turning in the air everywhere.

BELOW — <<<image_8>>>. COLD CYAN-BLUE light, and only where it falls through the ragged holes. Everything outside those shafts is CRUSHING BLACK with no detail recoverable — not dark grey, BLACK. The blue does not spread, does not fill, does not bounce.

【THE CAMERA DOES NOT COMPENSATE — NO AUTO-EXPOSURE LIFT, NO IRIS OPENING UP, NO BRIGHTENING OF THE DARK ROOM AT ANY POINT】

FAIL TEST: IF THE ROOM BELOW BECOMES READABLE OR EVENLY LIT, IT IS WRONG.

## COLOUR LAW

Desaturated, cold, chalky. Pale grey concrete, bone-white plaster, the washed blue-green dado of the corridor, grey dust, grey cloud. The only colours permitted: the muted brick-red accents of the exosuit and rifle, the worn ORANGE of the anchor, and the COLD CYAN of the light below. No teal-and-orange grade, no warm hour, no filter look.

## DUST LAW

DUST IS EVERYWHERE AND IT IS ALWAYS MOVING — hanging in the air, turning slowly, kicked up by his boots, pouring off the broken slab edges in fine streams.

## EARBUD LAW — RIGHT EAR, ALWAYS

The earbud is <<<image_5>>> and IT IS ALREADY IN HIS RIGHT EAR IN THE FIRST FRAME. He does not put it in here. It never moves to the left ear, never falls out, never gets adjusted, never gets removed, never swaps sides at a cut.

【WHEN THE CAMERA FACES HIM, HIS RIGHT EAR IS ON THE LEFT OF FRAME. WHEN THE CAMERA IS BEHIND HIM, HIS RIGHT EAR IS ON THE RIGHT OF FRAME. SAME EAR EITHER WAY — DO THE ARITHMETIC, DO NOT MIRROR IT.】

FAIL TEST: IF IT APPEARS IN HIS LEFT EAR OR IN BOTH EARS, IT IS WRONG.

## BRD-1 LAW — SHOULDER, THEN GONE

BRD-1 is a small mechanical bird, machined and worn. IT IS PERCHED ON HIS LEFT SHOULDER PLATE FROM THE FIRST FRAME, gripping the armour, riding his walk, absorbing the motion with tiny adjustments of its feet and small counter-rotations of its head as he moves.

【IT IS THERE AT 0.00 — NOT ARRIVING, NOT LANDING, ALREADY ON HIM】

THEN IT LEAVES. In FRAGMENT ONE, as he reaches the hole, IT DROPS OFF HIS SHOULDER AND FLIES — a fast, low, curving line AWAY from us, out across the corridor and out of frame. IT DOES NOT FLY AT THE CAMERA, does not pass the lens, does not grow huge in the foreground, does not circle, does not hover. The camera does not follow it. AFTER THAT IT IS GONE and it does not appear again in these fifteen seconds.

It never becomes a real bird, never grows feathers, never softens, never blinks like an animal.

FAIL TEST: IF IT IS NOT ON HIS LEFT SHOULDER IN THE FIRST FRAME, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF IT FLIES TOWARD OR PAST THE CAMERA, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF IT IS VISIBLE IN FRAGMENT TWO OR THREE, IT IS WRONG.

## ANCHOR LAW — SMALL, AND IT FACES DOWN

THE DEVICE IS <<<image_6>>> and it is used, not admired.

**IT IS SMALL.** It sits comfortably in one hand and is largely HIDDEN BY HIS FINGERS when he holds it — no bigger than a cigarette packet, thinner than his palm is wide. Against the concrete it should read as a modest little object, dwarfed by the rubble around it.

【IT IS A HAND-SIZED TOOL, NOT A BRIEFCASE】 FAIL TEST: IF IT IS AS BIG AS HIS FOREARM OR LARGER THAN HIS HAND, IT IS WRONG. FAIL TEST: IF IT LOOKS LIKE A LARGE CASE OR A PIECE OF LUGGAGE, IT IS WRONG.

**THE SPIKES POINT AT THE FLOOR.** He sets the device DOWN onto the ground, FLAT, with THE SPIKED FACE DOWNWARD — the three blunt hardened spikes pointing straight at the concrete, ready to go into it. The marked top face with the logo is UPWARD, under his palm. The spikes are NOT sideways, NOT pointing at the camera, NOT pointing outward, NOT visible standing out to the side of the body.

FAIL TEST: IF THE SPIKES POINT ANYWHERE OTHER THAN DOWN INTO THE FLOOR, IT IS WRONG.

**THE ACTION.** His hand lowers it onto the slab and presses down. His thumb hits the ORANGE STUD. THE THREE SPIKES FIRE DOWNWARD — driven out hard and fast in a single violent stroke, punching into the concrete, the slab cracking and spitting pale dust around each one, the body slamming flush to the floor. His hand lifts away and it STAYS THERE, gripping, the thin grey steel cable running out of it toward the lip.

It is a punch, not a machine sequence. The spikes do not retract, do not glow, do not spin, do not extend into long stakes. FAIL TEST: IF THE DEVICE GLOWS, HOVERS, LIGHTS UP OR TRANSFORMS, IT IS WRONG.

## CABLE LAW

A THIN GREY STEEL CABLE, three or four millimetres — fine multi-strand wire rope with a visible helical lay and a broken satin sheen. Not a rope. Not fibrous. Not thick.

## SILENCE LAW

NO DIALOGUE. No voice, no whisper, no shout, no voiceover, no narration. NOBODY SPEAKS.

## MAINTAIN CONSISTENCY

Same man, same face, same exosuit, earbud in his RIGHT ear from the first frame. BRD-1 IS ON HIS LEFT SHOULDER AT 0.00 AND FLIES AWAY FROM CAMERA EARLY IN FRAGMENT ONE, then is gone. 35mm anamorphic, full frame, no bars. Two hard cuts, three fragments — steadicam, then locked from below, then locked extreme close-up. HE STARTS WITH THE RIFLE IN HIS HANDS AND PUTS IT ON HIS BACK when he reaches the hole. THE SKY IS FLAT GREY OVERCAST, never blue, and the daylight is soft and shadowless. Below is crushing black cut by cold cyan shafts and it NEVER brightens. THE DEVICE IS SMALL — hand-sized, half-hidden by his fingers — AND HE SETS IT DOWN WITH THE SPIKES FACING THE FLOOR, which fire straight down into the concrete. The cable is thin grey steel, not rope. NOBODY SPEAKS.

REFERENCE PRIORITY: the references are the authority on face, wardrobe, materials, machinery, markings and colour; where this text and a reference disagree, the reference wins. This text governs action, camera, light and sound only. THERE ARE EXACTLY FIVE REFERENCES AND NO OTHERS, AND ALL FIVE MUST BE ATTACHED — 01 CHARLIE, 02 EXOSUIT, 03 RIFLE, 04 THE TUNNEL INTERIOR, 05 BRD-1. <<<image_1>>> defines CHARLIE — his build, his height and his shaved head. 【HIS FACE IS NEVER SEEN】 he is a silhouette throughout — see SILHOUETTE LAW. <<<image_2>>> defines THE EXOSUIT — its bulk, its collar, its pauldrons, its proportions. 【ONLY ITS SHAPE MATTERS HERE, NOT ITS COLOUR】 【IF <<<image_2>>> SHOWS A HELMET OR VISOR, IGNORE IT】 <<<image_3>>> defines THE RIFLE — its shape and length only; carried, never raised, never fired. <<<image_4>>> IS THE TUNNEL INTERIOR AND IT IS THE ONLY LOCATION — a huge flooded railway tunnel: a VAULTED CONCRETE BORE with heavy ribbed arches banding the roof and walls, pale grey-brown concrete streaked with damp, white mineral bloom and dark staining; RAISED LEDGES along both sides just above the waterline, thick with moss and lichen; LONG HANGING VINES, IVY AND PALE ROOTS trailing down from the roof in curtains; A RUSTED RAIL LINE running away down the floor; BLACK LEAF-STREWN WATER over the floor; and A SMALL BRIGHT ARCHED PORTAL OF DAYLIGHT AT THE FAR END, blown out white. 【TAKE THE ARCHITECTURE, MATERIALS, VINES, RAILS AND FAR PORTAL EXACTLY】 but not its camera position, not its stillness and not its calm. 【THE PLATE SHOWS A BLACK MIRROR — HERE THE WATER IS ONLY ANKLE TO SHIN DEEP over the old trackbed, shallow enough to sprint through and to throw hard】 <<<image_5>>> IS THE BRD-1 CHARACTER AND SCALE SHEET — design and size, 12 CM from claws to crest tip. 【DO NOT COPY THE SHEET'S PICTURE】 here it is also a silhouette. 【Unused assets】 nothing else is used for anything.

PRODUCTION FRAME — a controlled film-set sequence: a costumed sixteen-year-old actor running through a flooded tunnel set with a small puppet drone flying beside him, filmed guerrilla-style by an operator running with him. NOTHING IS FIRED, nothing is aimed at anyone, nobody is hurt, no violence, no injury, no blood, and nothing is chasing him in frame.

FORMAT LAW — SUPER 16MM FILM, HANDHELD, RUN AND GUN, PUSHED AND FILTHY. THE ENERGY IS 28 DAYS LATER BUT THE FORMAT IS FILM, AND BOTH MATTER. This is a documentary camera operator with a small 16mm camera on his shoulder, running, in the dark, with no lights and no time.

IT IS FILM AND IT MUST READ AS FILM: SUPER 16 NEGATIVE, HEAVY CRAWLING GRAIN boiling in the shadows, GATE WEAVE, real 180-degree SHUTTER MOTION BLUR on every fast move — smooth organic smear, never a digital stutter. HALATION BLOOMING off the bright portal, the highlight glowing and spreading rather than clipping flat. MILKY LIFTED BLACKS. Dust, hairs and dirt in the gate. The odd splice bump at a cut, like a workprint.

AND IT IS UNDEREXPOSED AND PUSHED, WHICH IS WHERE THE GRIT COMES FROM: there is not enough light in here for the stock, so the negative is thin and the lab has pushed it. THE GRAIN IS ENORMOUS AND ALIVE, especially in the dark two-thirds of the frame; the shadows are muddy and swimming; the contrast is harsh and ugly; the colour has almost fallen out, leaving a cold sour near-monochrome image with a dirty green-grey cast.

THE LENS IS CHEAP AND FAST: a wide-ish 16mm zoom, soft in the corners, breathing when the focus moves, flaring milkily when the portal swings into it. FOCUS IS PULLED BY THE OPERATOR HIMSELF AND HE IS LOSING — it hunts, arrives late, racks to the wrong thing, and whole fragments are simply out of focus.

BANNED OUTRIGHT: anything digital or clean. NO video look, NO camcorder look, NO interlace combing, NO compression blocking, NO 4K sharpness, NO HDR, NO polished grade, NO glossy CGI sheen, NO drone smoothness, NO beauty lighting, NO composed and pretty frame. IF IT LOOKS SLICK, IT IS WRONG. It should look like exposed film that was shot in a hurry, in the dark, by somebody who was running.

CUT LAW — THIS IS NOT ONE SHOT. IT IS A RIPPED-APART SEQUENCE OF FRAGMENTS AND IT IS CUT TO PIECES. Across the fifteen seconds, USE MANY HARD CUTS — somewhere between EIGHT AND FIFTEEN of them — and INVENT THE ANGLES YOURSELF. There is no master, no establishing shot, no coverage, no rhythm.

THE FRAGMENTS ARE UNEVEN AND MOSTLY VERY SHORT: some a few frames, some a second, one or two stretching to three. NEVER the same length twice, NEVER a pattern, NEVER on a beat. CUT ON MOVEMENT, mid-stride, mid-whip, mid-blur — never on a still frame, never on a clean composition, never at the end of an action.

THE CUTS DO NOT MATCH AND ARE NOT MEANT TO: JUMP CUTS in the same direction, sudden reversals of screen direction, angles that skip forward in space, a fragment that seems to repeat a moment we just saw, a cut to something that takes a second to identify. THE GEOGRAPHY SHOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE TO HOLD ONTO — only that he is running, that it is dark, and that there is light ahead.

WHAT MUST SURVIVE THE CHAOS: he is running, he never stops, the bird is with him, the portal is getting bigger. NOTHING ELSE HAS TO BE LEGIBLE. NO dissolves, NO fades, NO wipes, NO white flash frames, NO speed ramps, NO slow motion, NO freeze frames, NO stylised transitions — every cut is a hard straight cut.

RIG LAW — PUT THE CAMERA IN PLACES A SANE CREW WOULD NOT. Every fragment is from somewhere different and most of them are wrong. Draw from these and invent more:

DOWN IN THE WATER at ankle height, the surface slapping the lens, his boots smashing past over the top of frame. BEHIND HIM AND FAR TOO CLOSE, the back of his skull and pauldron filling half the picture, the portal flaring past his shoulder. RUNNING BACKWARDS AHEAD OF HIM, the operator's own stumble throwing the frame. FROM THE SIDE LEDGE, low, the rail line and black water raking the foreground. FROM BEHIND A CURTAIN OF HANGING VINES, roots whipping across the lens as he passes through. TILTED HARD OVER, thirty or forty degrees, and left there. POINTED UP AT THE ROOF as the arches strobe past. DOWN AT HIS FEET, nothing but water and boots. HELD OUT AT ARM'S LENGTH, wobbling and rolling. ONE SNORRICAM FRAGMENT ONLY, rigged to his body — see SNORRICAM LAW. A FRAGMENT WHERE HE HAS LEFT THE FRAME ENTIRELY and the operator is running down an empty black tunnel. A FRAGMENT SO CLOSE AND BLURRED it is unreadable for half a second before it resolves into part of him.

SNORRICAM LAW — EXACTLY ONE FRAGMENT, NEVER MORE. THE LAST VERSION WAS FULL OF IT AND THAT IS THE FAILURE TO AVOID. A snorricam is the shot where the camera is RIGGED TO HIS BODY, so he stays LOCKED AND CENTRED and unnaturally steady while the whole tunnel swings and rocks behind him. USE IT ONCE, BRIEFLY, THEN NEVER AGAIN. EVERY OTHER FRAGMENT IS A FREE, UNATTACHED CAMERA held by a person moving independently — HE SLIDES AROUND THE FRAME, drifts to the edges, is cut in half, is lost and found, and CHANGES SIZE as the operator gains and loses ground. FAIL TEST: IF HE SITS CENTRED, THE SAME SIZE AND ROCK STEADY WHILE THE BACKGROUND SWINGS IN MORE THAN ONE FRAGMENT, THE SEQUENCE IS WRONG. No chest mount, no helmet mount, no rig on the weapon anywhere else.

SHAKE LAW — 28 DAYS LATER, AND THEN MORE, AND THEN MORE AGAIN. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ABOUT THE CAMERA AND IT CANNOT BE OVERDONE. IT HAS BEEN TOO TAME EVERY TIME SO FAR. A person is sprinting flat out through shin-deep water with a 16mm camera barely held on his shoulder, and he is losing the fight with it.

A HARD VERTICAL SLAM ON EVERY SINGLE FOOTFALL — and the operator is sprinting, so THAT IS THREE OR FOUR VIOLENT JOLTS EVERY SECOND, the whole picture dropping a good fraction of the frame height and snapping back. THE HORIZON ROLLS THROUGH TWENTY, THIRTY, FORTY DEGREES AND SOMETIMES PAST IT, and is never level for more than a moment. THE FRAME SWINGS OFF HIM ENTIRELY, TRAVELLING A WHOLE FRAME WIDTH OR MORE, then WHIPS BACK, overshoots, corrects, overshoots again. SUDDEN LURCHES as the operator's boot goes out from under him in the water. THE CAMERA IS KNOCKED — brushed by a vine, jolted by a shoulder, half dropped and caught.

EVERYTHING SMEARS: on the fast swings the picture is pure horizontal streak for several frames at a time, unreadable, the arches and the portal drawn out into bands of light. WATER HITS THE LENS and sits on it in fat beads. THE OPERATOR'S OWN BREATH AND EFFORT ARE IN THE FRAME as a constant heavy judder underneath everything else.

IT IS ILLEGIBLE FOR STRETCHES AND THAT IS CORRECT — SOME OF IT SHOULD BE GENUINELY HARD TO WATCH. FAIL TEST: IF ANY HALF-SECOND OF THIS COULD PASS FOR A STEADICAM, A GIMBAL, A DRONE, A DOLLY OR A STABILISED SHOT, IT IS FAR TOO SMOOTH. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN COMFORTABLY READ THE WHOLE FRAME AT ANY POINT, THE SHAKE IS TOO SMALL. But it is A RUNNING HUMAN BEING, never a machine: irregular, uneven, different sized movements at different speeds layered over each other — NEVER a rhythmic wobble, NEVER a looping shake cycle, NEVER a uniform buzz, NEVER a stylised camera-shake filter, NEVER a video-game headbob.

SILHOUETTE LAW — HE IS A BLACK SHAPE AND NOTHING MORE. He runs toward the only light, so we are always on the dark side of him. HE IS FLAT BLACK: NO face, NO eyes, NO skin tone, NO colour on the armour, NO red, NO white, NO YGGD marks, NO detail on the rifle. He reads ONLY as an OUTLINE — round shaved skull, high collar, the hard line of the pauldrons, legs driving, rifle carried low. WE READ HIM BY EDGE, NOT SURFACE: the bright water beneath him, the blown portal ahead, a thin wet rim of light along one shoulder and the top of his skull. NOTHING FILLS IN, and in the darkest fragments HE IS BARELY THERE AT ALL. FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN SEE HIS FACE OR THE RED AND WHITE OF THE SUIT, THE SHOT IS WRONG.

THE ACTION — A DEAD SPRINT FOR FIFTEEN SECONDS. HE IS NOT JOGGING, NOT LOPING, NOT RUNNING STEADILY — HE IS FLAT OUT, AT HIS ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM, AND HE IS NEARLY OUT OF CONTROL. THE LAST VERSION WAS FAR TOO SLOW AND THAT IS THE FAILURE TO AVOID.

WHAT MAKES IT READ AS FAST IS THE WORLD, NOT THE LEGS: THE TUNNEL RIPS PAST HIM. The vaulted arches band overhead SEVERAL EVERY SECOND, strobing by; the ledges tear past; the vines come at the camera and are gone; the walls streak and smear. THE PORTAL AHEAD GROWS VISIBLY ACROSS THE FIFTEEN SECONDS. AND THE BODY IS AT FULL TILT: HIGH CADENCE, feet turning over fast, strides long and hard; the body PITCHED FORWARD, almost falling and catching itself every step; the free arm driving; the armour hammering; his weight going into every footfall so the water EXPLODES around his boots in heavy bursts and sheets, spray hitting the lens.

FAIL TEST: IF YOU COULD KEEP PACE WITH HIM AT A JOG, HE IS FAR TOO SLOW. IF THE BACKGROUND IS DRIFTING PAST RATHER THAN TEARING PAST, HE IS FAR TOO SLOW. He should look like he is about to lose his footing and does not.

HE NEVER STOPS, never slows, never looks back, never trips, never turns, never speaks. NOTHING CHASES HIM AND NOTHING IS SHOWN BEHIND HIM. THE ONLY PROGRESSION IS THE LIGHT — the portal small and distant at the start, large and blinding by the end, with him blacker against it every time we find him again.

BRD-1 — FLYING WITH HIM, FRANTICALLY, AND IT IS TINY. It flies around him at roughly head height, never in one place — see ZIGZAG LAW. IT IS 12 CM FROM CLAWS TO CREST — robin-sized, roughly as tall as the distance from his chin to his eyebrows, its whole body would fit in his closed fist. NEVER crow-sized, NEVER hawk-sized, NEVER the size of his head, NEVER changing size.

IT FLIES LIKE A SMALL FAST MACHINE, NOT A BIG BIRD: a QUICK, SHALLOW, BLURRED WINGBEAT far too fast to count, the wings a flicker either side of a level body. IT NEVER GLIDES, NEVER soars, NEVER flaps slowly, NEVER circles lazily, NEVER banks like a hawk, NEVER hovers like a helicopter.

ZIGZAG LAW — IT DOES NOT FLY BESIDE HIM. IT IS FRANTIC AND IT NEVER HOLDS A LINE. 【NEVER A WINGMAN】 it does NOT hold station off his shoulder, does NOT pace him, does NOT sit in formation, does NOT travel in a straight line with him, does NOT stay in one part of the frame.

IT MOVES IN HARD ZIGZAGS: sharp, sudden changes of direction with almost no curve between them — a fast burst one way, a snap turn, a fast burst back the other way, up, down, diagonally, and again. THE TURNS ARE ABRUPT, like a bat or a swift or a panicking bird trapped indoors, not the smooth swooping arcs of a big bird. Between the bursts it stalls for a fraction of a second, flutters, and then rips off in a new direction.

IT USES THE WHOLE TUNNEL: cutting across in front of him and behind him, shooting up toward the roof and dropping back down, skimming the water, swerving out to a wall and tearing back, crossing right in front of the lens, left of frame in one fragment and right in the next. IT IS EVERYWHERE AND NOWHERE — agitated, urgent, almost erratic, a small thing in a panic that is somehow still keeping up.

FAIL TEST: IF ITS PATH COULD BE DRAWN AS A SMOOTH LINE, OR IF IT SITS ALONGSIDE HIS HEAD FOR MORE THAN HALF A SECOND, THE FLIGHT IS WRONG. Every second of its flight should contain at least one hard change of direction.

PERFORMANCE LAW — HE IS FURIOUS AND ALMOST NONE OF IT SHOWS. THE PROBLEM TO AVOID IS AN ACTOR PLAYING ANGER. There is no shout, no snarl, no grimace, no head shake, no eye roll, no jaw clench, no fist, no strike at the weapon, no throwing anything, no punching the air. Everything is INWARD AND MUSCULAR AND SMALL.

PICK A FEW OF THESE AND NO MORE: a single hard exhale down the nose; the corner of the mouth pulling back a few millimetres and releasing; a fast flick of the eyes down and back up; one blink held a fraction too long; the muscle at the hinge of the jaw moving once and stopping; a swallow that never completes; the head dropping a centimetre and coming back. THE WORD ITSELF IS THE RELEASE and it is under-played almost to nothing — he does not project it, he breathes it out.

NOTHING ESCALATES: the frustration does not build, does not peak, does not resolve. It is the same at 0:05 as at 0:01. The only real change across the shot is that he stops looking and starts moving. AVOID THE SYNTHETIC TELLS: perfectly smooth eased facial motion, symmetrical movement on both sides of the face, micro-expressions that loop or repeat, a face morphing between states, blinking on a regular rhythm, eyes gliding smoothly instead of flicking. HUMAN EYES MOVE IN FAST JUMPS AND THEN HOLD. If it looks like acting, it is wrong.

**STEP TWO — THE SPIKES EMERGE.** THREE STEEL SPIKES PUSH OUT OF THE THREE FRONT BORES — one from each hole, all three together, fast and hard. They come out exactly as far as the reference shows: short, blunt, faceted, standing clear of the body.

**STEP THREE — THEY DOUBLE.** 【THIS IS THE KEY MOVEMENT】 Each spike then EXTENDS AGAIN — a SECOND SEGMENT TELESCOPES OUT OF THE FIRST, DOUBLING ITS LENGTH in one hard snap. What was a short stub becomes a long steel pin, twice as long, with a hardened point on the end. Three of them, simultaneously.

**STEP FOUR — THEY GO INTO THE GROUND.** As they double, THEY DRIVE DOWNWARD AND BURY THEMSELVES IN THE CONCRETE. The points punch through the surface and disappear into the slab. The concrete SPLITS around each entry — a starburst of cracks, chips flying, pale dust blowing out from all three holes. The body of the box slams down flush and hard against the floor with the recoil. The frame jumps a few pixels.

**END STATE — AND THIS IS WHAT THE LAST FRAME MUST SHOW.** THE THREE DOUBLED SPIKES ARE EMBEDDED IN THE CONCRETE, sunk to their collars, immovable. The box is PINNED FLAT TO THE FLOOR and does not shift, wobble or lift. Three cracked craters around three buried steel shafts. IT IS PART OF THE BUILDING NOW.

**STEP FIVE — THE CABLE.** His hand lifts away. The device stays exactly where he put it. THEN THE THIN GREY STEEL CABLE PAYS OUT OF THE ROUND PORT ON THE SIDE END — not the front, not the top — runs across the concrete, over the lip, and SNAPS TAUT as weight comes onto it below, out of frame. The box does not move a millimetre when the load hits it.

FAIL TESTS: IF THE SPIKES DO NOT END UP BURIED IN THE CONCRETE, THE SHOT HAS FAILED — THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FAIL TEST HERE. IF THEY EXTEND AND JUST HANG IN THE AIR, IT IS WRONG. IF THEY REST ON TOP OF THE SURFACE WITHOUT PENETRATING, IT IS WRONG. IF THEY DO NOT DOUBLE IN LENGTH, IT IS WRONG. IF THEY RETRACT AGAIN, IT IS WRONG. IF THE BOX SLIDES, TIPS OR LIFTS AFTER THEY BITE, IT IS WRONG. IF THE CABLE EXITS ANYWHERE BUT THE SIDE PORT, IT IS WRONG. IF THE DEVICE GLOWS, HOVERS OR TRANSFORMS, IT IS WRONG. IF IT IS BIGGER THAN HIS HAND, IT IS WRONG.

Cold overcast daylight from above, soft and shadowless, a stop over on the pale concrete. The hole beyond the lip is CRUSHING BLACK — no detail, no lift, and the camera does not compensate. Almost every pixel is CRUSHING BLACK — no detail, no texture, no architecture, no walls, no depth cues, no readable environment. Do not build a space. Do not show us where we are.

THE ONLY THINGS VISIBLE, EVER:
— a few ragged holes in the ceiling far above, glowing weak COLD CYAN-BLUE, hazy with dust, torn rebar and hanging roots trailing around their edges
— thin cyan shafts falling from them through the dusty air
— CHARLIE, and only the parts of him a shaft happens to catch

Everything else is BLACK. If a surface is not directly in a cyan shaft, IT IS NOT VISIBLE AT ALL.

## THE OTHER THINGS THAT MATTER

**NO WALL. NO SHAFT.** He is in OPEN AIR in the middle of blackness, HOLDING HIS WEIGHT ON THE CABLE WITH BOTH FISTS, body upright beneath his hands. Nothing within reach, nothing visible around him. His boots touch NOTHING and he does NOT walk down a surface — but he is NEVER limp, horizontal or floating. FAIL: a wall behind him = wrong. FAIL: he hangs slack or lies back in the air = wrong.

**THE SPIKES GO INTO THE CONCRETE.** Three spikes push out of the three FRONT bores, then EACH DOUBLES IN LENGTH — a second segment telescoping out — and they DRIVE IN AND BURY THEMSELVES, splitting the slab, embedded to the collars. FAIL: spikes resting on the surface = wrong.

**NOBODY ELSE.** No BRD-1, no bird, no drone, no flying object — not on his shoulder, not in the air, not in the background, not audible, not at the end. HE IS COMPLETELY ALONE FOR THIRTY SECONDS.

**HIS FACE IS UNMARKED UNTIL HE LANDS.** No scar, no old cut, no gash, no blood anywhere on his face or head in the first five shots. Dirt and dust only. The ONLY blood in the film is what he coughs up at the very end.

0.00–0.80 — FULL WHITE. IT OPENS ON A COMPLETELY WHITE FRAME, EDGE TO EDGE, NOTHING IN IT — no figure, no shape, no text, no logo. Blown-out film, alive with grain and a faint flicker, not a flat white card. IT HOLDS FOR UNDER A SECOND. FAIL TEST: IF THE FIRST FRAME IS ANYTHING OTHER THAN PURE WHITE, IT IS WRONG.

0.80–5.00 — THE WORLD COMES BACK, AND HE RUNS INTO IT. The white is the overcast sky, and THE IMAGE BLEEDS DOWN OUT OF IT as the exposure recovers over half a second: sky, then mist, then columns, then ground. WE ARE INSIDE THE PORTICO OF <<<image_4>>>, LOOKING OUT between two enormous columns, down the leaf-strewn steps and ACROSS THE OPEN FIELD TO THE SMALL PALE SHAPE OF <<<image_5>>> IN THE MIST. CHARLIE ENTERS FROM BEHIND THE CAMERA — he comes past us and runs away down the middle of frame, SEEN ONLY FROM BEHIND, soaked black, kicking the dead leaves up in a wake, BRD-1 ripping through high above him. THE CAMERA DOLLIES IN AFTER HIM — see DOLLY LAW.

5.00–8.60 — CUT TO GOD'S VIEW. STRAIGHT DOWN FROM SIX OR SEVEN METRES, TRACKING WITH HIM — see GOD'S-EYE LAW. HE IS OUT IN THE FIELD NOW, running through leaf litter and tall dry grass, BRD-1 crossing above him, then HE STOPS DEAD — see STOP LAW.

8.60–12.00 — CUT TO HIS FACE. A slow steady push in, close, low, never stopping. He stares up and forward at the building, breathing hard, WATER ALL OVER HIS FACE per <<<image_6>>> — see REACTION LAW. BRD-1 has come back and hovers soft-focus at his shoulder.

12.00–14.20 — STILL ON HIM: HE WIPES HIS FACE ONCE, hard, forehead to chin — see WIPE LAW.

14.20–17.00 — CUT TO WIDE, NOW ACROSS THE FIELD AND CLOSE TO IT. The full front of <<<image_5>>> fills the frame and HE IS TINY AT THE BOTTOM OF IT, walking away from camera toward the black opening through the dry grass — see APPROACH LAW and SCALE LAW. THE CAMERA CREEPS FORWARD BEHIND HIM THROUGHOUT, slow and dead level. IT ENDS WITH HIM STILL SHORT OF THE STEPS, STILL WALKING.

MOTION LAW — THE CAMERA IS MOVING IN EVERY FRAGMENT, FIRST FRAME TO LAST, BUT EVERY MOVE IS CONTROLLED AND PERFECTLY SMOOTH. NO LOCKED-OFF FRAME ANYWHERE, AND NO HANDHELD ANYWHERE. The fast fragments move fast; the quiet ones still creep — a slow push or drift, never a dead stop. Motorised, dead level, easing rather than jerking. 【THE SHAKING IS OVER — IT DOES NOT COME BACK】 FAIL TEST: IF ANY FRAGMENT IS A STATIC LOCKED FRAME, IT IS WRONG. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF ANY FRAGMENT WOBBLES OR READS AS HAND-HELD, IT IS WRONG.

DOLLY LAW — ELEGANT AND FAST, AND ABSOLUTELY ROCK STEADY. The camera tracks straight forward on rails at his back, dead level, no roll, no bob, no float. IT STARTS MOVING THE INSTANT THE IMAGE APPEARS and ACCELERATES, passing between the two foreground columns so they SWEEP OUT PAST THE EDGES OF FRAME and the field opens ahead of him. IT NEVER CATCHES HIM — he stays ahead of it and gets smaller. IT DOES NOT PAN, TILT, ZOOM OR SHAKE. FAIL TEST: IF THERE IS ANY HANDHELD MOVEMENT, WOBBLE OR SHAKE HERE, IT IS WRONG. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF THE MOVE IS SLOW AND DREAMY RATHER THAN FAST AND CLEAN, IT IS WRONG.

GOD'S-EYE LAW — THE CAMERA POINTS STRAIGHT DOWN AT THE GROUND, AT A PERFECT NINETY DEGREES, FROM SIX OR SEVEN METRES ABOVE HIM — ABOUT A SECOND-FLOOR WINDOW, NOT A DRONE. AT THAT HEIGHT HE READS CLEARLY: roughly a third of the frame's height, the plating on his shoulders and the shape of the rifle legible, individual leaves on the ground distinct.  THE ONLY THINGS IN FRAME ARE THE GROUND AND HIM ON IT — NO horizon, NO sky, NO tree line, NO building front, NO perspective on anything vertical. THE GROUND FILLS THE FRAME FLAT: pale cracked paving, coarse green weed, drifts of dead brown leaves, and TALL GOLDEN GRASS bending as he passes through it. WE SEE HIM FROM DIRECTLY OVERHEAD: shaved skull, two pauldrons, the rifle across him, boots swinging out either side, LEAVES AND GRASS BLOWING OUT BEHIND HIM. NO CAST SHADOW — the light is flat overcast. THE CAMERA TRACKS WITH HIM, sliding smoothly overhead at his speed, easing to a stop after he does. FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN SEE THE HORIZON, THE SKY, A BUILDING OR THE SIDE OF ANYTHING VERTICAL, THE ANGLE IS NOT STEEP ENOUGH AND IT IS WRONG. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF IT LOOKS LIKE A HIGH DRONE SHOT AND HE IS TINY, THE CAMERA IS TOO HIGH.

STOP LAW — THE STOP IS SUDDEN AND IT IS THE POINT OF THAT FRAGMENT. He runs at full speed and then, with no warning, HE PLANTS AND KILLS IT IN TWO STEPS — heels skidding in the wet grass, the body pulling up short, arms and rifle jolting, leaf litter thrown forward past him. THEN HE IS ABSOLUTELY STILL for a full beat. NOTHING CAUSED IT THAT WE CAN SEE — nothing enters frame, no sound cue, no threat. HE SIMPLY SEES SOMETHING AND STOPS. FAIL TEST: IF HE SLOWS GRADUALLY TO A HALT, IT IS WRONG — IT IS ABRUPT.

REACTION LAW — SMALL, HELD, AND NOT PERFORMED. The camera is close and PUSHES IN SLOWLY AND STEADILY on a dolly, never stopping, never wobbling. HE LOOKS UP AND PAST THE LENS at something enormous — the eyeline high and fixed. HIS FACE IS SOAKED per <<<image_6>>>: skin sheeting wet, water beaded on the shaved scalp and in the eyebrows, drips falling from the jaw. HIS CHEST IS HEAVING and his breathing is the loudest thing here. THE PERFORMANCE IS ONE THING: he is seeing something he did not expect and cannot measure. Give it in MICRO-GESTURE — the mouth a little open, the jaw setting, ONE SLOW BLINK, the eyes travelling upward as though following something tall, the smallest tightening around them. BANNED: gasping, mouth falling open in awe, eyebrows shooting up, head shaking, stepping back, hand to mouth, tears, smiling, nodding, speaking, any look into the lens. ONE CHANGE, THEN STILLNESS. FAIL TEST: IF A STRANGER COULD NAME THE EMOTION IN ONE WORD, IT IS TOO BIG.

WIPE LAW — ONE PASS, FUNCTIONAL, NOT TENDER. A gloved hand comes up and DRAGS DOWN OVER HIS FACE ONCE — palm flat, hard against the skin, forehead to chin, PUSHING THE WATER OFF IN A VISIBLE SHEET, deforming the features slightly, taking a smear of grey silt off his cheek. He BLINKS THE REST OUT and flicks the hand to shed it. THE FACE IS LEFT DAMP AND SHINING, NOT DRY. He does NOT wipe twice, does NOT rub his eyes, does NOT use a cloth or sleeve, does NOT wipe slowly. IT TAKES A SECOND, AND HIS EYES GO STRAIGHT BACK UP.

APPROACH LAW — CAUTIOUS, HEAVY AND SLOW, ABOUT WEIGHT RATHER THAN SNEAKING. He walks away from camera toward the black opening. EVERY STEP IS DELIBERATE AND SHORT, the front foot testing the ground before it takes the weight, the body upright and squared to the building, THE RIFLE HELD LOW IN BOTH HANDS — never raised, never shouldered, never aimed. HE STOPS ONCE, briefly, then goes on, head up, scanning the dark gap. HE IS NOT CROUCHING, NOT TIPTOEING, NOT HUGGING COVER, NOT DOING TACTICAL MOVEMENT, NOT LOOKING BACK. NO running, NO striding confidently. FAIL TEST: IF HE MOVES LIKE A SOLDIER CLEARING A ROOM, OR LIKE A CARTOON OF SOMEONE SNEAKING, IT IS WRONG. IT IS A TIRED, SOAKED BOY WALKING INTO SOMEWHERE HE DOES NOT WANT TO GO.

SCALE LAW — THE BUILDING IS COLOSSAL AND HE IS NOTHING. ONE COLUMN OF <<<image_5>>> IS MANY TIMES HIS HEIGHT. He occupies a small part of the bottom of frame and GETS SMALLER AS HE WALKS. The composition is symmetrical and frontal and allowed to be beautiful — but the camera is still creeping forward. FAIL TEST: IF HE READS AS THE SAME ORDER OF SIZE AS THE ARCHITECTURE, THE BUILDING IS FAR TOO SMALL.

LOCATION LAW — COLD, STILL, WET AND ABANDONED. Flat white overcast sky, no sun, no shadows. MIST IN THE AIR so the far wing and the tree line fade into it. Everything damp: dark staining, green algae down the columns, moss at the bases. DEAD BROWN LEAVES EVERYWHERE. STANDS OF TALL DRY GOLDEN GRASS across the field, waist to chest high, bending and rattling — DESATURATED AND DULL, the colour of old straw and wet hay, NEVER bright, NEVER glowing, NEVER warm. Bare black winter trees. NOTHING MAINTAINED IN YEARS — weeds through the paving, bramble on the steps — but NOTHING IS RUINED: no rubble, no collapse, no graffiti, no cars, no signage, no modern objects. IT IS EMPTY AND INTACT AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT WRONG.

BRD-1 LAW — IT IS WITH HIM AND IT IS TINY. 12 CM FROM CLAWS TO CREST — robin-sized, its whole body would fit in his closed fist. NEVER crow-sized, NEVER hawk-sized, NEVER head-sized, NEVER changing size. IT FLIES LIKE A SMALL FAST MACHINE, NOT A BIG BIRD: a quick shallow blurred wingbeat too fast to count. IT NEVER GLIDES, NEVER soars, NEVER banks like a hawk.

WHILE HE RUNS IT IS HIGH ABOVE HIM AND AHEAD — well over his head, out in front, ranging, crossing frame in fast straight bursts with hard changes of direction. IN THE TOP-DOWN FRAGMENT IT PASSES THROUGH FRAME ABOVE HIM AS A SMALL DARK SHAPE, closer to the lens than he is and therefore blurred. WHEN HE STOPS, IT COMES BACK TO HIM — dropping out of the air fast, decelerating hard, and SETTLING INTO A HOVER AT HIS SHOULDER, level with his head, holding station while he stares. It is the only thing in frame still moving. IT DOES NOT LAND OR PERCH. IN THE FACE FRAGMENT IT IS OUT OF FOCUS BESIDE HIM OR OUT OF FRAME — IT NEVER STEALS THE CLOSE-UP. FAIL TEST: IF IT FLIES AT HIS SHOULDER WHILE HE IS RUNNING, IT IS WRONG.

CAST — ONE BOY AND ONE SMALL MACHINE. No second figure, no creature, no crowd, no other bird, nothing in the doorway or windows, nothing moving in the mist, no vehicles.

PRODUCTION FRAME — a controlled set sequence: a costumed actor kneeling in shallow water on a flooded tunnel set, lifting a prop rifle out of the water, filmed close by a handheld operator. SHOT LAW — ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE, FIVE SECONDS, NO CUTS. THE SHOT DOES NOT END ON THE PICKUP — HE GRABS THE RIFLE AND THEN HE GETS UP, AND BOTH ARE IN THIS SHOT. No cutaways, no inserts, no second angle, no dissolves, no fades, no speed ramps, NO SLOW MOTION, no freeze frames. The camera never leaves the water and the hands. THE WHOLE SHOT IS ONE UNBROKEN PIECE OF HANDHELD VIDEO.

FRAMING LAW — EXTREME CLOSE-UP. THIS IS AS TIGHT AS A SHOT GETS. AT THE START THE FRAME IS TWO GLOVES, A STRIP OF FOREARM PLATING AND BLACK WATER, AND NOTHING ELSE — knuckles, seams, tendons, wet material, filling the whole picture. FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN SEE HIS FACE, OR IF THE SHOT EVER READS AS A WIDE OR MEDIUM SHOT OF A MAN CROUCHING OR STANDING, IT IS WRONG.

THE ACTION — HE GRABS IT AND HE GETS UP.

0.00–1.00 — THE HANDS ARE ALREADY IN THE WATER, submerged to the wrist and moving fast, SEARCHING BLIND. The black surface churns, leaves and scum swirling, nothing readable underneath. One glove breaks the surface and goes back under. HE IS NOT CALM AND HE IS NOT LOOKING — the hands are hunting.

SPLASH LAW — THE LENS GETS HIT, AND IT STAYS HIT. THIS IS NOT A CLEAN CAMERA. THREE SEPARATE STRIKES AT MINIMUM: first a hard SPATTER as the hands work, then A FULL SLAB OF WATER AS THE RIFLE COMES OUT that WASHES ACROSS THE GLASS AND HALF-BLINDS THE PICTURE FOR A BEAT, then more thrown up as he stands. GRIP LAW — IT IS URGENT AND CLUMSY, NOT COOL. WEAPON LAW — IT IS ONLY EVER CARRIED. THE MUZZLE NEVER POINTS AT THE LENS and never sweeps across it. FORMAT LAW — THIS IS NOT FILM. IT IS SHOT ON A CANON XL1: A 1998 STANDARD-DEFINITION 3-CCD MiniDV CAMCORDER, HELD IN ONE HAND. THE AUTO-FOCUS IS LOST FOR MOST OF THIS. BANNED OUTRIGHT: anything that reads as cinema. The operator is crouched in the water on one knee with a light plastic camcorder in one hand, off balance, breathing hard, AND HE HAS LOST CONTROL OF IT. At this focal distance every tiny movement of his hand throws the whole picture across the frame.

PRODUCTION FRAME — a controlled set sequence: a costumed sixteen-year-old actor runs through a flooded tunnel set with a small puppet drone, takes a rehearsed, padded fall into shallow water and gets up, filmed guerrilla-style by an operator running with him. FORMAT LAW — THIS IS NOT FILM. IT IS SHOT ON A CANON XL1: A 1998 STANDARD-DEFINITION 3-CCD MiniDV CAMCORDER, HELD IN ONE HAND BY A MAN RUNNING. Cheap, light, ugly — a consumer video camera in a dark tunnel with the gain cranked to the top, and it is failing.

IT MUST READ AS MiniDV TAPE: STANDARD DEFINITION AND SOFT, a mushy image blown up past its resolution. INTERLACED 60i WITH VISIBLE FIELD COMBING — on every fast move the picture SHREDS INTO HORIZONTAL SAWTOOTH TEARS along his edges. DV COMPRESSION BLOCKING in the shadows, the dark breaking into crawling squares. CRANKED GAIN: the blacks full of BOILING COLOURED CHROMA NOISE. SMEARED 4:1:1 COLOUR bleeding behind the edges. VERTICAL CCD SMEAR off the portal. HIGHLIGHTS CLIP FLAT AND HARD — no roll-off, no glow, just dead white holes. THE AUTO-IRIS PUMPS every time the bright end swings in. THE AUTO-FOCUS HUNTS AND FAILS. Cheap zoom flare and colour fringing. THE ODD TAPE DROPOUT.

BANNED OUTRIGHT: anything that reads as cinema. NO FILM GRAIN, NO halation, NO gate weave, NO film stock, NO anamorphic, NO cinematic motion blur, NO shallow depth of field, NO 4K sharpness, NO HDR, NO polished grade, NO glossy CGI sheen, NO drone smoothness, NO beauty lighting. IF IT LOOKS EXPENSIVE OR CINEMATIC, IT IS WRONG. IT SHOULD LOOK LIKE A TAPE SOMEBODY FOUND.

EVERY CUT LANDS MID-MOVEMENT — never on a still frame, never on a clean composition, never at the end of an action. THE CUTS DO NOT MATCH: screen direction reverses, space skips forward. THE GEOGRAPHY SHOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE TO HOLD ONTO. NO dissolves, NO fades, NO wipes, NO flash frames, NO speed ramps, NO slow motion, NO freeze frames. FAIL TEST: IF ANY ONE ANGLE RUNS LONGER THAN TWO SECONDS, THE SEQUENCE IS WRONG. 【THE FALL IS NEVER IN SLOW MOTION】

THE OPERATOR'S BOOT GOES OUT FROM UNDER HIM AND THE PICTURE LURCHES SIDEWAYS. THE CAMERA IS STRUCK — by a vine, a shoulder, the wall — and knocked clean off its aim.

PRODUCTION FRAME — a controlled film-set sequence: a costumed sixteen-year-old actor running through a flooded tunnel set with a small puppet drone, filmed guerrilla-style by an operator running with him. NOTHING IS FIRED, nobody is hurt, no violence, no injury, no blood, and nothing is chasing him in frame.

FORMAT LAW — SUPER 16MM FILM, HANDHELD, RUN AND GUN, PUSHED AND FILTHY. This is a documentary news cameraman with a small 16mm camera on his shoulder, running for his own life, in the dark, with no lights and no time to think about the frame.

IT MUST READ AS FILM: SUPER 16 NEGATIVE, HEAVY CRAWLING GRAIN boiling in the shadows, GATE WEAVE, real 180-degree SHUTTER MOTION BLUR on every fast move — smooth organic smear, never a digital stutter. HALATION BLOOMING off the bright portal, the highlight glowing and spreading rather than clipping flat. MILKY LIFTED BLACKS. Dust, hairs and dirt in the gate. The odd splice bump at a cut, like a workprint.

AND IT IS UNDEREXPOSED AND PUSHED, WHICH IS WHERE THE GRIT COMES FROM: there is not enough light for the stock, the negative is thin and the lab has pushed it hard. THE GRAIN IS ENORMOUS AND ALIVE, especially in the dark two-thirds of the frame; the shadows are muddy and swimming; the contrast is harsh and ugly; the colour has almost fallen out, leaving a cold sour near-monochrome image with a dirty green-grey cast.

THE LENS IS CHEAP AND FAST: a wide 16mm zoom, soft in the corners, breathing on focus moves, flaring milkily when the portal swings into it. FOCUS IS PULLED BY THE OPERATOR AND HE IS LOSING — it hunts, arrives late, racks to the wrong thing, and whole fragments are simply out of focus.

BANNED OUTRIGHT: anything digital or clean. NO video look, NO camcorder look, NO interlace combing, NO compression blocking, NO 4K sharpness, NO HDR, NO polished grade, NO glossy CGI sheen, NO drone smoothness, NO beauty lighting, NO composed pretty frame. IF IT LOOKS SLICK, IT IS WRONG. It should look like film shot in a hurry, in the dark, by somebody running.

CUT LAW — THIS IS NOT ONE SHOT. IT IS EIGHT SEPARATE FRAGMENTS AND THEY ARE LISTED BELOW. A HARD STRAIGHT CUT EVERY TWO SECONDS, SEVEN CUTS IN TOTAL, AND THE CAMERA IS IN A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PLACE AFTER EVERY ONE. There is no master, no establishing shot, no coverage. EVERY CUT LANDS MID-STRIDE, MID-WHIP, MID-BLUR — never on a still frame, never on a clean composition, never at the end of an action. THE CUTS DO NOT MATCH AND ARE NOT MEANT TO: screen direction reverses, space skips forward, a fragment can seem to repeat a moment we just saw. THE GEOGRAPHY SHOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE TO HOLD ONTO — only that he is running, that it is dark, and that the light ahead is getting bigger. NO dissolves, NO fades, NO wipes, NO flash frames, NO speed ramps, NO slow motion, NO freeze frames, NO stylised transitions. FAIL TEST: IF ANY ONE ANGLE RUNS LONGER THAN TWO SECONDS, THE SEQUENCE IS WRONG.

THE EIGHT FRAGMENTS — FOLLOW THIS ORDER AND USE NO OTHERS.

0.00–2.00 — DOWN IN THE WATER AT ANKLE HEIGHT, the surface slapping and half-flooding the lens, HIS BOOTS SMASHING PAST over the top of the frame in sheets of spray, the portal a small white smear far away between them. The camera is wrenched upward at the end and the picture tears into smear.

2.00–4.00 — BEHIND HIM AND FAR TOO CLOSE, the back of his skull and one pauldron filling half the picture, the operator gaining and losing ground so HE SURGES BIGGER AND SMALLER, the portal flaring milkily past his shoulder.

4.00–6.00 — RUNNING BACKWARDS AHEAD OF HIM, wide, HE CHARGES STRAIGHT AT THE LENS and nearly reaches it. The operator's own footing goes and the frame drops, swings and rolls hard over.

6.00–8.00 — FROM THE SIDE LEDGE, LOW AND TILTED FORTY DEGREES OVER, the rusted rail and black water raking the foreground. HE TEARS PAST LEFT TO RIGHT and is gone before the fragment ends, LEAVING AN EMPTY BLACK TUNNEL for the last beat.

8.00–10.00 — FROM BEHIND A CURTAIN OF HANGING VINES, roots and ivy whipping across the lens. HE PUNCHES THROUGH THEM toward the camera, something hits the body of the camera and the frame is knocked sideways.

10.00–12.00 — POINTED UP AT THE ROOF, THE RIBBED ARCHES STROBING PAST OVERHEAD, BRD-1 RIPPING ACROSS THE FRAME AS A BLACK SMEAR. The camera falls back down and hunts to find him again, focus arriving late.

12.00–13.50 — HELD OUT AT ARM'S LENGTH AND ROLLING, ON TOP OF HIM, UNREADABLE FOR THE FIRST FEW FRAMES before it resolves into part of his shoulder and skull. THE PORTAL IS NOW HUGE AND BURNING behind him.

13.50–15.00 — INTO THE LIGHT. He runs straight at the portal and it opens up and swallows the frame. THE PICTURE BLOWS OUT TO PURE WHITE — see WHITE LAW — AND THE SHOT ENDS THERE.

WHITE LAW — THE LAST THING WE SEE IS FULL WHITE, EDGE TO EDGE. As he reaches the portal the film cannot hold the exposure: the daylight floods the gate, halation eats outward from the arch until it consumes the whole picture, his silhouette is burned away from the edges inward, and THE FRAME GOES COMPLETELY, UNIFORMLY WHITE and stays that way to the last frame. It is BLOWN-OUT FILM, not a white card and not a fade — the grain and halation still boiling right up to the moment nothing is left. HOLD PURE WHITE FOR THE FINAL BEAT. FAIL TEST: IF THE SHOT ENDS ON THE TUNNEL, ON HIS BACK, ON DARKNESS, OR ON ANYTHING THAT IS NOT A FULL WHITE FRAME, THE ENDING IS WRONG. Nothing appears in the white — no figure, no shape, no text, no logo.

NO BODY-MOUNTED CAMERA — THE CAMERA IS NEVER ATTACHED TO HIM. NOT ONCE, NOT BRIEFLY, NOT IN ANY FRAGMENT. THE LAST VERSIONS WERE FULL OF THIS AND IT IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST FAILURE TO AVOID. There is no chest rig, no body rig, no harness, no arm mounted out in front of him, no mount on the armour or rifle. THAT LOOK — WHERE HE STAYS LOCKED AND CENTRED AND THE SAME SIZE WHILE THE WHOLE TUNNEL SWINGS AND ROCKS BEHIND HIM — IS BANNED. THE CAMERA IS ALWAYS A SEPARATE PERSON with his own footing, his own stumble and his own bad luck: HE SLIDES AROUND THE FRAME, drifts to the edges, is cut in half, is lost and found, and CHANGES SIZE constantly as the operator gains and loses ground. FAIL TEST: IF HE IS CENTRED, THE SAME SIZE AND STEADY WHILE THE BACKGROUND SWINGS BEHIND HIM, THE SHOT IS WRONG. Nothing is composed. Nothing is centred.

SHAKE LAW — MORE VIOLENT THAN ANY HANDHELD YOU HAVE EVER MADE, AND THEN MORE AGAIN. IT CANNOT BE OVERDONE AND IT HAS BEEN TOO TAME EVERY SINGLE TIME SO FAR. A man is sprinting flat out through shin-deep water with a 16mm camera barely held on his shoulder, and he is losing the fight with it.

A HARD VERTICAL SLAM ON EVERY SINGLE FOOTFALL — and he is sprinting, so THAT IS THREE OR FOUR VIOLENT JOLTS EVERY SECOND, the whole picture dropping a good fraction of the frame height and snapping back. THE HORIZON ROLLS THROUGH TWENTY, THIRTY, FORTY DEGREES AND SOMETIMES PAST IT, and is never level for more than a moment. THE FRAME SWINGS OFF HIM ENTIRELY, TRAVELLING A WHOLE FRAME WIDTH OR MORE, then WHIPS BACK, overshoots, corrects, overshoots again. SUDDEN LURCHES as the operator's boot goes out from under him. THE CAMERA IS KNOCKED — brushed by a vine, jolted by a shoulder, half dropped and caught.

EVERYTHING SMEARS: on the fast swings the picture is pure horizontal streak for several frames at a time, unreadable, the arches and the portal drawn out into bands of light. WATER HITS THE LENS and sits on it in fat beads. THE OPERATOR'S BREATH AND EFFORT ARE IN THE FRAME as a constant heavy judder under everything else.

IT IS ILLEGIBLE FOR STRETCHES AND THAT IS CORRECT — SOME OF IT SHOULD BE GENUINELY HARD TO WATCH. FAIL TEST: IF ANY HALF-SECOND OF THIS COULD PASS FOR A STEADICAM, A GIMBAL, A DRONE, A DOLLY OR A STABILISED SHOT, IT IS FAR TOO SMOOTH. SECOND FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN COMFORTABLY READ THE WHOLE FRAME AT ANY POINT, THE SHAKE IS TOO SMALL. But it is A RUNNING HUMAN BEING, never a machine: irregular, uneven, different sized movements at different speeds layered over each other — NEVER a rhythmic wobble, NEVER a looping shake cycle, NEVER a uniform buzz, NEVER a stylised camera-shake filter, NEVER a video-game headbob.

SILHOUETTE LAW — HE IS A BLACK SHAPE AND NOTHING MORE. He runs toward the only light, so we are always on the dark side of him. HE IS FLAT BLACK: NO face, NO eyes, NO skin tone, NO colour on the armour, NO red, NO white, NO YGGD marks, NO detail on the rifle. He reads ONLY as an OUTLINE — round shaved skull, high collar, the hard line of the pauldrons, legs driving, rifle carried low. WE READ HIM BY EDGE, NOT SURFACE: the bright water beneath him, the blown portal ahead, a thin wet rim of light along one shoulder. NOTHING FILLS IN, and in the darkest fragments HE IS BARELY THERE AT ALL. FAIL TEST: IF YOU CAN SEE HIS FACE OR THE RED AND WHITE OF THE SUIT, THE SHOT IS WRONG.

THE ACTION — A DEAD SPRINT FOR FIFTEEN SECONDS. HE IS NOT JOGGING, NOT LOPING, NOT RUNNING STEADILY — HE IS FLAT OUT, AT HIS ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM, AND HE IS NEARLY OUT OF CONTROL. THE LAST VERSION WAS FAR TOO SLOW AND THAT IS THE FAILURE TO AVOID.

WHAT MAKES IT READ AS FAST IS THE WORLD, NOT THE LEGS: THE TUNNEL RIPS PAST HIM. The vaulted arches band overhead SEVERAL EVERY SECOND, strobing by; the ledges tear past; the vines come at the camera and are gone; the walls streak and smear. AND THE BODY IS AT FULL TILT: HIGH CADENCE, feet turning over fast, strides long and hard; the body PITCHED FORWARD, almost falling and catching itself every step; the free arm driving; the armour hammering; his weight going into every footfall so the water EXPLODES around his boots in sheets, spray hitting the lens.

FAIL TEST: IF YOU COULD KEEP PACE WITH HIM AT A JOG, HE IS FAR TOO SLOW. IF THE BACKGROUND IS DRIFTING PAST RATHER THAN TEARING PAST, HE IS FAR TOO SLOW. He should look like he is about to lose his footing and does not.

HE NEVER STOPS, never slows, never looks back, never trips, never turns, never speaks. NOTHING CHASES HIM AND NOTHING IS SHOWN BEHIND HIM. THE ONLY PROGRESSION IS THE LIGHT — the portal small and distant at the start, huge and blinding by the end, until it takes the whole frame.

BRD-1 — FLYING WITH HIM, FRANTICALLY, AND IT IS TINY. It flies around him at roughly head height, never in one place — see ZIGZAG LAW. IT IS 12 CM FROM CLAWS TO CREST — robin-sized, roughly as tall as the distance from his chin to his eyebrows, its whole body would fit in his closed fist. NEVER crow-sized, NEVER hawk-sized, NEVER head-sized, NEVER changing size.

IT FLIES LIKE A SMALL FAST MACHINE, NOT A BIG BIRD: a QUICK, SHALLOW, BLURRED WINGBEAT far too fast to count, the wings a flicker either side of a level body. IT NEVER GLIDES, NEVER soars, NEVER flaps slowly, NEVER banks like a hawk, NEVER hovers.

ZIGZAG LAW — IT DOES NOT FLY BESIDE HIM. IT IS FRANTIC AND IT NEVER HOLDS A LINE. 【NEVER A WINGMAN】 it does NOT hold station off his shoulder, does NOT pace him, does NOT travel in a straight line with him, does NOT stay in one part of the frame.

IT MOVES IN HARD ZIGZAGS: sharp, sudden changes of direction with almost no curve between them — a fast burst one way, a snap turn, a fast burst back the other way, up, down, diagonally, and again. THE TURNS ARE ABRUPT, like a bat or a swift or a panicking bird trapped indoors, not the smooth swooping arcs of a big bird. Between bursts it stalls for a fraction of a second, flutters, then rips off in a new direction.

IT USES THE WHOLE TUNNEL: cutting across in front of him and behind him, up to the roof and back down, skimming the water, swerving out to a wall and tearing back, crossing right in front of the lens, left of frame in one fragment and right in the next. IT IS EVERYWHERE AND NOWHERE — a small thing in a panic that is somehow still keeping up.

FAIL TEST: IF ITS PATH COULD BE DRAWN AS A SMOOTH LINE, OR IF IT SITS ALONGSIDE HIS HEAD FOR MORE THAN HALF A SECOND, THE FLIGHT IS WRONG. Every second of its flight should contain at least one hard change of direction.

IT IS ALSO A BLACK SILHOUETTE — no red, no white, no glowing eyes, no lights. THE CAMERA CATCHES IT BY ACCIDENT AS MUCH AS ON PURPOSE: in one fragment a smear tearing across the picture, in another simply not there. FAIL TEST: IF IT LOOKS LIKE A LARGE BIRD FLYING ALONGSIDE A MAN, IT IS FAR TOO BIG.

LIGHT LAW — ONE SOURCE, DEAD AHEAD. All light comes from THE BRIGHT PORTAL at the far end: flat overcast daylight, cold and colourless, BLOWN OUT AND HALATING on the film, growing across the sequence until it takes everything. The water carries its reflection back down the tunnel. NO lamps, NO torches, NO beams, NO helmet light, NO glow on the armour, NO glowing eyes, NO sun, NO god rays, NO coloured light. Everything else is MUDDY, GRAIN-BOILING, LIFTED BLACK — never a clean digital black.

CAST — ONE BOY AND ONE SMALL MACHINE. No second figure, no creature, no other people, nothing behind him and nothing in the portal.

PERFORMANCE LAW — HE IS FURIOUS AND ALMOST NONE OF IT SHOWS. THE PROBLEM TO AVOID IS AN ACTOR PLAYING ANGER. There is no shout, no snarl, no grimace, no head shake, no eye roll, no jaw clench, no fist, no strike at the weapon, no throwing anything, no punching the air. Everything is INWARD AND MUSCULAR AND SMALL.

PICK A FEW OF THESE AND NO MORE: a single hard exhale down the nose; the corner of the mouth pulling back a few millimetres and releasing; a fast flick of the eyes down and back up; one blink held a fraction too long; the muscle at the hinge of the jaw moving once and stopping; a swallow that never completes; the head dropping a centimetre and coming back. THE WORD ITSELF IS THE RELEASE and it is under-played almost to nothing — he does not project it, he breathes it out.

NOTHING ESCALATES: the frustration does not build, does not peak, does not resolve. It is the same at 0:05 as at 0:01. The only real change across the shot is that he stops looking and starts moving. AVOID THE SYNTHETIC TELLS: perfectly smooth eased facial motion, symmetrical movement on both sides of the face, micro-expressions that loop or repeat, a face morphing between states, blinking on a regular rhythm, eyes gliding smoothly instead of flicking. HUMAN EYES MOVE IN FAST JUMPS AND THEN HOLD. If it looks like acting, it is wrong.

PRODUCTION FRAME — a controlled film-set sequence: a distant puppet creature seen only as a blur in a far doorway, watched through a fictional prop optic. A blank round is fired HIGH INTO THE TUNNEL ROOF and IT MISSES THE CREATURE COMPLETELY — nothing living is hit, nobody is harmed, no injury and no blood, and the creature leaves unhurt.

SHOT — ONE CONTINUOUS FIVE-SECOND SHOT, INSIDE THE OPTIC THE ENTIRE TIME — see LOCKED-IN LAW. NO CUTS, no second angle, no insert, no exterior view at any point. We NEVER see the shooter, the weapon or the muzzle — only this display. THE SUBJECT OF THE SHOT IS THE CREATURE LEAVING, and everything else is there to make that beat land.

WHAT HAPPENS — THREE BEATS AND NOTHING ELSE. 0:00–0:01.5 ON AIM: the optic is up at magnification on the far end of the tunnel, the small bright arch blown white-hot at the centre of the aperture, and inside it a SMALL DARK BLUR working at the wall. THE WHOLE PICTURE IS SWINGING AND JOLTING with an unseen body — this is a boy who can barely hold a heavy weapon up, and the bright arch travels around the aperture the entire time. See SHAKE LAW.

0:01.5 — THE SHOT. No warning of any kind. See SHOT LAW and SHAKE LAW.

0:01.5–0:04 — SHE IS GONE. THIS IS THE BODY OF THE SHOT AND MOST OF ITS RUNNING TIME. As the image wallows back toward aim we get two or three broken glimpses: she is at the wall, then already far down the tunnel, then nothing. See EXIT LAW.

0:04–0:05 — THE EMPTY ARCH. The optic is still swimming and still trying to find the aim. The far arch sits there blazing and empty, dust drifting down from the roof, the water disturbed. NOTHING ELSE HAPPENS AND NOTHING ELSE IS SHOWN. Cut while the picture is still moving.

LOCKED-IN LAW — WE NEVER LEAVE THE OPTIC, AND THE END OF THE SHOT IS NOT AN EVENT. THIS HAS ALREADY FAILED: the last version broke out of the scope and cut to an exterior over-the-shoulder view of the weapon and the jungle. THAT IS THE FAILURE TO AVOID. ALL FIVE SECONDS ARE INSIDE THE DISPLAY, from the first frame to the last.

NEVER SHOW: the weapon from outside, a barrel, a scope body, a rail, a suppressor, a magazine, a sling; a hand, an arm, a glove, a shoulder, a cheek, a face or any part of a person; the jungle, the towers, the water or the channel seen from outside the optic; a third-person angle of any kind; a wide shot; a reverse; a pull-out; a reveal of where the shooter is standing. THE APERTURE AND ITS BLACK SURROUND ARE IN FRAME FOR THE WHOLE SHOT.

AND NOTHING NEW HAPPENS AT THE END: NO lifting the gun, NO lowering the gun, NO swinging the view up to the sky or the canopy, NO panning off, NO searching for her, NO second target, NO reload, NO looking away, NO tilt, NO whip, NO settle onto anything else. AFTER SHE IS GONE THE OPTIC SIMPLY KEEPS WALLOWING ON THE EMPTY ARCH UNTIL THE CUT. FAIL TEST: IF ANY FRAME SHOWS THE WORLD FROM OUTSIDE THE SCOPE, THE SHOT IS WRONG.

SHOT LAW — THE ROUND GOES HIGH AND HITS THE ROOF. There is NO wind-up, NO breath held on cue, NO reticle settling, NO cue of any kind — it simply happens on the first beat. THE ROUND STRIKES THE CONCRETE CEILING OF THE TUNNEL, well above her head and clearly ABOVE THE TOP OF THE BRIGHT ARCH: a hard burst of pale dust off the underside of the roof and grit raining down through the light. THERE IS A WIDE, OBVIOUS GAP OF EMPTY AIR between that impact up on the ceiling and her body down at the floor, and the two are never in the same part of the frame. SHE IS NEVER HIT AND MUST NEVER LOOK HIT: no dust off her, no jolt, no stagger, no stumble, no flinch, no fall, no collapse, no blood, no wound. ONE SHOT ONLY — not two, not a burst, not automatic.

SHAKE LAW — THE WHOLE SHOT IS VIOLENTLY UNSTEADY FROM THE FIRST FRAME TO THE LAST, AND THE RECOIL ON TOP OF THAT IS ENORMOUS. DO NOT UNDERPLAY EITHER. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT THING ABOUT THE CAMERA.

BEFORE THE SHOT IT IS ALREADY BAD — far worse than ordinary handheld. At this magnification every millimetre of body movement is enormous on the glass: A FAST HARD TREMOR from the pulse running constantly under everything, A WIDE SLOW SWIM on the breathing that carries the bright arch well off centre and back, THE AIM CONSTANTLY WANDERING OFF and being HAULED BACK IN LATE, OVERCORRECTED, AND WANDERING AGAIN, and SUDDEN JOLTS as his stance shifts and his footing slips in the mud. THE BRIGHT ARCH IS ALMOST NEVER IN THE SAME PLACE FOR TWO FRAMES RUNNING — it travels around the aperture the whole time, sometimes sliding close to the edge of the picture before being dragged back. He can barely hold it.

FAIL TEST FOR THE OPENING: IF THE FRAMING LOOKS COMPOSED, OR THE ARCH SITS QUIETLY NEAR THE CENTRE, OR ANY HALF-SECOND OF IT COULD PASS FOR A LOCKED-OFF SHOT, THE SHAKE IS FAR TOO SMALL. IT IS NEVER STILL FOR A SINGLE FRAME. But it is A BODY FAILING TO HOLD A HEAVY WEAPON, not a machine: irregular, uneven, with different sized movements at different speeds layered over each other — NEVER a rhythmic wobble, NEVER a looping shake cycle, NEVER a uniform buzz, NEVER a stylised camera-shake effect.

ON THE SHOT the whole aperture is SLAMMED: the image FLUNG UP AND HARD OFF TO ONE SIDE, travelling a large fraction of the frame's width in one frame, so that FOR TWO OR THREE FRAMES THE TUNNEL IS NOT IN THE PICTURE AT ALL and we are looking at smeared black and concrete. It doubles, tears and motion-blurs, the amber blooming. THEN IT DOES NOT SIMPLY RETURN — it falls back, OVERSHOOTS PAST TARGET THE OTHER WAY, comes back and overshoots again smaller, with a second hard jolt a beat later, and it goes on wallowing and swimming for the rest of the shot. IT NEVER SETTLES.

AND IT DOES NOT CALM DOWN AFTERWARDS. For the rest of the shot the picture keeps swinging, drifting and jolting, the aim hunting for the arch and never quite holding it, and IT IS STILL MOVING HARD ON THE LAST FRAME. THE OVERLAY STAYS WELDED TO THE GLASS THROUGHOUT while the picture under it is thrown around — that mismatch is what makes the movement read as huge. FAIL TEST: IF THE FRAMING STAYS RECOGNISABLE ALL THE WAY THROUGH, THE SHAKE IS FAR TOO SMALL. Brutal and disorienting, but NEVER a stylised shake effect, NEVER a rumble, NEVER a vibration, NEVER an earthquake wobble.

EXIT LAW — SHE DOES NOT FADE AND WE DO NOT WATCH HER RUN. THE LAST ATTEMPT FADED HER OUT AND GAVE HER AN ODD RUNNING ANIMATION; BOTH ARE THE FAILURE TO AVOID. She is SOLID, OPAQUE AND FULLY DARK in every single frame she appears in, right up to the frame where she is not in the picture at all.

SHE IS NEVER SEEN LEAVING — SHE IS SIMPLY SOMEWHERE ELSE, AND THEN NOWHERE. THE RECOIL SHAKE DOES THE WORK: the picture is flung off her, and WE ONLY GET TWO OR THREE DISCONNECTED GLIMPSES as it swings back past the arch, each one a hard jump with no continuity between them —

GLIMPSE ONE: she is at the wall where she was.
GLIMPSE TWO, a fraction of a second later: SHE IS ALREADY DEEP IN THE TUNNEL, well past where she was, much further away, caught mid-motion and heavily smeared.
GLIMPSE THREE: THE ARCH IS EMPTY. Nothing there. Just the blazing daylight and dust drifting down from the roof.

THOSE GLIMPSES ARE THE POINT OF THE WHOLE SHOT — give them room and let them play out across the middle of it, rather than rushing past them to get somewhere else. There is nowhere else to get to.
