# CHARLIE — PART 3G — 20s — THE WAVE

*One unbroken shot. Low medium close-up of his face, he turns, the camera opens out as the air moves. 240fps. The camera swings behind him and follows him down the aisle — the creature tumbling ahead of him, his reach, the catch — then real time returns and he passes through the wall into daylight.*

---

# **THERE IS NO CUT. ONE SHOT, TWENTY SECONDS.**

One camera, one continuous piece of time. **The frame never blinks.** No cuts, no hidden cuts, no match cuts, no jump cuts, no whip-pan transitions, no dissolves, no fades, no black frames, no cutaways, no second angle.

**The timings below are moments inside ONE take, not a shot list.** If the result contains more than one shot, it is wrong.

**The camera is locked to Charlie for the entire shot.** **He is in frame in every single frame of the twenty seconds** — the camera travels around him and with him and never once looks somewhere he is not. **The speed changes are in-camera ramps, not edits. A change of speed is never a change of shot.**

---

# **THE SPEED**

**REAL TIME — 0.0 to 2.4s.** Normal speed, ordinary human motion. His face, his turn.

**RAMP DOWN — 2.4 to 3.0s.** **The world decelerates hard over six tenths of a second** as the camera opens out, motion stretching and then locking into crystalline slow motion. **A hard visible gear change, not a fade.**

**240 FRAMES PER SECOND — 3.0 to 16.2s.** **Thirteen seconds at roughly ten times slower than life.** **Every page, splinter and grain of dust is a separate readable object with its own trajectory.** No smearing, no strobing — **the clarity at this speed is the spectacle.**

**RAMP UP — 16.2 to 16.5s.** **Three tenths in which everything accelerates back to real time**, drifting debris ripping into streaks.

**REAL TIME — 16.5 to 20.0s.** Full speed. The wall, the light.

**Both ramps happen inside the shot with the camera running.** **No cut, no dissolve, no stutter, no strobe, no frame blending, no digital speed artefacts.**

---

# **PHYSICS — THE LAST ATTEMPT GOT THIS WRONG**

**Everything here is heavy and everything obeys gravity. Nothing floats.**

**A fast rush of air comes up the aisle from behind him and carries him with it.** **He travels one way — forward down the aisle, the direction he is already facing — for the whole shot.** **Never backward, never sideways, never toward the ceiling.**

**His path is low and flat and it is falling the whole time.** His feet leave the floor early; **he rises no more than his own height, and from the top of that he is descending** — a fast shallow downward arc toward the wall. **He never hangs, never hovers, never levels out, never gains height a second time.**

**His body is loose and his arms are not.** **Torso and legs hang back behind the direction of travel**, boots trailing, head low. **Only his arms act.** **No rubber-limbed flailing, no spinning like a doll, no gymnastics, no heroic pose, no wire-work grace.** His rotation is **slow and slight** — a lazy quarter turn onto one side across the whole flight, nothing more.

**The creature travels at very nearly his speed, alongside and slightly ahead of him** — **that is the only reason a catch is possible.** It is **not sitting still in the air waiting for him**, not slower, not faster: **it is falling on the same path**, tumbling.

**All the debris does the same.** **Everything in the air travels the same way at once — up the aisle, with him — and everything is also falling.** Pages, boards, books, plaster and ash **arc and descend**; nothing hangs still, nothing drifts backward, nothing rises once it has begun to fall, **nothing is weightless.** **Heavy things fall faster and further than light things** — timber and books drop out of frame while paper stays up longest.

**And the camera obeys the same rules**: it travels forward down the aisle at his speed, **sinking as he sinks.** It never hovers, never rises smoothly, never glides on rails.

**If any object in this shot appears to hang motionless in the air, the physics have failed.**

# THE TWENTY SECONDS

## **REAL TIME**

**0.0–1.4s — his face.** **Medium close-up from below, looking up at him.** Filthy, dust-caked, the earbud in his right ear at the left of frame. **His eyes are down**, on something at his feet we cannot see. **He does almost nothing** — the smallest tightening, one blink. A faint red light from below on the underside of his chin.

**1.4–2.4s — the turn.** **Sudden, fast, animal.** He **whips around away from it**, shoulder leading, head last, **his face sweeping out of frame** — throwing dust off himself — and in the same movement **his arms fold in and clamp the creature against his chest**, shoulders hunching, chin dropping, **his whole body curling into a shell around it.**

## **THE RAMP DOWN — 2.4–3.0s**

**The world decelerates hard** as the camera begins to pull back. On the last frames of the ramp **the picture behind him goes white.**

## **240 FRAMES PER SECOND**

**3.0–4.4s — THE AIR MOVES, and the frame opens.** **A single hard white flash** low behind him, brief and dirty, **blowing the exposure out for a few frames** and reducing him to a black silhouette — **and the camera is racing backwards and up, the frame opening into the full aisle.** Then it arrives: **an opaque front of dust, ash and paper**, **the stacks on both sides splitting and throwing timber**, **hundreds of books coming off the shelves at once.** The camera is punched sideways.

**4.4–6.5s — HE IS CARRIED, and we go behind him.** **The rush reaches him and he goes forward off his feet**, low and fast down the aisle, **and the camera arcs around him onto his back.** **The armour opens as we arrive there** — plates lifting and peeling outward, fittings shearing, webbing and hoses pulling free, the underlayer stripping back, **the whole rear of the suit coming apart around him.**

**6.5–9.5s — THE AISLE, and the creature.** **From behind him now**, the corridor running away ahead, **and this is the most beautiful part of the shot.** **Thousands of pages** turning individually in the air; **whole books tumbling end over end**; **long splinters of shelf timber spinning**; plaster, ash and grit filling every part of the frame; **everything travelling forward with him and falling as it goes.**

**And ahead of him, revealed over his shoulder: the creature.** **It has come out of his arms and it is out there in the air in front of him**, tumbling slowly, **completely intact and perfectly fine, small against everything else** — **the only living thing in the air, and the only thing in the frame that matters.** **His head comes up.**

**9.5–13.5s — THE REACH AND THE CATCH.** **His right arm extends forward past his own head toward it**, fingers spread — **the slowest, most deliberate movement in the shot**, taking two full seconds while everything around him comes apart. **The camera drifts round to his shoulder and his face comes into view in profile** — **filthy, dusted, calm, exactly as it was at the top of the shot.** **There is nothing on it but focus.**

**His hand closes around the creature.** He **pulls it back in against his chest and folds his body shut around it a second time**, arms locked over it, **his back to everything.**

**13.5–16.2s — the wall arrives.** Still slow, still crystalline, still descending. **Beyond him, growing at the end of the aisle, the plaster wall.** Pages and ash still filling the frame. **He is turning slowly so that his back and shoulders reach it first.** **The last slow frames are almost peaceful.**

## **THE RAMP UP — 16.2–16.5s**

**Everything accelerates at once.** The drifting debris **rips into streaks**, pages tear across the frame, the sound rushes back up, **and the world is running at full speed.**

## **REAL TIME**

**16.5–17.5s — THE WALL, AND THE LIGHT.** **He meets it back-first at full speed and the old plaster gives way completely**, bursting outward in brick fragments, dust and shattered lath, **a ragged opening punched clean through** — **and behind it is daylight.**

**A hard white sun floods back through the opening into the dark room**, instantly, **blowing the exposure out**, **the whole frame going from cold near-black to pure white in a few frames.** **Every particle of dust and every falling page in the aisle lights up at once**, thousands of them suddenly visible in hot shafts. **He is gone into it — a black silhouette for two or three frames, then only the light.**

**17.5–20.0s — the flare, and the end.** **The camera holds on the opening.** **The daylight is blinding** — the dark room reduced to silhouettes of stacks against white. **Dust pours out and hangs in the beam.** Debris and single pages still coming down through it.

**And the sun catches the lens: one long anamorphic flare drawn across the frame**, spilling and streaking, **veiling the picture, the grain crawling through it.** **The flare is the last thing in the shot.**

**Nothing else happens. It ends on the light.**

# **THE FEELING — THIS IS THE WHOLE BRIEF**

**A dark ASMR marble run.** The sphere descends through the wreckage **striking one clean, separate, deliberate note at a time**, and the pleasure of the shot is that **every single contact is distinct.**

**Precision, not chaos.** It is **tuned**: measured, rhythmic, inevitable. **Not a crash, not a tumble, not a scramble, not an avalanche.** Nothing happens twice at once. There is **air around every event** — a small space of near-silence before and after each contact.

**Tempo.** Roughly **one contact per second** at the top, **tightening to two per second** across the middle, then the long rest of the fall, then one heavy final note. **You should be able to count the beats.** If two things happen at the same moment, or the sound becomes a continuous roar, the shot is wrong.

**Restraint.** No spraying debris, no clouds of dust, no showers of books, no collapsing shelves. **Small, exact, physical events**, close and tactile.

**It travels in one smooth continuous movement**: a tight orbit around the machine while it folds, then a steady descent with the sphere all the way to the floor, then down onto the boards with it. **The sphere stays framed and sharp for almost every frame**, occupying a good part of the picture, the shelving and books huge and soft behind it.

**It leans and tilts with the geometry** — following a diagonal down a paddle board, levelling along a flat run, tipping into the drop — always a smooth continuous descent, never a series of jerks. **Focus rides the sphere throughout**, softening only for a beat when something passes close to the lens. # **PHYSICS**

**A dense fifteen-centimetre metal ball.** **It never bounces up.** Its upward velocity after any impact is zero — it never rises, never hops, never rebounds, never arcs, never leaves a surface it has landed on. **The only airborne moment is the single drop near the end, and it is going downward.**

**It stays in contact with the set almost the whole way**, running, sliding and rolling **through** the structure rather than falling down it. # THE SEVENTEEN SECONDS

**0.0s — the first frame is <<<image_2>>>, exactly.** BRD-1 in its bird form per <<<image_1>>>, on the top board of the bookcase. **It is held for no time at all — by 0.3s it has already begun.**

**0.3–3.5s — THE FOLD, and the camera orbits it.** From the first movement the camera **arcs continuously around the machine**, roughly halfway around across these three seconds, **staying tight**: plates, panel lines, markings and dust in the seams all legible, the shelving behind destroyed into blur, **the background swinging heavily behind it and the angle changing every frame.**

The fold is **mechanical, intricate and believable** — panels on real hinges, plates on real rails, parts folding into spaces that were visibly there. **Every piece of the sphere is a piece of the bird, moved.** Watchmaking, not a robot movie. No flourish, no pose, no reveal.

→ **0.3–0.7s:** every seam cracks open a millimetre at once; the shell becomes a jigsaw of hundreds of standing plates; dust lifts off it. → **0.7–1.5s:** the beak splits and the halves rotate back along the skull; the skull plates peel and hinge down; the head withdraws into the chest. **The eye lenses turn inward and are covered last — from that frame there is no face.** → **1.5–2.4s:** shoulder plates rotate forward over the cavity; wings fold three times, lie flat and slide inside; the tail collapses in; the torso shortens and rounds, spars and cabling glimpsed for a fraction of a second before plates seal over them. → **2.4–3.0s:** the claws release the lip and the legs **fold up and inward and are swallowed**, leaving no stub and no socket. → **3.0–3.5s:** the raised plates **drop flush in a running wave**, each with a small hard click, until the shell is **one unbroken sphere — exactly <<<image_3>>>.** The orbit ends on its flank.

**3.5–4.3s — the first roll.** Round and legless, it **rolls forward along the top board**, slow and heavy, its weight in the wood, and runs off the front edge onto the first angled board.

**4.3–7.0s — the paddles. Four beats, one per board, alternating.** It lands on the first angled paddle board, **runs its diagonal**, drops off the low end onto the next, alternating direction each time — **left, right, left, right** — four boards, four clean landings, **evenly spaced, roughly 0.68s apart.** Each landing a single dull knock on wood; the run between a low grinding roll. **The camera slides down with it in one continuous diagonal descent.**

**7.0–8.0s — the lane and the bracket.** Off the last paddle onto the **flat lane of books laid face down**, running its length — **a smooth quiet passage, no impact, just a soft rolling hush on board covers** — and it strikes the **black iron bracket** at the end. **One hard bright ring**, and the ring turns it.

**8.0–8.6s — the slot.** It drops into the **vertical slot between two leaning stacks and through the brass pipe wedged inside it** — **gone from view for half a second**, the sound going hollow and boxed-in — and comes out lower down.

**8.6–10.2s — the rail. The showpiece.** It lands on the **brass book-rail curving out of the shelving** and **runs the whole arc**, striking **the comb of thin iron rods one after another** — **a fast, even run of small bright rings**, a dozen of them in a second and a half, perfectly spaced. **The most musical moment in the shot; the camera holds close on it.**

**10.2–11.1s — the ladder rung, and the first break.** Off the rail onto the **flat top edge of a ladder rung**, running its length — and **through a thin dry lath spanning the gap at the end**, which **snaps clean in the middle**, the halves dropping away, pale splintered wood bright against the char. **One sharp dry crack.**

**11.1–12.0s — the drawer, and the second break.** It drops into the **open drawer channel** and runs it end to end, low sides guiding it — **a dry wooden rattle** — **snapping a second lath** across the drawer's open front as it goes. **One crack.**

**12.0–12.9s — the sagging shelf.** It lands on the **cracked shelf that sags to one side**, follows the slope, and the **split lip at the end turns it out toward the front**, onto the last short board. **One knock, one long roll.**

**12.9–13.4s — the last lath, and the edge.** It runs the last board, **snaps the frail lath on the very lip** — **one final crack** — and **comes off the edge.**

**13.4–14.0s — THE FALL.** **Nothing under it.** A clean vertical drop through open air, accelerating. **And the sound stops** — no contact, no rolling, nothing: **a full half-second of near-silence, the longest gap in the piece.** The camera drops with it, still smooth.

**14.0–14.3s — the floor.** **One enormous flat concussive impact** on the scorched boards — the biggest note in the shot, the room ringing after it. **It does not rise.** The impact throws it flat forward into a roll.

**14.3–15.1s — to the boots.** It rolls forward across the floorboards through drifted paper, **slowing**, and **the boots of <<<image_4>>> come into frame ahead of it** — planted, side by side, unmoving. The camera is down on the floor with it now, lens a few centimetres above the boards.

**15.1–15.6s — contact.** It comes to rest **directly in front of him, square on, a hand's width from the toes of both boots, centred between them**, its last movement a gentle nudge against one toe cap — **a soft tap, almost nothing, the quietest sound in the piece.** It stops dead, **the readout panel turned toward him.** Silence.

**15.6–17.0s — the counter.** The camera is close on the sphere where it sits, **the readout panel and both boots in the same frame** — panel sharp, boots dark and soft behind it. The panel is blank. Then, in one frame, it wakes:

→ **15.6s: `10`** → **16.6s: `9`**

# AUDIO — THE RUN IS THE SCORE

**No music of any kind, at any volume** — no drone, no swell, no riser, no sting, no bass hit, no synth, no strings, no instruments, no score. **Every sound is something in the room actually making it.**

**Close and tactile — ASMR-close.** Each contact is **distinct, separate and clean**, with a small silence around it. **Never a continuous roar, never mush, never two events at once.** A stone hall full of paper: dry flat slap-back, low dead air, quiet enough that the small sounds carry.

**The vocabulary, one per event:** at the unlock, **one sharp dry crack** of hundreds of seals breaking; through the fold, a **dense fast cascade of tiny dry mechanical sounds** — servos, plates on rails, hinges, detents — all small-object sounds; the lock a **running wave of hard clicks** ending on one seating clack; then the **low heavy rumble** of the roll on old wood, the board resonating under the weight; the **dull knock** of each paddle landing; the **soft hush** of running on book covers; the **hard bright ring** of the iron bracket; the **hollow boxed tone** inside the brass pipe; the **fast even run of small bright rings** along the rod comb; the **dry rattle** of the drawer; the **three sharp dry cracks** of the laths; the **half-second of silence** in the fall; the **enormous flat thud** on the floor; the **low gritty roll**; the **soft tap** at the boot; then **two small dry ticks**, a second apart.

**The rhythm emerges from the impacts themselves** — never created by music, an instrument, pitching or tuning the sounds, or a beat underneath. **If an instrument or a score is audible, the piece is wrong.**
